### Small Fixes: an Empty Board's Export, Column Order, a Team's Last Owner, Add Sent Once, Manage Categories' × and Role Pickers That Wait for Change

**Cards 2371, 2372, 2373, 2374, 2375 and 2376.** No migration, no setting, no route added. Two web-application routes answer differently (cards 2371 and 2373), and three `/api/v1` answers give tied columns in a set order (card 2372, OpenAPI change item 101, still version 1.2.0). The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2371-2376-small-fixes.md`.

- **2371.** The board CSV export (`/api/boards/<id>/export/csv`, which no page links to) of a board with no columns put the board's name in the file-name header as it was: a name with an emoji or another character outside Latin-1 was a `500`, and a double quote cut the name short. Now its file is named as any board's is, `<name>-<date>.csv` with every character but letters, digits, `-` and `_` made `_`.
- **2372.** A board's columns were read by position alone, so two at one position (a column made through v1 with a chosen `position`, or a reorder that sent one twice) came in no set order. Every reader now orders them by position, then the older first: the board page, All Tasks, All To Do, the inbox, the internal picker, the CFD, both CSV exports, the daily snapshots, the reports' To Do fallback, a board's columns in the graph view (`/api/graph?boardId=`, which gave them in the order they were made), and `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}`, `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns` and `POST /api/v1/boards`.
- **2373.** A team's owner, or an administrator, could make the team's last owner a member or remove them, leaving a team only an administrator could run. Both are now refused for everyone: "A team needs at least one owner. Make someone else an owner first, or delete the team." (`409`, nothing changed).
- **2374.** **Add** under a team (the Teams page and **Admin → Team Management**) sent the add again on a second click while the first was out: two requests and two "Member added". Now a second press while it is out sends nothing, and Add keeps the keyboard's focus. An Add for someone already in the team (added meanwhile elsewhere) sets their role, and now says "*name* was already in the team; role set to *Role*" rather than "Member added".
- **2375.** Manage Categories' **×** closed the window while a change was on its way, so the server's answer was said to nobody (Escape already waited). Now × waits as Escape does.
- **2376.** The member role pickers (Teams page, admin Team Management) and the admin **User Management** role picker saved as soon as a value was chosen. On Windows, Up and Down on a closed picker choose at once, so a keyboard user arrowing through it saved each role passed (on User Management, Admin included). Now choosing saves nothing: each row has a **Change** button beside the picker, dimmed and doing nothing until a role other than the stored one is chosen, and pressing it saves. While it is on its way a second press sends nothing and a screen reader is told "Saving *name*'s role…". A role chosen and not saved is forgotten once the member or account is removed, or the page reads them back gone or already holding it. On User Management the picker and Change are drawn for the superadmin alone, as only the superadmin has a second role to give.

A team left with no owner from before (or by deleting its only owner's account, which this does not stop) is still run by administrators. See [Admin Operations Guide](admin-guide.md#team-owners-and-members).

### The Plan Re-Read Only After a Change, Unused CSS Reported, a Team's Only Owner Kept on Account Delete, and a Missing Role Kept

**Cards 2324, 2357, 2377 and 2378.** No migration, no setting, no route added. Two web-application routes answer differently (cards 2377 and 2378); no `/api/v1` operation changes, and the OpenAPI document is as it was (version 1.2.0). The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2324-2357-2377-2378.md`.

- **2324.** Closing a card window on a plan page read the whole plan again every time, for a window only looked at too. Now it reads it again only when the window changed something the plan draws: a save that changed the card, a subtask ticked, added, edited or deleted, a dependency added or removed, or the card's milestone. An assignee, the cover, labels, a comment or a file changed in the window do not re-read it (the plan draws none of them).
- **2357.** The build's check for style rules that match nothing was switched off for the whole app; it is on again, and the one dead rule it found (on the request form page) is gone. Nothing on any page looks different.
- **2377.** Deleting an account that was the only owner of a team left that team with no owner, run by administrators alone. Now it is refused, nothing changed: "This account is the only owner of: *the teams*. Make someone else an owner or delete those teams first." ("… that team first" for one).
- **2378.** `POST /api/teams/{id}/members/{userId}` with no `role` set someone already in the team to Member, quietly demoting an owner (the pages always send a role, so only a script could). Now a role left out keeps theirs; someone new is still added as Member.

**Owner to know.** **An account that alone owns a team cannot be deleted** until another member is made an owner of each such team (**Admin → Team Management**, their row's picker, **Change**) or the team is deleted; the toast after **Confirm** names the teams. See [Admin Operations Guide](admin-guide.md#disabling-enabling-and-deleting-an-account). **On a plan page**, closing a card window you only looked at no longer reloads the plan.

### Goal Membership Webhooks, the Plan Re-Read After a Refused, Unanswered or Late Window Write, and the Sole Team Owner Named Before an Account Delete

**Cards 2343, 2379 and 2380.** No migration, no setting, no route added. One `/api/v1` change: two new webhook event types, OpenAPI change item 102 under version 1.2.0 (the version is unchanged). Cards 2379 and 2380 change page code only. The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2343-2379-2380.md`.

- **2343.** A card put in a goal or taken out recorded it on the card's board but told no webhook. It now sends `milestone.card_added` or `milestone.card_removed` to the webhooks of the card's board, by every way of doing it: the card window's **Milestone** picker, the plan page, and the API's single, bulk and card-update routes (one delivery per card for the bulk ones). The body is every event's: `data.cardId`, `data.action`, `data.source`, `data.user` and `data.detail` (`Added "<card>" to milestone "<goal>"`). A card moved from one goal to another is one `milestone.card_added` naming the goal it left. A change to a goal itself still sends nothing.
- **2379.** On a plan page, a card-window change that was refused because someone else had already made it (a dependency already removed), that got no answer, or that was answered after the window was closed, did not read the plan again, so the plan could show a link or a tick that was no longer true. Each now reads it again: the first two as the window closes, the last as soon as the answer comes.
- **2380.** Deleting an account that alone owns a team is refused (card 2377), but the confirmation did not say so. It now names those teams before **Confirm** is pressed.

**Owner to know.** **Every webhook whose events list is empty (sent every event) starts receiving `milestone.card_added` and `milestone.card_removed` from this deploy**, one delivery per card for a bulk change of up to 500 cards. A receiver that cannot take them should be given the list of events it wants (`PUT /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` with `events`) before or straight after the deploy. **In Admin → User Management**, the delete confirmation of an account that is the only owner of a team now says so in its second sentence; **Confirm** still sends the delete, and the server still refuses it unless someone else has been made an owner since the page was loaded.

### One Reader for Both Audit Logs, a Webhook for Every Card That Leaves a Goal, and the Card Window's Dependency Read When the Network Drops

**Cards 2294, 2381 and 2382.** No migration, no setting, no route added. One `/api/v1` change: `milestone.card_removed` is sent in more cases, OpenAPI change item 103 under version 1.2.0 (the version is unchanged); `GET /api/v1/audit-log` answers exactly as before. The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2294-2381-2382.md`.

- **2294.** The Audit page's log (`GET /api/audit`) and the API's (`GET /api/v1/audit-log`) were two copies of one query that had drifted apart. Both now read the log through one function. The page's route reads a page's board names in one query, where it asked once per board; takes `cardId`; refuses a bad id in the API's words (`Invalid board ID`, where it said `Invalid boardId`); and answers `rawAction`, `source`, `total` and `hasMore` as the API does. The page shows what it showed.
- **2381.** A card that left a goal because of something else (moved to another board, its goal deleted, or deleted itself, alone, with its column, by an administrator's **Clear Cards** or by **Purge All**) recorded nothing for the goal and told no webhook. Each now writes `milestone_card_removed` on the card's board, with why in brackets, and sends `milestone.card_removed`. A card deleted together with its own board still sends nothing: the board's webhooks go with it.
- **2382.** When the card window could not read a card's dependencies (no network, a proxy's page, a refusal), it said nothing and the browser logged an error. It now says so above the lists and keeps the links it was showing.

**Owner to know.** **Every webhook whose events list is empty (sent every event) starts receiving `milestone.card_removed` for these cases from this deploy**: one delivery per card, so an administrator's **Clear Cards** on a board of 400 cards in goals sends 400, and **Purge All** one per purged card that was in a goal. A receiver that cannot take them should be given the list of events it wants (`PUT /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` with `events`). A script that reads `/api/audit` with a bad id reads `Invalid board ID` (or `Invalid user ID`) where it read `Invalid boardId` (or `Invalid userId`).

### The Share Window Says Which Webhooks a Removal Stops, the Audit Page's Load More, and the Card Window's Dependency Search

**Cards 2329, 2383 and 2384.** No migration, no setting, no route added, and no `/api/v1` change (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). One internal answer gains keys: `GET /api/boards/{id}/share` gives the board's owner and an administrator `stopsWebhooks` on each person and team and `heldWebhooks` on the answer. The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2329-2383-2384.md`.

- **2329.** A webhook is sent only while the account that set it up can open the board (card 2325), but nothing on screen said when one stopped. The board's **Share Board** window now asks before removing a person or a team whose removal would stop webhooks, saying how many (**Remove** or **Cancel**), and says above its list how many of the board's webhooks send nothing now, whatever stopped them, ones with no recorded setter included. Only the board's owner and administrators see either.
- **2383.** The Audit page offered **Load more** after a page of exactly 100 entries even when nothing followed. It now offers it only while the answer says more follows.
- **2384.** The card window's dependency search said nothing when it failed (no network, a proxy's page, a refusal) and showed "No cards match"; it now says so under the box. Only the latest search's answer is shown, and the window's reads of a card's links keep only the newest answer, so an older one arriving late no longer puts back links that were changed.

**Owner to know.** In the Share window, ✕ on someone who set up a webhook that would stop now opens a **Remove Access** confirmation first; ✕ on anyone else removes them at once, as before. A board with held webhooks shows a line about them in the Share window from this deploy, the first time its owner opens it.

### Making a Board Private Warns Before It Stops Webhooks, the Card Window's Search Timer, and the Audit Log's Cursor

**Cards 2385, 2386 and 2387.** No migration, no setting, no index and no route added. One `/api/v1` change, additive: `GET /api/v1/audit-log` takes an optional `before` (OpenAPI change item 104; `info.version` stays 1.2.0). One internal answer gains a key: `GET /api/boards/{id}/share` gives the board's owner and an administrator `privateStopsWebhooks`. The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2385-2386-2387.md`.

- **2385.** Making a public board private holds every webhook whose setter could open it only because it was public, and the Share window said nothing. The switch now asks first when it would stop any, saying how many (**Make Private** or **Cancel**), and the window reads its list again after the switch, so the line about held webhooks follows at once. The window also reads its list once on opening, where it read it twice.
- **2386.** A dependency search typed in the card window within a quarter of a second of closing it was still sent. It is no longer sent once the window closes or its card changes.
- **2387.** The Audit page's **Load more** asked for the next page by counting the rows shown, so an entry written meanwhile made the next page begin with a row already shown. It now asks for the entries older than the last row shown. Integrations can page `GET /api/v1/audit-log` the same way with `before`; `offset` works as it did.

**Owner to know.** In the Share window, the switch from public to private now opens a **Make Private** confirmation when it would stop a webhook; otherwise it switches at once, as before.

### A New Card Is Made With Its Subtasks, Labels, Assignees and Sub-Boards in One Request, and the Dependency Picker's Close

**Cards 2296 and 2388.** No migration, no setting, no route added, and no `/api/v1` change (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). One internal route takes more: `POST /api/cards` takes `subtasks`, `labelIds`, `assigneeIds` and `subBoards`, written with the card or not at all. The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2296-2388.md`.

- **2296.** The board's New Task window made the card, then sent each subtask, each label of its template, each person chosen and each sub-board in a request of its own, so a refusal or a lost answer part way left half a card. It now sends one request, and the server makes the card with all of it or makes nothing; the entries, live updates, webhooks and mail are the same as before. A template label deleted while the window is open is left out rather than refusing the card. With no answer the board is read again, so a card that was made after all shows behind the window, and the toast ends "Check the board before creating it again."
- **2388.** A dependency search typed in the card window's picker within a quarter of a second of closing the picker (Escape, ✕, or opening the other list's picker) was still sent. It no longer is.

**Owner to know.** A New Task whose subtask, label, person or sub-board is refused (a sub-board too deep, say, or someone taken off the board meanwhile) is no longer made without that part: nothing is made, the window stays open with everything typed, and the toast names the part as the window shows it, as `Sub-board "Phase two" could not be made: Sub-boards can be nested at most 20 levels deep, …` or `"bob" could not be assigned: User does not have access to this board`.

### The Admin Page and Dashboard Loads Read a Fixed Number of Queries, and Duplicate Copies a Card With Its Subtasks in One Request

**Cards 2297, 2298 and 2389.** No migration, no setting, no index, no route added, and no API change (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2297-2298-2389.md`.

- **2297.** The admin page's load read three queries for every board and one for every team, and every change made on the page reads it again. It now reads seven queries whatever the installation holds. What the page shows is the same.
- **2298.** The dashboard's load read two queries for every top-level board, two for every level of sub-boards, two for every assignee row of the Team Leaderboard, and the whole subtasks, requests, assignees and users tables. It now reads the same number of queries however many boards, levels and assignees there are, and reads only the boards the person can open. What it shows is the same. It is still read again a quarter of a second after a burst of changes on any board.
- **2389.** Duplicate made the copy and then sent its subtasks one at a time, so a subtask refused part way left a copy with some of them. The copy's subtasks now go in the copy's one request, and the copy is made with all of them or not at all.

**Owner to know.** A Duplicate whose subtask is refused, or of a card with more than 100 subtasks, now makes no copy at all; the toast says why (`"<card>" was not duplicated: subtask "<title>" could not be copied: …`, or `"<card>" was not duplicated: subtasks must have at most 100 entries`; any other refusal is the server's words after the same `"<card>" was not duplicated: `). It made a copy with part of its subtasks, or with all of them.

### The Dashboard's Team Leaderboard Leaves Out Archived Cards

**Card 2391.** No migration, no setting, no index, no route added, and no API change (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). The plan is `docs/planning/card-2391.md`.

### Administrators Can Use the Email and Backup Settings

**Card 2395.** No migration, no setting, no index, no route added, and nothing in `/api/v1` changes (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). The plan is `docs/planning/card-2395.md`.

- **2395.** The mail settings (📧 Email / SMTP, with Send Test), the App URL (🌐 Application Settings, saved by the same route) and the scheduled backups (☁️ Scheduled Backups: the schedule, the destinations, 🧪 Test, ▶ Run Now and Google Drive's 🔗 Connect) were the superadmin's alone. Every administrator can now see and use them, on the admin page and by their routes. Export Backup, Import Backup and Reset Everything stay the superadmin's, and the 🔒 section an administrator sees names only those three. An administrator made a user is refused at once, a save or a send already on its way included.

**Owner to know.** This was the superadmin's because each of these settings is the user list by another way, and it still is:

- **An administrator who sets a backup destination can receive a full copy of the database**: every account's password hash and email address, every board, card and comment. They can add a destination of their own and press Run Now.
- **An administrator who sets the mail server sees every mail DumpFire sends**, invite links and password-reset links included, the superadmin's among them; whoever reads such a link can set that account's password. The App URL decides where every link in a mail points.
- So any administrator can make themselves any account, the superadmin included.
- **The stored secrets stay where they were saved.** The mail password and each destination's secrets are masked for everybody, and cannot be pointed at another server without being typed again, with two exceptions: an administrator may confirm the host key of an SFTP destination that has a stored password but no confirmed key yet, and the password then goes to whichever server shows that key; and **🔗 Connect** on a Google Drive destination already set up with a client ID and secret ties it to the Google account of whoever connects, using the stored ID and secret (a `WARN` line under `BACKUP` where it replaces a connection the destination had).
- **An administrator can leave nothing to restore from.** Lowering **Keep Last** (its least is 1) and pressing **▶ Run Now** deletes every older copy at every destination; removing the destinations or switching the schedule off stops the copies. So damage an administrator does can be left with no backup to restore from. Each such change is a `WARN` line under `BACKUP` with the chip of who made it: logged, not prevented.
- **An administrator can probe the inside of the network.** The SMTP host, an SFTP host and an S3 endpoint may be any address, inside the network included (loopback, the Docker host, internal ranges, `169.254.169.254`), and what **🧪 Send Test** and **🧪 Test** answer tells whether a port answered: a simple internal port scan. Webhooks refuse addresses inside the network (card 2161); these settings do not, since real setups use a NAS or a mail relay on the LAN.
- **The settings outlive whoever saved them.** A destination or mail server an administrator set stays in force when that administrator is demoted or deleted. After demoting an administrator, look at Scheduled Backups and Email / SMTP. Each backup settings change is a line under `BACKUP` on the Audit page with the chip of who made it; a mail settings change writes no line, except the "Allow mail without a checked, encrypted connection" box.

### Settings Go With Their Setter; Fewer Backups Are the Superadmin's

**Cards 2397 and 2398.** **One migration**, `0059_add_setting_setters.sql`: a new table, `setting_setters`, with its index (its key is the setting and a digest of where it sends, its `place`). No setting is added, and nothing in `/api/v1` changes (the OpenAPI document is unchanged; `PUT` and `DELETE /api/users/:id` answer `settingsRemoved` where they removed something). One method is added, an administrator's `GET /api/users/:id`, which the admin page reads just before it asks to make an account a user or delete it. The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2397-2398.md`.

- **2398.** Any administrator could lower **Keep Last** and press **▶ Run Now**, deleting every older copy at every destination, or remove the destinations, or switch the schedule off. Now each of the three is the superadmin's: an administrator's save that does one is refused, `Lowering Keep Last, removing a destination or switching the schedule off needs the superadmin. This save would …`, and nothing is saved. A destination renamed is the old one removed. On ☁️ Scheduled Backups an administrator sees one line saying so under the schedule, 🗑️ dimmed (pressed, it says the rule), **Disabled (superadmin only)** in the schedule (chosen, it puts the schedule back), and Keep Last putting a lower number back. Raising Keep Last, changing between schedules that run, adding and editing destinations, Test, Connect and Run Now stay every administrator's. The superadmin's panel is as before.
- **2397.** DumpFire now records who last changed where mail goes (the mail host, port, user name or the box that allows mail without a checked, encrypted connection), who last set the App URL to an address, and who last added each backup destination, pointed it at another place or account, or connected its Google Drive. A sender's name or address, a password or secret typed again for the same place, an App URL cleared or an SFTP host key confirmed makes nobody the setter. When the setter is made a user, or deleted, what it set is removed in the same step, with a `WARN` line under `SMTP` or `BACKUP`; the admin page names what would go before the change is confirmed (a role change to User asks first where anything would), says what went in a ⚠️ message that stays, and reads again the panels that showed it.

**The migration.** 0059 creates one table and changes no row. Every setting already saved has nobody recorded as its setter, and **stays in force whoever is demoted** until somebody next changes it. A backup taken before the deploy restores with every setting unattributed in the same way; one taken after brings its setter rows with the accounts they name. Nothing is declared to the rehearsal: it is no one-off.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Old["Older image:<br/>settings record nobody"] --> Deploy["First start:<br/>0059 applied, table empty"]
    Deploy --> Legacy["Every saved setting:<br/>unattributed, in force"]
    Deploy --> Next["Next change of a setting:<br/>its saver recorded"]
    Next --> Demote["Saver made a user or deleted:<br/>that setting removed, WARN line"]
    Deploy -.->|"going back"| Back["Older image: ERROR line for 0059,<br/>table left alone, nothing removed"]
```

**Owner to know.**

- **Demoting or deleting the administrator who pointed the mail where it is stops all mail**: invites (their links are shown in the dialog instead), password-reset invites, notifications, request mail, reports and the backup failure mail, until an administrator sets the mail up again under 📧 Email / SMTP. The App URL they saved goes too, and links then use `APP_URL`, or else `ORIGIN`, the server's own address.
- **Their destinations go with their stored secrets**, and backups to them stop. The copies already at a destination are not touched.
- **The last to move a setting is its setter.** Only a change of where mail or backups go moves it: an administrator who corrects the sender's name, or types your password or secret again, does not take your settings over, and their demotion leaves them. A superadmin who moves the mail (another port, say) takes it over, and demoting whoever first set it then removes nothing. To take over the settings saved before this deploy, change one that moves them and change it back.
- **A backup already running finishes.** A run reads the destinations as it starts, so one under way at the demotion or delete still uploads to a destination removed with it; the next run does not.
- **The superadmin is under the same rule**, once lowered to user on the admin page (from the host they are made `admin`, which keeps them an administrator).
- **The host's command line runs none of this.** A role written to `user`, or an account deleted, with `docker exec … node -e` leaves their settings in force.
- **Run Now can still push the older copies out.** Each press adds a copy and Keep Last keeps the newest, so an administrator who presses it Keep Last times still leaves only new copies; a schedule made more frequent does the same over time. Each Run Now is in the backup history.
- This replaces card 2395's "The settings outlive whoever saved them" and "An administrator can leave nothing to restore from" (above, left as written for that release).

#### Before the deploy

On production, on the older image, as **S**, the superadmin, signed in. Nothing here writes anything. Note:

- In **Admin**, under ☁️ Scheduled Backups, the schedule, the number in **Keep Last**, and each destination's name; under 📧 Email / SMTP, the SMTP Host and From Email; under 🌐 Application Settings, the Application URL.
- The times the schedule runs, so that checks 453 to 456 can be done between two runs (the scratch destinations of 453 and 456 are removed again within minutes, and a run between would try them).

**Check 0y: the rehearsal.** `npm run rehearse -- <export.db>` on an Admin Export copy, with the new code, as check 0c runs it (see [Testing](testing.md#rehearsing-the-runner-against-a-copy-of-a-real-database)). Expect `0059_add_setting_setters.sql` among the files applied, `PASSED` and no schema difference; nothing under `Worth knowing` for it, since it is no one-off. It is a fault if it prints `FAILED`, or a difference naming `setting_setters`.

#### What changes at the first start

### Run Now Copies Counted Apart From Scheduled Ones; a Setter Made a User From the Host Loses Their Settings at the Next Start

**Cards 2405, 2406 and 2409.** No migration, no setting, no index, no route added, and nothing in `/api/v1` changes (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2405-2406-2409.md`.

- **2405.** Each **▶ Run Now** added a copy and Keep Last kept the newest, so an administrator who pressed it Keep Last times pushed every older copy out, the way round card 2398's rule. Now a Run Now names its copy `dumpfire-backup-<UTC date and time>-manual.db`, and Keep Last counts those apart from the scheduled copies: a Run Now removes only the oldest `…-manual.db` copies beyond Keep Last, a scheduled run only the oldest scheduled ones, so a destination holds at most twice Keep Last. Its `Backup succeeded` line ends `. Made by Run Now: Keep Last counts Run Now copies apart from scheduled ones, so only an older Run Now copy can be removed`, and the panel says the same under Keep Last and in the Run Now toast.
- **2406.** A role written to `user`, or an account deleted with foreign keys off, from the host ran no application code, so that person's mail settings, App URL and destinations stayed in force. Now every start, after the migrations and before the schedulers, removes them by card 2397's rule, with the same `WARN` lines under `SMTP` and `BACKUP`, ending `(found at start-up: the role was changed outside the admin page)` or `(found at start-up: it was deleted outside the admin page)`, filed under nobody. A working copy (Import Backup with the outside switched off) now also clears the setter rows of the mail settings and destinations it removes.
- **2409.** Three tests could fail when a run crossed midnight; they no longer read the date twice. Nothing changes in the application.

**Owner to know.**

- **A destination can hold up to twice Keep Last copies**: Keep Last scheduled copies and Keep Last Run Now copies. A Run Now copy made before this deploy has no `-manual` and is counted with the scheduled ones, as before.
- **A schedule made more frequent** still keeps Keep Last copies over a shorter time: changing between schedules that run stays every administrator's (card 2398's ruling).
- **A role lowered to `user` from the host takes effect for the settings at the next start**: restart the container after such a change. An account deleted from the host with the documented `node -e` (better-sqlite3 keeps foreign keys on) takes its setter rows with it, and its settings stay in force, unattributed: delete accounts on the admin page.

**Cards 2410, 2411 and 2412.** No migration, no setting, no index, no route added, and nothing in `/api/v1` changes (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2410-2411-2412.md`.

The `WARN` lines under `SMTP` and `BACKUP` end `(found after a restore)`, and the import's result and its `INFO` line add `Removed after the restore, because whoever set them is not an administrator in the restored data, or has no account in it: …`, naming what went (mail settings gone means no invites or password resets until mail is set again); a mail password or destination removed is not listed as kept or to enter again. ### Backup History Kept by Runs; the Failure Mail Says Run Now; a Daily or Weekly Backup Made Once in Its Minute

**Cards 2413 and 2414.** No migration, no setting, no index, no route added, and nothing in `/api/v1` changes (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). The plan is `docs/planning/cards-2413-2414.md`.

- **2413.** `backup_log` keeps every row of the newest 30 runs (a run is the rows of one copy's name, one a destination), and the last successful scheduled run's row whatever came after it; it kept the newest 10 rows, under three runs with four destinations. Backup History (`GET /api/admin/backup`) shows every row of the newest 30 runs. After a restart an interval schedule always finds the last scheduled run, however many **▶ Run Now** presses or failures came after it. A Run Now's failure mail is headed **Run Now Backup Failed**, "A backup made by ▶ Run Now to …"; a scheduled run's still says **Scheduled Backup Failed**.
- **2414.** In a daily or weekly backup's minute the scheduler also asks `backup_log` whether a scheduled run has already finished in that minute, and makes none if so, with one `[WARN] [BACKUP] Scheduled daily backup at 02:00 not made: …` line: the clock put back across a restart into that minute, or a second instance checking in it after the first one's run has finished, no longer makes a second copy. A second instance checking while the first is still uploading does: that run has no row yet. A plain restart never could repeat it (its first check is a minute after the start). Only a run recorded within the hour from the minute's start counts, so one stamped ahead by a clock that ran fast and was put back does not stop the next days' backups; while it is the newest, each daily or weekly check writes `[WARN] [BACKUP] The last scheduled backup is recorded at …, later than the server's clock …`.

**Owner to know.**

- **Backup History grows** over the next runs to every row of the last 30 runs (with four destinations, 120 rows); the panel still shows five and **▼ Show all N entries**. Nothing is removed by the deploy itself: the first run after it keeps all that is there, which is under 30 runs.
- **Nothing to do for 2414.**

```mermaid
flowchart LR

    Get["GET /api/admin/backup"] --> Hist["the newest 30 runs' rows"]
    Fail["a destination fails"] --> Mail["Run Now Backup Failed<br/>or Scheduled Backup Failed"]
    Tick["daily/weekly minute"] --> Ask{"a scheduled run stamped<br/>in this minute?"}
    Ask -->|"yes"| None["nothing"]
    Ask -->|"no"| Back["back up"]
```

### A Missed Daily or Weekly Backup Made Up Once; a Failed Backup Tried Again; One Failure Mail a Run; Copies Named to the Millisecond

**Card 2415.** No migration, no setting, no index, no route added, and nothing in `/api/v1` changes (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). The plan is `docs/planning/card-2415.md`.

- **A daily or weekly schedule is decided by its latest time.** At each check the scheduler finds the latest time the schedule was due (today's 02:00, or yesterday's before 02:00; the weekday's for weekly) and backs up where no successful scheduled backup is recorded since it. A server down or busy through the time makes that backup once at the first check after (a minute after the start), with `[WARN] [BACKUP] Scheduled daily backup at 02:00 was not made at its time, <ISO> (the server was down, or busy past the check): made now.`; it made none until the next day. A server started with such a schedule and no scheduled backup since its latest time makes one then. A schedule, time or day changed while the server runs waits for its next time. Where the server's zone has daylight saving (not the image's UTC), a time in the hour skipped runs an hour on, and one in the hour that comes twice runs once.
- **A scheduled run that failed at every destination is tried again 15 minutes later, up to three times**, for every schedule (it waited an interval, up to a week). The tries come back after a run that succeeds somewhere. **A restart** makes the backup due once a minute after the start; where that backup had already failed before the restart, that is its one try until a run succeeds (no tries again), so a server restarted again and again sends one failure mail and makes one SFTP login a start. A run where every destination failed before anything was sent (credentials not entered, a host key not confirmed) is not tried again, and a failure of a run older than one that has since succeeded arms none.
- **One failure mail a run**, naming every destination that failed with its error; it sent one for each.
- **Copy names to the millisecond**: `dumpfire-backup-YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SS-mmm.db` (`…-mmm-manual.db` for a Run Now), so two Run Now presses in one second no longer share a name.
- **An hourly, 6-hourly or 12-hourly schedule after a start** leaves out a scheduled row recorded later than the server's clock, and says so with `[WARN] [BACKUP] The last scheduled backup is recorded at …, later than the server's clock …`; such a row held every run off until the real time passed it and one interval more.

**Owner to know.**

- **The first start may make a backup a minute in** (check 466): only where a daily or weekly schedule's latest time has passed with no successful scheduled backup since, a failed one included.
- **An outage of every destination can send four failure mails in 45 minutes**, then one a scheduled run as before.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Start["start"] --> T{"daily/weekly: a scheduled success<br/>since the latest time?"}
    T -->|"no"| Up["made up once, a minute in<br/>(WARN: not made at its time)"]
    T -->|"yes"| Wait["next time"]
    Fail["a run fails everywhere"] --> R["tried again at +15 min, ≤ 3"]
    Mail["destinations failing"] --> One["one mail for the run"]
```

#### Before the deploy

Where `ahead` is above 0, one `later than the server's clock` `WARN` at the first check (hourly, 6-hourly, 12-hourly) or the first daily or weekly check.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 466 | 2415 | Daily or weekly schedules only (skip otherwise). From the numbers noted before the deploy, work out the schedule's latest time before the start, in UTC (the container's zone, where `TZ` is not set: see 0058's check), and watch the Live Console for the first minute after the start | Where `last_scheduled_before_now_utc` is before that latest time (or empty): one `Scheduled <daily\|weekly> backup at HH:MM was not made at its time, …: made now.` and one `Scheduled backup triggered` a minute after the start, then nothing more until the next time. Where it is at or after it: no backup at the start | A backup at the start though `last_scheduled_before_now_utc` is at or after the latest time; or none though it is before; or a second one within the hour, unless the first one failed (a try again at +15 min; none where that backup had already failed before the deploy, or failed before anything was sent) |

| 468 | 2415 | Where `ahead` noted before the deploy is above 0 only (skip otherwise) | One `The last scheduled backup is recorded at …, later than the server's clock …` `WARN` at the first scheduler check that reads `backup_log` after the start; an hourly, 6-hourly or 12-hourly schedule runs one interval after the newest scheduled backup recorded before now (`last_scheduled_utc` is the row ahead here), not one interval after the row ahead | No such line; or no interval run until the row ahead has passed |

The command, read-only, prints the schedule, the last successful scheduled backup in UTC (not a Run Now's), the newest of them recorded at or before now, the scheduled rows recorded later than now, and the server's UTC time:

```bash
docker exec <container> node -e "const db = require('better-sqlite3')(process.env.DB_PATH || 'dumpfire.db', { readonly: true, fileMustExist: true }); console.table(db.prepare(process.argv[1]).all()); db.close();" "SELECT (SELECT value ->> 'schedule' FROM settings WHERE key = 'backup_config') AS schedule, (SELECT value ->> 'scheduleTime' FROM settings WHERE key = 'backup_config') AS schedule_time, (SELECT value ->> 'scheduleDay' FROM settings WHERE key = 'backup_config') AS schedule_day, MAX(created_at) AS last_scheduled_utc, MAX(CASE WHEN created_at <= datetime('now') THEN created_at END) AS last_scheduled_before_now_utc, COALESCE(SUM(created_at > datetime('now')), 0) AS ahead, datetime('now') AS now_utc FROM backup_log WHERE status = 'success' AND filename NOT GLOB '*-manual.db'"
```

A destination failing (the tries again and the one mail), two Run Now presses in one second, and a clock change in a zone with daylight saving are not arranged on production: each would need a failing destination and a mail, a double press timed to the second, or a `TZ` set on the container. The suite covers them (`tests/gdrive-retention.test.ts`, `tests/mail-escaping.test.ts`).

#### Going back to the previous image

Nothing is done to the database. The older image runs a daily or weekly backup only in its minute again (no making up), waits an interval (up to a week) after a run that failed everywhere, sends one failure mail a failed destination, names copies to the second, and counts from a scheduled row stamped ahead. Copies named to the millisecond stay where they are and sort among the older names by their time; retention counts and removes them as before.

### The Backup Failure Mail Is the Superadmin's to Switch Off or Send Elsewhere

**Card 2408.** No migration, no setting, no index, no route added, and nothing in `/api/v1` changes (the OpenAPI document is unchanged). The plan is `docs/planning/card-2408.md`.

- **Any administrator could switch the backup failure mail off, or send it to an address of their own**, so that backups made to fail were heard of by nobody else. Now an administrator's save that unticks **Email on failure** where it is ticked, or changes its addresses in any way (an address added beside the others, one removed or replaced, all cleared, or a change made while it is unticked), is refused like card 2398's: `Lowering Keep Last, removing a destination, switching the schedule or the failure mail off, or changing who receives the failure mail needs the superadmin. This save would …`, and nothing is saved. The same addresses in another order, in capitals or separated by semicolons are no change. Ticking it on stays every administrator's.
- **On ☁️ Scheduled Backups** an administrator sees the line under the schedule in those words, **Email on failure** dimmed while it is ticked (unticked, it ticks itself again with the rule in a toast), and its address box dimmed and read-only. The superadmin's panel is as before.

**Owner to know.**

- **The failure mail's switch and its addresses are now yours alone.** A backup an administrator makes fail (a destination edited with a wrong secret) sends the failure mail to the addresses you chose, so you hear of it.
- **Two quiet ways remain, logged and not prevented.** An administrator can point a destination, in place, at a store of their own (another host, bucket, folder or account, its secret typed again): every run succeeds, so no failure mail goes, and from then on the copies go to their store and not yours; the save is a `WARN` row under `BACKUP` naming them. And the mail settings under 📧 Email / SMTP are every administrator's (card 2395): pointed at a server that does not deliver, or cleared, they silence every mail, the failure mail included; the save is a `WARN` row under `SMTP` naming them (card 2396).
- **An administrator who ticks Email on failure on where it has no address** sends nothing until you add one: the address box is yours.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Save["An administrator's save"] --> Q{"Email on failure unticked,<br/>or its addresses changed?"}
    Q -->|"yes"| R["403, nothing saved, no row"]
    Q -->|"no (ticked on, or the same addresses)"| S["saved as before"]
```

### Upstream Kanban, Part One: the Options Column and Its Conversion

**As card 2527 left it.** This part was written for card 2459, when an Options column was added or converted by hand; card 2527 made it a fixed part of every delivery board before release, and its own checks are [Part Seven](#upstream-kanban-part-seven-every-delivery-board-has-its-options-column). The text and checks below describe the image as it is deployed, with both.

**Card 2459, milestone 22, slices S1a and S1b.** **One migration**, `0060_add_upstream_options.sql`, which is the data model of the whole milestone: `columns.role` (NULL, or `'options'` for the board's Options column), `boards.kind` (`'delivery'`, the default, or `'ideas'`), and on cards `committed_at`/`committed_by` and `discarded_at`/`discarded_by` (both `_by` columns `REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`, each with its index). Its one-off commits every existing card at its `created_at` and by its `created_by`: before 0060 nothing was upstream, so every card was committed as it was made. Three repairs join the start-up backfills (step 5 of [Start-Up Sequence](#start-up-sequence)). The plan is `docs/planning/milestone-22-upstream-kanban.md`.

- **Every card created from now on records its commitment** as it is made (`committed_at = created_at`, by its creator), on every creation route, unless it is created in an Options column, where it is an option.
- **Every delivery board has one Options column** (card 2527), titled **Options**, at its far left, with no WIP limit: made with the board, and given to every board made before at the first start ([Part Seven](#upstream-kanban-part-seven-every-delivery-board-has-its-options-column)). It is drawn folded to a narrow strip with its count and its options aging (the oldest option's age, and how many are older than 30 days); a press opens it, the arrow in its header folds it, and each viewer's choice is kept in their browser, per board (`dumpfire-options-open:<user>:<board>`).
- **No column is made into the Options column.** Milestone 22's More → Add Options Column, Add Column's Options tick, the column menu's Make this the Options column… and Stop being the Options column, and the column conversion with its `column_converted_to_options` entry went before release with card 2527. The entry's label stays, for a database a milestone 22 build wrote.
- **Refused, 409**: the Options column renamed to anything but Options, its role taken away, deleted (empty or not), given a WIP limit or passed by any other column; the role or the title Options on any other column of a delivery board; an Options column on an ideas board. Its menu offers no Rename and no Delete column.
- **In `/api/v1`**: `role` on `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns` and `PUT /api/v1/columns/{columnId}`, which answer the refusals above; a 409 on the column delete. There is no convert route for a column. The OpenAPI version and its change note follow with slice S6 of the milestone.
- **Later slices of the milestone**: moving a card out of Options records its commitment from slice S2, [Part Two](#upstream-kanban-part-two-the-commitment-on-a-move) below; archiving an option is a discard from slice S3, [Part Three](#upstream-kanban-part-three-discards-and-abandoned-work); and the delivery figures leave options out from slice S4, [Part Four](#upstream-kanban-part-four-options-left-out-of-the-measures).

**Owner to know.** After the deploy every delivery board shows an empty, folded **Options** strip at its far left (card 2527); nothing else on a board moves, and no figure changes. The Options column is always called Options and cannot be deleted: fold it away instead.

### Upstream Kanban, Part Two: the Commitment on a Move

**Card 2460, milestone 22, slice S2.** No migration. Every route that moves a card (the drag, the board page's menu move and bulk move, All Tasks' move and `PUT /api/v1/cards/{cardId}/move`) goes through `moveCard`, which now records the commitment point:

- **Out of an upstream column into a committed one** (out of the Options column, or off an ideas board), the card is committed: `committed_at` is the moment of the move and `committed_by` the mover. Its activity entry is **Committed card** (`card_committed`, `"<title>": Options → To Do (column <to>, from column <from>)`, the ids naming the column it went into, for the cycle time, and the column it left, for its time in options; an entry written before slice S4 names only ` (column <to>)`, and still reads) in place of Moved card, and its webhook is the new event **`card.committed`**, in place of `card.moved` within a board. Straight into Complete it is Committed card then Completed card.
- **Back into an upstream column**, the commitment is cleared: **Returned card to Options** (`card_returned_to_options`), sent as `card.moved`. From Complete it is Reopened card then Returned card to Options, and one `card.moved`, from the return.
- **Refused, 409, nothing written**: an archived card across the commitment point, either way (`Card "<title>" is archived: restore it before moving it out of or back into Options`), and a committed card with a sub-board into an upstream column (`… has a sub-board, so it cannot go into the Options column: a card with sub-boards is committed work. Keep it in a committed column, or archive it if it is no longer wanted.`). A card already upstream with a sub-board may still move within upstream.
- **Every move on a page says so**: a toast `Committed "<title>"` or `Returned "<title>" to Options` after a drag, an On Hold confirmation, the card menu's **Move to**, a bulk **Move** and All Tasks' **Move** window (the last three in place of "Moved to …"), read from the answer: `PUT /api/cards/reorder` now also lists the ids it committed and returned, and `PUT /api/cards/{id}` adds `committed: [id]` or `returnedToOptions: [id]` for a move that crossed. Each **Move to** list names the Options column (one still carrying another name is marked "(Options)" after it).
- **`card.committed` is a new webhook event.** A webhook whose `events` list is empty receives it from this deploy; one that lists `card.moved` alone does not receive commitments, as it does not receive completions.

**Owner to know.** Moving an idea out of the Options column now commits it, and moving it back makes it an idea again. Receivers of webhooks that mirror columns should add `card.committed`.

**Deploy this slice with slice S4** (the S2 review's C9), which is now built: [Part Four](#upstream-kanban-part-four-options-left-out-of-the-measures). A commitment writes `card_committed`, not `card_moved`, and before S4 a board's cycle time (`src/routes/api/boards/[id]/metrics/+server.ts`) started only at a `card_moved` entry: deployed alone, S2 would leave a card committed straight into a working column (In Progress, say) with no cycle time, and give one committed into To Do its cycle time from its next move. S4 reads the start of work from `card_committed` as well (ruling a), so S2 and S4 go out together, in one image, and the measures follow the commitment point as the plan intends.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Opt["Options<br/>committed_at NULL"] -->|"any move route:<br/>Committed card, card.committed"| Todo["To Do<br/>committed_at = now, committed_by = mover"]
    Todo -->|"moved back:<br/>Returned card to Options, card.moved"| Opt
    Arch["archived card across,<br/>or a committed card with sub-boards into Options"] -->|"409"| Refused["nothing written"]
```

### Upstream Kanban, Part Three: Discards and Abandoned Work

**Card 2461, milestone 22, slice S3.** No migration: the discard mark, `discarded_at`/`discarded_by`, came with 0060 in [Part One](#upstream-kanban-part-one-the-options-column-and-its-conversion). Every archive, delete and restore of a card goes through `archiveCard`, `deleteCard` and `restoreCard` (the card window and the card menu on a board, the card window in All Tasks and in All To Do, the board page's bulk archive, the Archived page, All Tasks' and the board's Archived Cards, and `DELETE`/`PUT` on `/api/v1/cards/{cardId}`), which now record what was archived:

- **An option archived is discarded.** A card archived from the Options column, or from any column of an ideas board, gets `discarded_at` (the archive's moment) and `discarded_by` (who archived it); its activity entry is **Discarded card** (`card_discarded`, `"<title>": discarded from <column>`) in place of Archived card, and its webhook the new event **`card.discarded`**. The Archived page, All Tasks' Archived Cards and the board's Archived Cards mark it **Discarded**, with the tooltip "Discarded from the Options column. Restoring it makes it an idea again."
- **The page says so as it happens**: archiving an idea on the board (card window or card menu) or from All Tasks' card window asks with "This idea will be recorded as discarded." at the end of the question, and the toast reads `Discarded "<title>". Restore it from Archived Cards.`; the board's bulk archive counts the ideas among what it archived. All Tasks tells an idea by its column and its board's kind, so a card on an ideas board is named a discard there too since [Part Five](#upstream-kanban-part-five-ideas-boards-and-send-to-board); All To Do lists no upstream column.
- **An option deleted for good** writes **Discarded card** (`"<title>": deleted from <column>`) and then **Deleted card**, and sends `card.discarded` then `card.deleted`. A card already archived writes only Deleted card, wherever it is: one discarded already, or one archived as committed work before its column was converted to Options (which only a milestone 22 build before card 2527 could do).
- **A restore** clears the mark with the archive: the card is back in its column, still an option, and its entry is **Restored card**, `"<title>": back in <column>`. No webhook, as before.
- **Committed work archived before it was finished is abandoned**: a card archived from a committed column that is not Complete writes **Archived unfinished card** (`card_abandoned`, `"<title>": archived unfinished, from <column>`) in place of Archived card, with no webhook and nothing on the card. A card archived from Complete (or Done) is still **Archived card**.
- **Not discards**: deleting a column or a board, Clear Cards and Purge Archived Cards (decision M22-9).
- **The Options column's delete refusal** said that archiving discards: `This Options column still holds 2 options: move them out, or archive them to discard them, first.` Card 2527 then made the Options column never deleted, empty or not, and its menu offers no Delete column ([Part Seven](#upstream-kanban-part-seven-every-delivery-board-has-its-options-column)).
- **`card.discarded` is a new webhook event.** A webhook whose `events` list is empty receives it from this deploy.
- **The upstream figures** (`upstreamFigures` in `src/lib/server/upstream.ts`: options now, committed from options, returned to options, discarded, sent on, abandoned, the discard rate and the options' aging, over a window that includes both its ends, as reports do) are shown from slice S4 on: on the board's Stats panel, in reports and in the activity report ([Part Four](#upstream-kanban-part-four-options-left-out-of-the-measures)).

**What changes at the first start.** Nothing new. The start-up repair `Cleared the discard mark on <n> card(s) that are not archived` should not appear: every restore now clears the mark itself.

**Owner to know.** Archiving or deleting an idea in the Options column now discards it, and the page and the archive lists say so; restoring it brings it back as an idea. Archiving unfinished committed work is recorded as **Archived unfinished card**, not Archived card. A board whose last column is not titled Complete or Done (Released, Shipped) has its finished work read as unfinished when archived. Searching the Audit page's Action filter, or a script calling `GET /api/v1/audit-log?action=card_archived`, no longer finds unfinished work archived (now `card_abandoned`) or options archived (now `card_discarded`); ask for those too. Receivers of webhooks that mirror the Options column should add `card.discarded`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Opt["Options"] -->|"archive:<br/>Discarded card, card.discarded"| Disc["Archived, marked Discarded<br/>discarded_at, discarded_by"]
    Disc -->|"restore:<br/>Restored card: back in Options"| Opt
    Opt -->|"delete for good:<br/>Discarded card, Deleted card"| Gone(("gone"))
    Work["To Do / In Progress"] -->|"archive:<br/>Archived unfinished card (no webhook)"| Arch["Archived"]
```

### Upstream Kanban, Part Four: Options Left Out of the Measures

**Card 2462, milestone 22, slices S4a and S4b.** No migration. One rule: **a delivery measure counts committed cards on delivery boards only**. A card in a board's Options column, or on an ideas board, is an option, and is in none of them; where a figure describes upstream it comes from `upstreamFigures`, and time in options from `timeInOptions`. Deploy it with slice S2 ([Part Two](#upstream-kanban-part-two-the-commitment-on-a-move)), in one image.

- **Lead time** runs from the commitment, `committed_at`, to completion, labelled **Lead time (commitment to done)**: Complete is the delivery point, so customer lead time and system lead time are the same. For every card made before milestone 22 the commitment is its creation, so its lead time is as it was.
- **Cycle time**, "time from start of work to done", starts at the first **Moved card** entry, or at a **Committed card** entry into a column that is not a queue, at or after the card's current commitment and not after its completion, and is clamped to between 0 and the lead time. A queue is the board's first committed column, a To Do or On Hold column, or a column titled as one (the titles reports take for To Do, and Ready, Selected, Next, Up Next, Queue, Queued). A card created straight into a working column has no cycle time, as before.
- **New figures on `GET /api/boards/:id/metrics`**: `committed` (**Committed (all)**, the cards that arrived as committed work in the window), `timeInOptions` (how long the cards committed from options waited there) and `upstream` (options now, committed from options, returned to options, discarded, sent to other boards, abandoned, discard rate, the oldest option's age and how many are over 30 days).
- **The board's Stats panel** (More → Statistics): its totals, average age and bars leave the Options column out; the board's options are one line, `Options N · discard rate X%`. Under Delivery Metrics: **Lead time (commitment to done)** and **Cycle time: time from start of work to done**, each with its help; **Throughput** and **Committed (all)** side by side; `Abandoned: N` on any board with some (help: "committed work archived before Complete"); and, where the Options column holds a card now or an upstream figure of the period is not zero (card 2527: every delivery board has an Options column, mostly empty), an **Upstream** block: Committed from options, Options now, Returned to options, Discarded, Sent to other boards, Discard rate, Oldest option (days), Options over 30 days, Time in options. An ideas board's panel shows `N ideas`, the Upstream block and the flow diagram, and no delivery tiles, bars, metrics or burndown. A failed read of the metrics says `Metrics could not be loaded` with **Retry**; All Tasks' panel with no board chosen says `Choose a board to see its delivery metrics`, and with one chosen counts that board's cards only, its Options stand-in only where it has an upstream column (every delivery board, since card 2527).
- **The flow diagram** leaves the Options band out. On a delivery board whose Options column has something to show, as the Upstream block, it offers **Show upstream**, off by default, which asks `GET /api/boards/:id/cfd?days=30&upstream=true` and draws the band at the bottom with its top edge dashed and labelled **commitment point**; each viewer's choice is kept in their browser (`df-cfd-show-upstream`). A column converted to Options during the window, which only a milestone 22 build before card 2527 could do, is left out with its band in the default view, its committed history before the conversion too. An ideas board draws all its columns, with no toggle.
- **The dashboard**: a board's count and bar are its committed cards; on a board with options the count's tooltip says `Committed cards only: N options in its Options column are not counted`. An ideas board's row reads `N ideas`, with no completion bar, and is left out of board health and the category distribution; sorting by Cards orders it by its ideas. Display's done boards switched off does not hide a board that still holds options. The All Tasks row's tooltip says its cards are committed ones, options not counted. Aging runs from the commitment.
- **All Tasks**: every board's options are one **Options** bucket, drawn first and marked **not committed**, in none of the header's figures, and drawn only while it holds cards (card 2527). An ordinary column called Options keeps its own bucket.
- **Goals and the plan**: the goals list writes `3/5 and 2 options`; the plan's progress notes `and 2 options` under its cards complete; the work table marks an option **Option** (with an **Options** filter where there are any), the graph draws it dashed with the legend **Option (not committed)**, and the critical path tags it **option**. An option is never startable nor listed as waiting, and stays in the graph as an open blocker.
- **Reports**: the PDF gives one line `Upstream: N options now … discard rate X%` when an upstream figure is not zero, and `Abandoned (committed work archived before Complete): N` on its own when that is not zero. A report about one person has neither and, where its boards have an Options column, an ideas board or abandoned work in the period, says `The upstream line (options, commitments from options, discards and abandoned work) is left out of a report about one person: those figures describe the boards, not one person's work.`; the Reports page's Person hint says the same. `GET /api/v1/reports/activity` gives `upstream`, null for one person.
- **Burndown**: a card's scope starts at its commitment, and options are left out. **Sub-boards**: an option on a sub-board does not hold back completing its parent card. **My Tasks** and `GET /api/v1/me/stats`: an option is not active work.
- **Both CSV exports** gain **Stage** (Option or Committed: they list live cards, options included) and **Committed** (`committed_at`) at the end; every other column keeps its place.
- **The Committed card entry's detail** now ends ` (column <to>, from column <from>)`; one written before ends ` (column <to>)` and still reads.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Opt["Options<br/>options: in no delivery figure"] -->|"commitment point:<br/>committed_at"| Todo["To Do (a queue)"]
    Opt -->|"straight into work:<br/>cycle time starts here"| Prog["In Progress"]
    Todo -->|"first move:<br/>cycle time starts"| Prog
    Prog --> Done["Complete<br/>lead time = completed_at − committed_at"]
    Opt -.->|"archive"| Disc["Discarded<br/>(discard rate)"]
    Prog -.->|"archive"| Ab["Abandoned"]
```

**What changes at the first start.** Nothing: no migration, and no repair.

**Owner to know.** Ordinary boards' figures are unchanged, with one exception: a card moved between two Complete columns after it was completed had a negative cycle time, and it now reads 0. The **Abandoned** line can appear on ordinary boards' report PDFs, and `Abandoned: N` on their Stats panel, since abandonment is recorded on every board from slice S3. A report about one person carries the sentence saying the upstream line is left out where its boards have an Options column, an ideas board or abandoned work in the period, so an ordinary board with abandoned work can show it too. The Stats panel names lead time "Lead time (commitment to done)" and shows Throughput and Committed (all) on every board. A script that reads a CSV export by its number of columns sees two more.

### Upstream Kanban, Part Five: Ideas Boards and Send to Board

**Card 2463, milestone 22, slices S5a and S5b.** No migration: `boards.kind` came with 0060 in [Part One](#upstream-kanban-part-one-the-options-column-and-its-conversion). Every board on production is a delivery board, and stays one until its owner changes it.

- **An ideas board.** **+ New Board** asks for the kind: **Delivery board** (the default, as before: To Do, On Hold, In Progress, Complete, with the Options column at its far left since card 2527) or **Ideas board** (New Ideas, Shaping, Ready for Replenishment). Every column of an ideas board is upstream: each offers **Add idea**, shows its oldest idea's age and how many are older than 30 days, keeps a WIP limit if one is set, and has no Show Add Task. The header says **Ideas board**; **More** has no Burndown; Statistics show `N ideas`, the Upstream block and the flow diagram. No column of an ideas board may be called To Do, On Hold or Complete, or a name that means one (Todo, Blocked, Parked, Waiting, Done); a column holding ideas is not deleted. A sub-board is always a delivery board, and none is made under an idea or an option.
- **Converting a delivery board** (the owner or an administrator): **More → Make this an ideas board…** counts the board's live and archived cards and asks; every card becomes an idea, its commitment cleared, the empty To Do, On Hold and Complete columns go, and so does the Options column when it holds no card (card 2527), and one entry, **Converted board to an ideas board**, is written, with no mail or webhook. A board with no cards has its columns replaced with the ideas board's. It is refused, said before the question, while a live card has a sub-board (one the page cannot see, archived or on a board you cannot open, is refused by the server in its own words), a To Do or On Hold column holds cards (rename it), or a Complete column holds cards (move or delete them). `POST /api/boards/:id/convert` and `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/convert`.
- **Going back**: **More → Make this a delivery board…** only while the ideas board holds no cards, live or archived; its columns are replaced with the delivery board's five, Options first (card 2527), recorded as **Updated board**.
- **Send to board…**, in the card menu and the card window, for an idea only (any card of an ideas board, or a card in a delivery board's Options column), to someone who can edit the board. The Send window lists the delivery boards the user can edit (`GET /api/cards/:id/send`, new, page only) and sends **To its Options**, still an idea, or **Commit to its To Do** (the first To Do column, else the first working column, never On Hold), which commits it. `POST /api/cards/:id/send` and `POST /api/v1/cards/{cardId}/send`. The board it left records **Sent card to another board** (`card_sent`), sending `card.moved`; the board it joined records the arrival, and **Committed card** for To Do.
- **Every move of an idea to another board is a Send in the record**: the card window's board picker, All Tasks' Move and the v1 move write **Sent card to another board** in place of Moved card to another board on the board it left, so "Sent to other boards" and the discard rate count every way an idea leaves. A card with a sub-board does not go into another board's Options column or onto an ideas board.
- **All Tasks** gives its Stats panel the chosen board's real kind, and names an idea archived from an ideas board a discard.
- **No sub-board is offered under an idea or an option**: the card menu's Add Sub-board and the card window's create, link and add are hidden for one (its existing sub-boards still open and delete), and the dashboard's New Sub-board is not offered on an ideas board. A Send from a card window with changes not saved asks first (**Send without saving**); after a Send the focus goes to the column the card left.

**What changes at the first start.** Nothing: no migration, and no repair.

**Owner to know.**

- Converting a delivery board needs its **To Do and On Hold columns renamed, or emptied, first**, and its **Complete column emptied** (move those cards to a delivery board, or delete them): an ideas board has no such columns. The board says which column before it asks.
- An idea moved to another board **by any route** (Send, the card window's board picker, All Tasks' Move, the API) is recorded and counted as **sent**, not moved: a script reading the audit log for `card_moved_away` no longer sees those, and should ask for `card_sent` too. Its webhook is still `card.moved`, with `data.action` `card_sent`.
- Only the board's owner or an administrator sees **Make this an ideas board…** or **Make this a delivery board…**; an editor does not. A sub-board offers neither.
- Going back to a delivery board is only possible once the ideas board is empty, archived cards included: move its ideas to delivery boards, or delete them.
- An empty board switched either way, and a board with no cards converted, has its columns replaced, and their flow-diagram history goes with them.
- Send keeps an idea's age; the labels, category and goal of the board it left stay behind, as for any move to another board.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    New["+ New Board<br/>Kind: Ideas board"] --> IB["Ideas board<br/>New Ideas · Shaping ·<br/>Ready for Replenishment"]
    DB0["Delivery board"] -->|"More → Make this an ideas board…<br/>(owner; count confirmed)"| IB
    IB -->|"More → Make this a delivery board…<br/>(empty only)"| DB0
    IB -->|"Send to board… → To its Options"| Opt["Another delivery board's<br/>Options (still an idea)"]
    IB -->|"Send to board… → Commit to its To Do"| Todo["Its To Do<br/>(Committed card)"]
```

### Upstream Kanban, Part Six: the Public API, Version 1.3.0

**Card 2464, milestone 22, slice S6.** No migration. The OpenAPI document (`/api/v1/openapi.json`, drawn at `/docs`) is version **1.3.0**, with a change note of its own dated 2026-10-26 listing every change milestone 22 made to v1; `DUMPFIRE_API.md` and [External API Reference](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-10-26) each have a "Changes on 2026-10-26" section with the same list. The writes of Parts One to Five reached v1 as they were built; this slice adds:

- **`GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/upstream`** (new), view access: over the last `days` days (1 to 365, 30 by default) the board's options now and their aging, committed from options, returned to options, discarded, sent on and abandoned, the discard rate, and `committedAll`, **Committed (all)**, the figures the board's Stats panel shows.
- **`GET /api/v1/boards?kind=delivery|ideas`** and **`GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/cards?stage=option|committed`** (new filters); anything else is `400` quoting what was sent.
- **`avgLeadTimeDays` on `GET /api/v1/me/stats`**, the average days from commitment to done, beside `avgCycleTimeDays` at the same value, which is a lead time named cycle time for history.

**What changes at the first start.** Nothing: no migration, and no repair.

**Owner to know.**

- An integration that reads `info.version` sees `1.3.0`. Every addition is a field, a filter or an operation, with one exception: a `kind` on `GET /api/v1/boards` or a `stage` on `GET /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/cards` that the older image ignored, `?kind=all` for example, is now `400`.
- **Scripts that read the audit log or the activity report**: `card_archived` is now written only for a card archived from a Complete column. Unfinished committed work archived is `card_abandoned`, and an option `card_discarded`, so a count of `card_archived` alone undercounts; a commitment is `card_committed`, not `card_moved`, and an idea leaving its board `card_sent`, not `card_moved_away`.
- **Webhooks**: a webhook with an empty events list receives `card.committed` and `card.discarded`; one that lists `card.moved` but not `card.committed` does not hear a card leave an Options column within one board. A move to another board still sends each board its own `card.moved` (`card_sent` to the board it left, `card_moved_in` to the board it joins), and the board it joins `card.committed` after it.
- `avgCycleTimeDays` on `me/stats` is unchanged in value; its description now says what it is, a lead time, commitment to done. Read `avgLeadTimeDays` in new code.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Key["API key"] --> U["GET /boards/:id/upstream<br/>?days=N"]
    Key --> K["GET /boards?kind="]
    Key --> S["GET /boards/:id/cards?stage="]
    Key --> M["GET /me/stats<br/>avgLeadTimeDays"]
    U --> F["upstreamFigures +<br/>committedAll"]
    F --> P["the same figures as<br/>the Stats panel"]
```

### Upstream Kanban, Part Seven: Every Delivery Board Has Its Options Column

**Card 2527, milestone 22, slices S1 and S2.** No migration and no schema change: `columns.role` came with 0060 in [Part One](#upstream-kanban-part-one-the-options-column-and-its-conversion). It ships in the same image as Parts One to Six: milestone 22 is not on production yet, so no live board has had an Options column, and the opt-in routes and menu items it replaces were never released. The plan is `docs/planning/2527-options-on-every-board.md`.

- **Every delivery board, sub-boards included, has exactly one Options column**, titled **Options**, at its far left, with no WIP limit; an ideas board has none. A new board, a sub-board, and an empty ideas board switched to delivery are made with Options, To Do, On Hold, In Progress and Complete, in both trees.
- **A start-up step gives it to every board made before**: the first step of `runBackfills`, at every start and after every restore. A delivery board with none gets one, empty, at one less than its lowest position, so every other column keeps its place; one with another title is renamed Options; one that is not leftmost is moved there; a second one on a board becomes an ordinary column, its cards committed work. No activity entry, webhook or mail. Each count has its `WARN` line (see [Start-Up Sequence](#start-up-sequence)) and its clause in Import Backup's answer: the added, renamed and moved ones in its "Filled in" line, a demoted one in its "Cleared:" sentence (`the Options role of <n> second Options column(s), each board keeping its leftmost`).
- **It is a fixed part of the board.** Renamed to anything but Options: `409 The Options column is always called Options.` Its role taken away: `409 Every delivery board keeps its Options column.` Deleted, empty or not: `409 Every delivery board keeps its Options column. Fold it away with the arrow on its strip instead.` The role on another column: `409 This board already has its Options column.` Another column of a delivery board created or renamed Options, in any case: `409 Only the board's Options column is called Options. Choose another name.` A value sent back unchanged writes nothing and is not refused. A plain column already called Options before the deploy is left as it is.
- **On the board**: folded by default to its strip; the strip opens it and the arrow in its header folds it, and each viewer's choice is remembered per board in their browser, so another browser opens it folded. Its menu has no Rename and no Delete column, and a click on its title renames nothing. No screen reads "Options (Options)". Add Column makes ordinary columns only; More has no **Add Options Column**, and no column menu offers **Make this the Options column…** or **Stop being the Options column**. On a phone or a narrow window (768 pixels or less, where the columns scroll sideways) the board opens scrolled to To Do, the strip a swipe to its left. Create Board's line for a delivery board names the Options column.
- **Where there is nothing upstream to show, nothing is shown**: the Stats panel's Upstream block and the flow diagram's **Show upstream** appear only where the Options column holds a card now or a figure of the period is not zero, and All Tasks' **Options** column only while it holds cards.
- **Making a delivery board an ideas board** removes an empty Options column with the empty To Do, On Hold and Complete columns, named in the question and the entry; one holding cards stays, an ordinary column.
- **API 1.3.0** (unreleased; its 2026-10-26 note amended in place): `POST /api/v1/columns/{columnId}/convert` and the page's twin are gone (`404`); `POST` and `PUT` on columns, and `DELETE`, answer the refusals above. The tracking wrapper has no `convert-column` and no `-Role`.

**Owner to know.**

- After the deploy every delivery board shows an empty, folded **Options** strip at its far left, its count `0`. Nothing else on a board moves, and no figure changes.
- The Options column cannot be renamed or deleted. Fold it away instead; the choice is kept per board, in each browser.
- A board that already had an ordinary column called Options keeps it: two columns read Options, and only the leftmost is the strip. Rename the plain one if that confuses.
- The start-up log has one line about it, at the first start, counting the boards.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Start["First start of the image"] --> Step["runBackfills, first step"]
    Step -->|"a delivery board with none"| Add["an empty Options column at<br/>MIN(position) - 1, titled Options"]
    Step -->|"a role column with another title"| Rename["renamed Options"]
    Step -->|"an ideas board"| None["no Options column"]
    Add --> Log["WARN: Added an Options column at the far left<br/>of N delivery board(s) that had none"]
    Log --> Board["every delivery board:<br/>a folded Options strip, nothing else moved"]
    Board -->|"rename, role off, delete"| Refused["409, nothing written"]
```

**Check 0z: the rehearsal and the boards.** Run check 0y's rehearsal (`npm run rehearse -- <export.db>`) on an Admin Export copy with the new code; then, on the same export, read-only, `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM boards;` (every board on production is a delivery board: 0060 is not there yet) and `SELECT b.id, b.name, c.id, c.title FROM columns c JOIN boards b ON b.id = c.board_id WHERE lower(trim(c.title)) = 'options';`. Expect `PASSED`; among the notes `columns had N row(s) and has M: each delivery board that had none was given its Options column at the start (card 2527)`, where M − N is the count of boards; and no `a second run's Options step found work`. Note the boards the second query lists, if any: each already has a plain column called Options (check 556). It is a fault if it prints `FAILED`, if M − N is not the count of boards, or if a second run's Options step found work.

- At the next start, none of the four lines. After **Import Backup** of a backup made before this image, the restore's "Filled in" line ends with `an Options column at the far left of <n> delivery board(s)`.

### API 1.3.1 (2026-10-27)

**Cards 2480, 2520, 2512 and 2541.** No migration, no schema change and nothing new at the first start. The OpenAPI document is version **1.3.1**, its "Changed on 2026-10-27" note listing the three v1 corrections; `DUMPFIRE_API.md` and [External API Reference](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-10-27) each have a "Changes on 2026-10-27" section with the same list. Four answers change:

- **The activity report's `created` bucket** (card 2480): a card raised in the window, not edited since and never moved, by the activity log, is `created` wherever it was raised. It had to be in the board's first column, so a card raised straight into In Progress and left alone was `progressed`.
- **A new column keeps the WIP limit sent with it** (card 2520), on `POST /api/v1/boards/{boardId}/columns` and the board page's route, read as an update reads it. It was dropped, and the column made with no limit.
- **Activity entries written in the same second list the later first** (card 2512), on the board's Activity Log and All Tasks' activity panel (`GET /api/activity`). A move that commits and completes a card writes both in one second, and "Committed card" could be listed above "Completed card".
- **`GET /api/v1/me/stats` averages live cards only** (card 2541): `avgLeadTimeDays` and `avgCycleTimeDays` leave out an archived card, as the board metrics do. `cardsCompleted` and `streak` still count its completion, a record of what the person did.

On production, as **O** with an API key of O's, in the `curl.exe` form of [Part Six](#upstream-kanban-part-six-the-public-api-version-130). Check 561 makes a board; check 564 deletes it. Check 565 makes and deletes its own.

### Card Images Through the API and Image Retention (API 1.7.0)

**Card 2754.** No migration and no schema change: `card_attachments` already holds what is needed, and `activity_log.source` is free text. The OpenAPI document is version **1.7.0**, with a "Changed on 2026-11-05" note; [External API Reference](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-11-05) has the same list. What changes:

- **Three `/api/v1` operations** list a card's files, download one, and attach an image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, up to 5 MB, its metadata taken out), into the same uploads folder as the card window's: see [Attachment Files](#attachment-files). The upload's 5 MB is set in the application ([Upload Size Limits](#upload-size-limits)). `BODY_SIZE_LIMIT` already allows more, but **behind nginx add the `location ~ ^/api/v1/cards/[0-9]+/attachments$` block** of [Reverse Proxy — Nginx](#reverse-proxy--nginx) before the deploy: without it nginx's own 1 MB default refuses every image over 1 MB with its own HTML `413`, which never reaches DumpFire. Cloudflare Tunnel needs nothing.
