- **Image retention** starts with the first sweep, 15 minutes after the first start where the schedulers run, and moves at most 200 images a run, every six hours: see [Image retention](#image-retention).
- **The card window shows an image only when its bytes are the image type it was stored as**; any other is a download. An image that was uploaded with the wrong type stops opening in the browser and downloads instead.
- **A new activity source**, `system`, on the Audit page's Source filter as DumpFire.

#### Before the deploy: count what retention will first move

Decide `IMAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` first: leave it unset for 180, set a number from 30 to 3650, or `off`. Then, on the production database, read-only, count what the first runs will move at 180 days (change both `-180 days` for another setting):

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS images, COALESCE(SUM(a.size_bytes), 0) AS bytes
  FROM card_attachments a
  JOIN cards c     ON c.id = a.card_id
  JOIN columns col ON col.id = c.column_id
 WHERE lower(trim(CASE WHEN instr(a.mime_type, ';') > 0
                       THEN substr(a.mime_type, 1, instr(a.mime_type, ';') - 1)
                       ELSE a.mime_type END))
       IN ('image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/gif', 'image/webp')
   AND (   (c.archived_at IS NOT NULL AND c.archived_at < datetime('now', '-180 days'))
        OR (c.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND c.completed_at < datetime('now', '-180 days')
            AND lower(trim(col.title)) IN ('complete', 'done')));
```

Run it with `sqlite3 -readonly <database>`. At most 200 move a sweep, so a count of 450 is moved over three runs, the last about twelve hours after the first. Every one stays in the trash 30 days. If the count is more than you expect, take a copy of the uploads folder first ([Backing up and restoring the files](#backing-up-and-restoring-the-files)), or deploy with `IMAGE_RETENTION_DAYS=off` and set it later.

#### After the deploy

- `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` answers `"version":"1.7.0"`.
- With a key, `POST /api/v1/cards/<a test card>/attachments` with a screenshot, `Content-Type: image/png`: `201` with an `id`; the card window shows the image, and its activity "Attached …" from the API. A file renamed from `.svg` to `.png` and sent the same way: `415`.
- 16 minutes after the start, where the count was above 0: one `[INFO] [UPLOADS] Moved N image(s) of cards closed more than 180 days ago to the trash` line, and the Audit page with Source DumpFire lists the `attachment_expired` entries. No `[ERROR] [UPLOADS]` line.

**Going back to the previous image.** Nothing is done to the database. Images uploaded through a key stay attached and open in the card window, which then shows an image by its name and stored type alone. The rows retention deleted stay deleted; their files are in the trash for 30 days, where an Import Backup of an earlier backup puts back what its rows name. The older image answers the three attachment paths `404`, runs no retention, reads a `system` entry as the web application's, and answers `info.version` `1.6.0`.

### The Update That Brings Migration 0065 and the MFA Key File

**Card 2768 (build card B1 of card 2669).** Migration `0065_add_mfa_storage.sql`, additive only:
four empty tables (`mfa_factors`, `mfa_recovery_codes`, `sign_in_challenges`,
`enrolment_links`) and eleven `users` columns at their defaults (see
[Data Model](data-model.md#two-step-sign-in-storage-migration-0065)). API v1 does not change.
What changes:

- **The server will not start without `MFA_KEY_FILE`.** The image runs under the production
  rules, so the key file must be made, mounted and named before this image's first start: see
  [The Key That Protects Authenticator Secrets](#the-key-that-protects-authenticator-secrets).
  A deploy without it fails loudly, with exit code 1 and one `[CRITICAL] [AUTH]` line, never
  silently.
- **Nobody notices anything else.** Sign-in does not ask for a second factor yet (card 2769),
  so no account has one, and nothing on any page changes.
- **Backups and Export** leave out pending sign-ins and enrolment links, and hold second
  factors only as ciphertext and recovery codes only as hashes, never the key. All are empty
  until card 2769.
- **Import Backup** restores second factors by their own rules, and names any account left with
  none, once two-step sign-in is in use: see
  [Restoring from Backup](admin-guide.md#restoring-from-backup).
- **Setting a password, and a change of an account's email address or role**, end its pending
  sign-ins and enrolment links, in the same transaction. Their answers and log lines are
  unchanged.

#### Before the deploy

**Check H1: make the key and mount it.** On the Docker host:
`openssl rand -hex 32 > /srv/dumpfire-secrets/dumpfire_mfa_key`, `chmod 600` it, copy it
somewhere apart from the database backups (a password manager), mount it read-only into the
container (`-v /srv/dumpfire-secrets/dumpfire_mfa_key:/run/secrets/dumpfire_mfa_key:ro`, or the
Compose `secrets:` of [Docker Compose](#docker-compose)), and set
`MFA_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/dumpfire_mfa_key`. Expect `wc -c` to say 65 (64 hex characters and a
newline) and `ls -l` mode `-rw-------`. It is a fault if it is any other size.

**Check H2, on a staging copy only: the refusal.** Start the new image without `MFA_KEY_FILE`
(the [rehearsal](#rehearsing-an-update-against-a-copy) helper `rehearse` does, unless given
`-e MFA_KEY_FILE=…`). Expect exit code 1, `docker logs` ending with `[CRITICAL] [AUTH] The
server will not start. MFA_KEY_FILE must be set in production…`, and no `Listening on`. It is a
fault if it starts, or if the line names no variable. A rehearsal of the migration itself then
needs the key: give `rehearse` `-v <key file>:/run/secrets/dumpfire_mfa_key:ro -e
MFA_KEY_FILE=/run/secrets/dumpfire_mfa_key` as its extra options.

#### What changes at the first start

- **One line from the runner**: `Applied migration: 0065_add_mfa_storage.sql`. Nothing is
  declared to the rehearsal and nothing is backfilled.
- **No `[AUTH]` line** about the key: with no factor stored there is nothing to compare. A key
  mounted as a Docker Swarm secret (`0444`) gives one `[WARN] [STARTUP]` line saying the file can
  be read by others, at every start, which is expected for that mount.

#### After the deploy

`<c>` is the container name. `q` is a read-only query of the database:

```bash
q() { docker exec <c> node -e "const D=require('better-sqlite3');const d=new D('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true});console.log(JSON.stringify(d.prepare(process.argv[1]).all()))" "$1"; }
```

| # | Do | Expect | A fault if |
|---|----|--------|------------|
| H3 | Start the new image with H1 in place; `docker logs <c>` | It starts (`Listening on`); no `[AUTH]` CRITICAL or ERROR line; no "inside the database's directory" WARN. A Swarm secret's one readable-by-others WARN is expected | A CRITICAL or ERROR line, or the inside-directory WARN |
| H4 | `q "SELECT hash FROM __drizzle_migrations WHERE hash LIKE '0065%'"`, then `q "SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mfa_factors) f, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mfa_recovery_codes) r, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sign_in_challenges) c, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrolment_links) l, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM settings WHERE key='mfa_key_check') k"` | One row, `0065_add_mfa_storage.sql`; all five counts 0 | 0065 missing, or any count above 0 before card 2769 |
| H5 | `q "SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM users WHERE mfa_known_wrong<>0 OR mfa_other_wrong<>0 OR failed_codes_since_sign_in<>0 OR last_sign_in_at IS NOT NULL"` | `n` 0 | Above 0 |
| H6 | On staging only: mount the key file into the database's folder, set `MFA_KEY_FILE=/app/data/mfa.key`, and restart | It starts, with one `[WARN] [STARTUP]` line on the console naming the key file as inside the database's directory | No WARN |
| H7 | Sign in; change your own password and your own email address; as an administrator reset another account's password and change its role | Each works as before; their `[AUTH]` lines on the Logs page read as before | Any change in what is answered or logged |
| H8 | Admin → Scheduled Backups → **Run Now**; and **Export Backup** | Both succeed. Their second-factor contents mean something only once card 2769 lets accounts enrol: then both hold `mfa_factors` rows as ciphertext, and neither holds the key | Either fails |
| H9 | On staging: Admin → Backup & Restore → **Import Backup** of the export from H8 | The report has no line about second factors (nobody has enrolled) and says everybody was signed out | A second-factor line, or a failed restore |

#### Going back to the previous image

Nothing is done to the database. The older image keeps 0065's tables and columns: it drops
nothing, its schema check reports them at every start (`[ERROR] [DB]`, expected) and does not act
on them, and it ignores `MFA_KEY_FILE`. Its backups carry any pending sign-in and enrolment link
rows, and its Import Backup copies the four tables as any other table, ignoring card 2768's
restore rules. Before card 2769 every one of them is empty, so none of that holds anything.
**Coming forward again**, 0065 is already recorded and is not run, and the key must still be the
one mounted before. Keep the key file and its mount in place while going back and forth. An
image from before card 2773 does not read `MFA_KEY_FILE_PREVIOUS` and cannot change the key: after
a [change of key](#changing-the-key), going back to one needs `MFA_KEY_FILE` to name the **new**
key, whose check the database now holds.

### The Update That Runs the Server as a User Who Is Not Root

**Card 2776 (build card B7 of card 2669).** No migration, no setting, no route. The server runs as
the image's own `node` user, uid and gid 1000, and no longer as root, so a fault that let
someone run code in it would not run as root, and a file's mode (the MFA key file's `600`) means
something inside the container. What changes:

- **The data folder must belong to uid 1000.** `/app/data`, on the volume, is the one folder the
  server writes: the database and its `-wal` and `-shm` files, `uploads/` and its `.trash/`,
  the backup's temporary copies, and now the import's two files (below). A new named volume takes
  the image's owner for it, so a new installation needs nothing. **A volume made by an older image
  is root's**, and the server cannot write it: give it to uid 1000 (check U1) before anything from
  this image touches the volume, the commands of this guide run from it included, and **again
  whenever an image from before card 2776 has run on it**: a rollback to one, or step 5 of a
  rehearsal, writes root's files (a card's uploads folder, `.trash/`, a `-wal` file) that the
  server then cannot write.
- **The MFA key file must be readable by uid 1000** (check U2). It was read as root.
- **An import writes its two files beside the database**, `/app/data/dumpfire.db.restore-temp`
  (named after the database, with no `.db` at its end, so one left by a stopped import is never
  taken for a hidden database at start) and `/app/data/.pre-restore-safety.json`, both readable by
  their owner alone, and no longer in `/app`, the code's folder, which the
  server cannot write. The safety copy is now on the volume: it survives the container being
  recreated. Remove it once an import is known to be
  good, as before, at its new path (see [How Large an Import Can Be](#how-large-an-import-can-be)).
- **`docker exec` and `docker run` run as `node` too**, by default. Three kinds of command in this
  guide change with it, and say so where they are: one that copies out of the volume to a folder
  of yours runs as your own user (`--user "$(id -u):$(id -g)"`); one that copies into the volume,
  or renames or moves files on it, runs as root and gives what it wrote to uid 1000; and a file put
  into the container with `docker cp` belongs to root, so it is made readable with `docker exec -u
  root <container> chown node <file>` and removed with `docker exec -u root <container> rm <file>`.
  **Under rootless Docker**, a container's uid 1000 is not you on the host: run a command that
  copies to or from a folder of yours with `--user root` there, which is you.
- **Nobody notices anything on the site.**

#### Before the deploy

**Check U1: give the volume to uid 1000.** With the old container stopped, and the volume's name
from `docker inspect --format '{{range .Mounts}}{{.Name}}{{println}}{{end}}' dumpfire`:

```bash
docker run --rm --user root -v dumpfire-data:/app/data --entrypoint chown dumpfire:latest -R 1000:1000 /app/data
docker run --rm -v dumpfire-data:/app/data --entrypoint sh dumpfire:latest -c 'id && touch /app/data/.write-test && rm /app/data/.write-test && echo writable'
```

Expect the second to print `uid=1000(node) gid=1000(node)` and `writable`. It is a fault if it
says `Permission denied`. A bind mount in place of a named volume is given the same way on the
host: `sudo chown -R 1000:1000 <the folder>`. Under rootless Docker or user-namespace remapping,
uid 1000 in the container is another uid on the host: run the first command as written, which
asks Docker to map it.

**Check U2: the MFA key file.** On the host: `sudo chown 1000:1000
/srv/dumpfire-secrets/dumpfire_mfa_key`, keeping mode `600`. A Docker Swarm secret is given
`uid: "1000"` and `mode: 0400` in its `secrets:` entry, or is read at its default `0444`, root's,
which `node` can read, with the warning
[Mounting It](#mounting-it) describes. It is a fault if the new container stops at start with
`[CRITICAL] [AUTH]` naming the key file as unreadable.

#### After the deploy

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| U3 | `docker exec dumpfire id` | `uid=1000(node) gid=1000(node)` | `uid=0(root)` |
| U4 | Sign in, and attach a file to a card | Both work | `attempt to write a readonly database` or `EACCES` in `docker logs` |
| U5 | On a staging copy, Import Backup | It succeeds, and `docker exec dumpfire ls -l /app/data/.pre-restore-safety.json` shows `-rw-------` owned by `node` | `EACCES`, or the file in `/app` |

**If the server does not start** after the update and `docker logs` says `attempt to write a
readonly database`, `unable to open database file` or `EACCES`, U1 was not made, or an image from
before card 2776 has run on the volume since: make it, and start the container again. Nothing in the data was changed by the failed start.

### The Release That Turns On Two-Step Sign-In (Card 2769)

**Card 2769 (build card B2 of card 2669), with card 2849.** Migrations
`0066_add_mfa_password_enrol.sql`, `0067_end_sessions_for_two_step.sql` and (card 2849)
`0068_end_plain_invite_tokens.sql`, three new pages (`/login/verify`, `/login/enrol`,
`/enrol/[token]`) and one new runtime dependency (`uqr` 0.1.3, see
[SBOM Analysis](sbom-analysis.md)). API v1 does not change. From this release **a right password
no longer signs anyone in**: every account proves an authenticator code or a recovery code, or
sets an authenticator up, before a session exists. How it works is in
[Two-Step Sign-In](authentication-security.md#two-step-sign-in-card-2769).

**Release rules.**

- **Never released without card 2773** (the reset and the host's command, built) **and card
  2849** (invite tokens stored as hashes, built: migration 0068 and the start-up sweep below):
  an invite is now a grant to set up the second factor. See
  [Invite Tokens Stored as Hashes](authentication-security.md#invite-tokens-stored-as-hashes-card-2849).
- **Card 2775** (session codes stored as hashes, limits by role, the `__Host-` cookie) **ships in
  this release.** It has no migration of its own and relies on 0067's sign-out of everybody. See
  [Session Codes Stored as Hashes, and Limits by Role](authentication-security.md#session-codes-stored-as-hashes-and-limits-by-role-card-2775).
- **`MFA_KEY_FILE` in place** (card 2768): see
  [The Key That Protects Authenticator Secrets](#the-key-that-protects-authenticator-secrets).
- **Stop every instance before the release starts**, and never run two images side by side
  across it. An older image still running would sign people in on a password alone.
- **Where mail is set up, the App URL or `ORIGIN` must be the real address** before the release,
  not the image's placeholder `http://localhost:3000`: the release mails links built from it.
- **Rolling back past this card is a security event** (below).

**What people notice.**

- **Everybody is signed out once, and every remembered browser is forgotten** (0067). The first
  sign-in from any browser is a new browser's.
- **Shorter sessions** (card 2775). The once-only sign-out is 0067's, already listed above. From
  the release an administrator is signed out after 12 hours unused and after 24 hours in any
  case, and every other account after 3 days unused and after 7 days in any case, each time
  asked for the password and the authenticator code again. Only a save or a full page load
  counts as use. A tab left open does not keep a session alive, and neither does a click on a
  link inside the app, which fetches data without loading a page. Changing someone's role signs them out. Over HTTPS the cookie is
  `__Host-dumpfire_session`; a browser's old `dumpfire_session` cookie is ignored and deleted at
  its first request.
- **Every invite not yet used is ended** (0068, card 2849). Its link shows the page for a link
  that no longer works. Send again, from User Management (📧), the ones check W15 listed that are
  still wanted. Used invites keep their row with the token replaced. From this release an
  invite's token is kept only as its SHA-256, so the database holds no working link.
- **At their next sign-in nobody has an authenticator yet**, so each account sets one up, by one
  of these, decided at the right password:

| The account | No mail host configured | A mail host configured |
|---|---|---|
| Existed at the release, with no authenticator and no set-up link | Sets up on its password alone, for **14 days** from the release (the accepted risk R1). After that it needs a link | The first right password emails it a set-up link, good for 7 days, and the sign-in page says so. A second sign-in within 24 hours is told when it went; after 24 hours a new link is mailed, and the older one ends once that mail has gone (a failed send keeps it). While a set-up from a mailed link is under way, a sign-in elsewhere is told so and nothing is mailed. The mail names the time and address of the sign-in |
| Reset (🛡️ or the host's command, by this image or an older one) before or after the release | Needs the link the reset gave | The same |
| Made after the release | Needs an invite or a 🛡️ link | The same |
| The superadmin made at a first-run set-up after the release, who left the set-up unfinished | Needs the host's command, which prints a link | The same |

- **A configured mail host that cannot send** (its password not entered on this server, no
  address to make the link from, or the placeholder) answers `503` "could not email" and gives
  no link. It never falls back to setting up on the password. Fix the mail, or give the person
  a 🛡️ link.
- **API keys, webhooks and scripts keep working** through the release. Keys were made on a
  password alone, which is accepted as a non-interactive credential (R2): review them first.
- **Clearing the mail settings within the 14 days reopens setting up on the password** for every
  account still marked: an administrator's decision. A working copy (Import Backup) takes the
  leave from every account.
- **Without the MFA key** an account with an authenticator still reaches the code page, where an
  authenticator code is `503` and a recovery code signs in; an account that would set up is
  `503` at the password. Production refuses to start without the key in any case.
- **The admin page** shows, under each account that may still set up on its password, "may set
  up on password until `<date>` UTC", and nothing while a mail host is set up. See
  [The Release That Turns On Two-Step Sign-In](admin-guide.md#the-release-that-turns-on-two-step-sign-in).
- **A pending sign-in left unfinished** is swept at start-up and every five minutes, and its
  owner mailed (at most once an hour).

#### Before the deploy

`<c>` is the container name. `q` is a read-only query of the database:

```bash
q() { docker exec <c> node -e "const D=require('better-sqlite3');const d=new D('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true});console.log(JSON.stringify(d.prepare(process.argv[1]).all()))" "$1"; }
```

**Check W1: a cold copy.** Take it as in [Taking and Returning the Cold Copy](#taking-and-returning-the-cold-copy).
It is the only way back to sessions and remembered browsers, and going back is a security event.

**Check W2: the address links are made from.** Where mail is set up:
`docker exec <c> printenv APP_URL ORIGIN` and `q "SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key='app_url'"`.
Expect the App URL setting, or else `APP_URL`, or else `ORIGIN`, to be this server's real
address. It is a fault if the first one set is empty or `http://localhost:3000`: every release
sign-in would answer "could not email".

**Check W3: review the API keys.** `q "SELECT u.username, k.name, k.created_at, k.last_used_at, k.expires_at FROM api_keys k JOIN users u ON u.id = k.user_id ORDER BY u.username, k.created_at"`.
Ask each holder about a key they do not recognise: they revoke it on their Account page. An
administrator ends every key of an account by setting its password (🔑). A key nobody recognises
is how someone who had a password stays in after this release.

**Check W4: who may set up on a password.** `q "SELECT username, role FROM users WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM mfa_factors f WHERE f.user_id = users.id) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enrolment_links l WHERE l.user_id = users.id)"`.
These get `mfa_password_enrol = 1` from 0066. Where no mail host is configured, whoever holds one
of their passwords can set up first, for 14 days. **Consider resetting every administrator's
two-step sign-in first**, and any account whose password may be known: 🛡️ for an administrator
(by the superadmin), and `docker exec <c> node scripts/mfa-reset.mjs <username>` for the
superadmin. A reset account needs its link, which you hand over yourself, and is never set up on
its password.

**Check W15: the invites the deploy ends** (card 2849; numbered after the others, and taken
here, before W5 stops the server). 0068 deletes every invite not yet used, so this lists them,
with the account each was for. **Take it before the deploy**: after it, nothing on the server
can list them, and only the cold copy still holds them.

```bash
q "SELECT u.username, u.email, i.created_at, i.expires_at FROM invite_tokens i JOIN users u ON u.id = i.user_id WHERE i.used = 0 ORDER BY i.created_at"
```

One row for each invite not yet used, expired or not, times in UTC. Nothing to rule on: keep the
list. One whose `expires_at` has passed was dead already. Send each one still to come again from
User Management (📧) once the deploy is done.

**Check W5: stop every instance.** `docker ps --filter ancestor=dumpfire` (or your image's name)
lists nothing running before the new image starts. Include staging copies that share the
database.

#### What changes at the first start

- **Three lines from the runner**: `Applied migration: 0066_add_mfa_password_enrol.sql`,
  `Applied migration: 0067_end_sessions_for_two_step.sql` and
  `Applied migration: 0068_end_plain_invite_tokens.sql`. All three are declared to the rehearsal
  (0066 keeps the rows of `users`; 0067 deletes the rows of `sessions` and one of `settings`;
  0068 deletes the unused rows of `invite_tokens` and replaces the used rows' tokens).
- **Every session ends**, and the remembered-browser secret is deleted.
- **No `Ended … session(s) held in plain` line** (card 2775): 0067 has emptied `sessions`, so the
  start-up sweep `endPlainSessions()` that runs before the clean-up finds nothing.
- **Every invite not yet used is deleted**, and every used invite's token is replaced by 32
  random bytes. The start-up sweep that follows the migrations (`endPlainInvites`) finds
  nothing at this start, so it writes no line (neither `Ended … invite(s) held in plain` nor
  `Replaced the token of … used invite(s)`).
- **`two_step_released_at`** is written to `settings`: the 14 days start.

#### After the deploy

| # | Do | Expect | A fault if |
|---|----|--------|------------|
| W6 | `q "SELECT hash FROM __drizzle_migrations WHERE hash LIKE '006%'"`, `q "SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM sessions"`, `q "SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key='two_step_released_at'"` | 0066 and 0067 recorded; `n` 0 straight after the start; the setting is the start's time | Either file missing, a session left from before, or no setting |
| W7 | `q "SELECT username, mfa_password_enrol FROM users"` | 1 for each account W4 listed, 0 for every other | Any other |
| W8 | Sign in yourself | The set-up page (or, with mail set up, the notice that a link was emailed). Finish it: the QR code, the first code, ten recovery codes, "I have saved these codes" | Signed in at once |
| W9 | Audit page, Live Console | `Two-step sign-in set up for "<you>" (user <id>) (<password, link, invite or setup>)` and `User "<you>" logged in`. No code, secret, token or link anywhere | Any secret in a line |
| W10 | `q "SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM sessions WHERE two_step <> 1"` | 0 | Above 0 |
| W11 | Sign out, sign in again | The code page; the current code signs in | No code asked |
| W12 | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <a key>" https://<host>/api/v1/boards` | `200` | `401` |
| W13 | Browser tools on `/login/verify` | `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin`; the challenge cookie `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`, named `__Host-dumpfire_challenge` over HTTPS | Cacheable, or the cookie readable from script |
| W14 | Admin → Users, where no mail host is set up | "may set up on password until `<date>` UTC" under each account W7 shows 1 that has not set up yet, 14 days after W6's time, your own row included. With a mail host set up, no such line | No date, one on an account that has set up, or one while a mail host is set up |
| W16 | `q "SELECT hash FROM __drizzle_migrations WHERE hash LIKE '0068%'"`, `q "SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM invite_tokens WHERE used = 0"` and `q "SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM invite_tokens WHERE typeof(token) <> 'blob' OR length(token) <> 32"`; and the start's log | 0068 recorded; both counts 0 straight after the start; no line from the sweep (`Ended …` or `Replaced the token of …`) | 0068 missing, an unused invite left from before, any token not a 32-byte BLOB, or the sweep's line at the release |
| W17 | Where you hold the link of an invite W15 listed, open it. Then send that account its new invite (📧), as W15 says, and `q "SELECT typeof(token) t, length(token) n FROM invite_tokens WHERE used = 0"` | The old link shows "This invite link no longer works…". The new invite's row is `blob` and 32 | The old link shows the password form, or the new row is not a 32-byte BLOB |
| W19 | After W8, `q "SELECT typeof(id) t, length(id) n, created_at, expires_at FROM sessions"`; and the start's log | Each row `blob`, 32; an administrator's `expires_at` about 12 h after `created_at`, a user's about 3 days; no `[WARN] [AUTH] Ended … session(s) held in plain` line at the release | A text id, an expiry 30 days out, or that line at the release |
| W20 | Browser tools, after signing in over HTTPS | One cookie `__Host-dumpfire_session`: `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`, no `Domain`, expiring 24 h after sign-in for an administrator; no `dumpfire_session` left | No prefix, a `Domain`, or a 30-day expiry |
| W22 | Audit page, Live Console: `Session created for user …` | Its meta has `sessionRef` (8 hex characters) and no `tokenPrefix` | A `tokenPrefix`, or anything longer |

(W21 was folded into W19; the number is not used. W18 is the optional check under
[Going back to the previous image](#going-back-to-the-previous-image).)

**A session an older image made is stored in plain and is never found by this image** (card
2775). At every start `endPlainSessions()` deletes it, before the clean-up of ended sessions,
with one `[WARN] [AUTH] Ended N session(s) held in plain, written by an older image: those
browsers sign in again.` line, and its browser is sent to sign in. At the release itself the
line is not written, since 0067 has emptied the table. The `A hashed session row with
two_step 0 — refused and deleted` `WARN` can still appear, for a hashed row with `two_step` 0,
which no image writes.

#### Going back to the previous image

**Going back past this card is a security event.** The older image signs people in on a password
alone for as long as it runs. Nothing has to be done to the database (for the invites, see below):
the columns and the setting stay,
unread, and its model check reports them at every start (`[ERROR] [DB]`, expected). Authenticators
set up meanwhile stay stored, and the older image ignores them. A reset made on the older image
(🛡️ or the host's command, from card 2773 on) leaves the account's mark at 1 but issues a link,
which this image reads as closing setting up on the password for that account.

**Invites, going back** (card 2849). Nothing has to be done. Every invite this image issued is
stored as its SHA-256 digest, a 32-byte BLOB, and the older image compares the column with the
address text: SQLite never treats a TEXT value as equal to a BLOB, so none of them works there,
and nothing read from the database file makes a working link. Those invites are simply dead on
the older image; send again (📧, on the older image) the ones still wanted. Ending the waiting
invites before the older image starts is still tidy, and optional (check W18 below).

**Check W18 (optional): end the waiting invites before going back.** With every container
stopped, against the file the older image will open:

```bash
docker stop dumpfire
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data -e DB_PATH=/app/data/dumpfire.db \
  dumpfire:rollback node -e "
const db = require('better-sqlite3')(process.env.DB_PATH, { fileMustExist: true });
console.log(db.prepare('DELETE FROM invite_tokens WHERE used = 0').run().changes + ' unused invite(s) deleted');
db.close();
"
```

Change the volume and `DB_PATH` to match the installation, as in
[Taking and Returning the Cold Copy](#taking-and-returning-the-cold-copy).

**A cold copy taken before 0068 is not the same** (where the new image never printed
`Listening on` and the copy is put back). It holds the invites that were waiting when it was
taken, as they were mailed, and the older image started on it makes every one of them work
again. Those are the invites W15 listed. Either send them again as usual, or, if any of their
mails may have gone astray, run W18's command against the returned copy before
`dumpfire:rollback` starts, and send again the ones still wanted.

**Invites, coming forward again.** 0068 is already recorded and is not run again. An invite the
older image issued is stored in plain, as it was mailed. At every start this image runs
`endPlainInvites()` after the migrations: in one transaction it deletes every unused invite not
in hash form (anything but a 32-byte BLOB) and gives every used one not in hash form 32 random
bytes, then writes one `[WARN] [AUTH]` line, built from what changed, when it changed anything:
`Ended N invite(s) held in plain, written by an older image: their links no longer work. Send again, from User Management, the invites still wanted.`
when it ended any, then
`Replaced the token of M used invite(s) held in plain, written by an older image, with 32 random bytes.`
when it replaced any; either part alone when only one applies. Send again (📧) the ones still
wanted. A second start writes nothing. If instead it writes `Invites held in plain by an older image
could not be ended: …`, the server still starts; those invites do not work on this image, and
the same two statements can be run by hand with the server stopped, as W18's command runs its
one:

```sql
DELETE FROM invite_tokens WHERE used = 0 AND NOT (typeof(token) = 'blob' AND length(token) = 32);
UPDATE invite_tokens SET token = randomblob(32) WHERE used <> 0 AND NOT (typeof(token) = 'blob' AND length(token) = 32);
```

**Sessions, going back** (card 2775). Nothing has to be done. Every session this image made is a
32-byte BLOB, which the older image's lookup by the cookie's text never matches, so everyone
signs in again on the older image. That is already part of the security event of going back.
The sessions this image made survive the rollback untouched: the older image cannot read them,
so its sign-outs and role changes do not end them. Rolling forward again inside the idle window
lets a browser that kept its cookie back in, even if the person signed out on the older image.

**Sessions, coming forward.** The older image writes its sessions in plain, and this image never
finds one by hash. `endPlainSessions()` deletes them at the next start, before the clean-up,
with the `Ended N session(s) held in plain` line described above, and those browsers sign in
again. If instead it writes `Sessions held in plain by an older image could not be ended: …`, the
server still starts, those sessions do not sign anyone in on this image (they would on the older
one), and the same statement can be run by hand with the server stopped, with the same
predicate as `SESSION_NOT_IN_HASH_FORM` in `src/lib/server/auth.ts`:

```sql
DELETE FROM sessions WHERE (typeof(id) <> 'blob' OR length(id) <> 32);
```

**Check W23 (going back and coming forward): end every session on the way forward.** If you went
back and are coming forward again, run `DELETE FROM sessions;` with the server stopped, before
this image starts. It ends the sessions this image made before the rollback, which would
otherwise work again inside their idle window, including for a person who signed out on the
older image. Expect everyone to sign in again; a fault if anyone is still signed in.

**Coming forward again**, 0066 and 0067 are already recorded and are not run, so nothing ends
the older image's sessions by migration. This image refuses them instead: each is in plain and
never found, so it is deleted at the next start, and each remembered-browser cookie the older
image signed is under the old MAC domain and not remembered. So everybody it signed in signs in
again with the second step. The 14 days still count from the first release. Treat everything
done while the older image ran as done by whoever held a password: review the Audit page and the
API keys (W3) again.

### The Release That Asks for the Code at Every Step-Up (Cards 2770 and 2771)

**Cards 2770 and 2771 (build cards B3a and B3b of card 2669).** From this release every action
that asks for the current password again (the thirty-two step-up actions of that release,
thirty-seven since card 2772, forty since card 2751, the Account page's email, password and Generate Key forms among
them) asks for a code from the authenticator app,
or a recovery code, beside it, and the server checks both: the action runs only when both are
right. How it works is in
[The Code Beside the Password](authentication-security.md#the-code-beside-the-password-card-2771);
the plan is `docs/planning/card-2771-step-up-requires-code.md`.

**Release rules.**

- **2770 and 2771 ship in the same release.** 2770 alone asks for a code nobody checks; 2771
  alone would refuse every dialog of the old pages.
- **2769 ships with 2773, 2849 and 2775** (above); card 2772 (a second authenticator) goes with
  2770 and 2771 or soon after (see
  [The Release That Gives Older API Keys a Deadline](#the-release-that-gives-older-api-keys-a-deadline-card-2772)).
- **No migration and no setting.** Every column the check uses exists already
  (`sessions.wrong_password_count`, `mfa_factors.last_step` and `last_used_at`,
  `mfa_recovery_codes.used_at`, `users.failed_codes_since_sign_in` and the security banner).
- **`MFA_KEY_FILE` must be set**, as since card 2768. Without it, an authenticator code at a
  step-up is answered `503` "Your authenticator cannot be checked on this server right now. Use
  one of your recovery codes, or ask an administrator. Nothing was changed.", and only recovery
  codes confirm.
- **`/api/v1` and API keys are unchanged.** No v1 route asks for a password, and a key needs no
  code.

**What people notice.**

- **Reload every open DumpFire tab** after the deploy. A page loaded before the release sends no
  `currentCode` (and the old Account page sends `password` to the email and key routes): it is
  answered `400` "Enter your password and a code from your authenticator app to confirm this.
  Nothing was changed.", with nothing changed and nothing counted. Say so in the release notice.
- **A wrong password or a wrong code** is answered "Your password or code was not right. Nothing
  was changed.", never saying which, and either counts toward the three that sign a browser out.
- **A code is spent once it confirms an action**, so two actions in one 30-second step need two
  codes: wait for the next code. A recovery code used at a step-up is spent for good, and its
  owner is mailed with the number left.
- **A right password with a wrong code** raises the account's security banner and mails the
  owner (with mail set up), as a wrong code at sign-in does.

**Scripts.** A script that calls DumpFire's internal routes as a signed-in session (not through
an API key) sends `currentCode` beside `currentPassword`; `PUT /api/account/email` and
`POST /api/account/api-keys` take `currentPassword` in place of `password`. See
[Changes on 2026-11-17](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-11-17).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Deploy["Deploy the image (no migration)"] --> Tab{"A tab opened<br/>before the deploy?"}
    Tab -->|"yes"| Old["Its confirm sends no currentCode:<br/>400 'Enter your password and a code…',<br/>nothing changed, nothing counted"]
    Old --> Reload["Reload the tab"]
    Reload --> New
    Tab -->|"no"| New["The dialog asks for the password and a code"]
    New --> Key{"MFA_KEY_FILE loaded?"}
    Key -->|"no"| Recovery["An authenticator code: 503 factor-unusable;<br/>a recovery code confirms"]
    Key -->|"yes"| Both["Both checked: the action runs<br/>only when both are right"]
```

**Hands-on checks** (on the dev server or a staging copy, signed in as an administrator with an
authenticator set up; the plan's section 6 has the full list, H1 to H16):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Danger Zone, **Reset All XP**: right password, right code | Done; system log `INFO` "Password and code confirmed by…" | Refused; the old `INFO` line |
| R2 | The same at once, with the same code and a wrong password | "That code has just been used…"; the password kept, the code empty and focused; no strike | 403 "not right", or a strike |
| R3 | Right password, a wrong code | "Your password or code was not right…"; both fields empty; `WARN` "Wrong code… the password was right"; the security banner; a mail with SMTP set | The words say which was wrong |
| R4 | **Use a recovery code instead** with a real recovery code | Done; `WARN` "A recovery code confirmed…: 9 left"; a mail "A recovery code was used to confirm a change…" | The mail says "to sign in"; the code works twice |
| R5 | Account page: change email, then password, then **Generate Key**, each with a new code | Each succeeds; both fields cleared after each send | A form sends `password` |
| R6 | A tab opened before the deploy: send a confirm | `400` "Enter your password and a code from your authenticator app…" in the dialog | `500`, or the action done |

**Going back.** An older image ignores `currentCode` and checks the password alone, which is the
state before this release: no data to put right, as nothing was migrated. Codes spent on this
image stay spent in `mfa_factors.last_step` and `mfa_recovery_codes.used_at`, which the older
image honours at sign-in.

### The Release That Gives Older API Keys a Deadline (Card 2772)

**Card 2772 (build card B3c of card 2669), built 2026-11-17.** The Account page gains a
**🛡️ Two-step sign-in** section (up to three authenticators, add and remove, new recovery codes),
the stolen-password warning moves to the top of the Account page where **That was me** clears
it, sign-in and every step-up accept a code from any of the account's authenticators, and
**migration 0069 gives every API key that exists at this release a deadline 60 days later**. A
key not kept by its holder by then, on the Account page with the password and a code, is
answered `401` `Invalid or expired API key` from that moment. This is a breaking change of the
published API by behaviour: no route, field or status changes, but a key that worked stops
working. How it works is in
[Managing Two-Step Sign-In on the Account Page](authentication-security.md#managing-two-step-sign-in-on-the-account-page-card-2772)
and
[Keys Made Before Two-Step Sign-In: the Deadline](authentication-security.md#keys-made-before-two-step-sign-in-the-deadline-card-2772);
the plan is `docs/planning/card-2772-account-two-step.md`.

**Release rules.**

- **Order.** 2769 ships with 2773, 2849 and 2775; 2770 and 2771 ship together; **2772 ships
  with 2770 and 2771 or after them, never before 2771**. In the same deploy as 2769 is fine:
  0069 runs after 0066 to 0068.
- **Before the deploy, tell the key holders (owner).** Run this read-only query on Production
  as close to the deploy as you can, and tell each holder the date (the deploy's day plus 60
  days) and that **My Account → API Keys → Keep this key**, with their password and a code,
  keeps the key unchanged. Without the notice, their integrations stop on that date. A key made
  after the query and before the deploy is not listed: run it again just before.

  ```sql
  SELECT u.username, u.email, k.name, k.key_prefix, k.created_at, k.last_used_at, k.expires_at
  FROM api_keys k JOIN users u ON u.id = k.user_id
  WHERE k.expires_at IS NULL OR k.expires_at > datetime('now', '+60 days')
  ORDER BY u.username, k.created_at;
  ```

  With the container's own reader, as in the 2769 release above: `q "<the query on one line>"`,
  where `q` opens the database read-only. Or `sqlite3 -readonly -header -column <database>` on a
  copy. Every key the query lists has no expiry, or one later than the deadline: those are the
  keys 0069 marks (a key listed whose expiry falls between the query's day and the deploy's,
  plus 60 days, gets no deadline; telling its holder does no harm).
- **The date is fixed when 0069 runs**: `settings.api_key_deadline` = the moment the migration
  runs plus 60 days, written once and never moved. To read it after the deploy:
  `q "SELECT value FROM settings WHERE key = 'api_key_deadline'"`.
- **Deploy.** 0069 runs once at start. No setting, no new environment variable; `MFA_KEY_FILE`
  as since card 2768 (without it, adding an authenticator is refused `503` "Two-step sign-in
  cannot be set up on this server right now. Ask an administrator."). **Reload every open DumpFire tab**: the Account page is
  new, and a confirm dialog of an old page knows nothing of several authenticators.
- **After.** A fortnight before the date, list the keys still not kept and remind their holders:

  ```sql
  SELECT u.username, u.email, k.name, k.key_prefix, k.deadline_at, k.last_used_at
  FROM api_keys k JOIN users u ON u.id = k.user_id
  WHERE k.deadline_at IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY k.deadline_at, u.username;
  ```

  A key past its deadline is never revived, by Keep or anything else: its holder generates a new
  key and puts it where the old one was used.
- **Reset Everything** (`POST /api/admin/reset`) empties `api_keys` and `settings`: no key is
  left to need a deadline, the setting is gone with the rest, and keys made afterwards get none
  (the plan review's S11). A restore of a backup made before 0069 gives that backup's keys this
  server's deadline, and the import's answer says how many (see
  [What a Backup Holds](authentication-security.md#what-a-backup-holds-and-what-a-restore-brings-in)).
- **Rollback is a security event.** An older image keeps the column and the setting, unread:
  it ignores `deadline_at`, so every key past its deadline works again while it runs, and it
  reads one authenticator of an account only, so codes from the others are refused there. Rolling forward
  again refuses those keys once more. Do not go back past this card unless the keys' holders
  are told, or the keys revoked.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q["Owner: run the read-only query on Production,<br/>tell every holder the date and Keep this key"] --> D["Deploy: 0069 runs once"]
    D --> S["settings.api_key_deadline = now + 60 days,<br/>deadline_at set on every key with no expiry<br/>or one later than it"]
    S --> R["Reload every open tab"]
    R --> W["Holders press Keep this key<br/>(password and a code): deadline_at NULL"]
    W --> F["A fortnight before the date:<br/>query deadline_at IS NOT NULL, remind"]
    F --> E{"The date"}
    E -->|"kept"| OK["The key works as before"]
    E -->|"not kept"| End["401 Invalid or expired API key;<br/>never revived: generate a new key"]
    D -.->|"rollback"| Old["Older image: deadlines ignored,<br/>passed keys work again: a security event"]
```

**What people notice.**

- **My Account → API Keys** shows each key's expiry ("Expires *date time* UTC" or "No expiry")
  and, for a key made before this release, "⚠️ Made before two-step sign-in: stops working on
  *date time* UTC unless you keep it" with **Keep this key**; past the date, "Stopped working on
  … Generate a new key."
- **My Account → 🛡️ Two-step sign-in**: the last sign-in, the authenticators (added, last
  used), **Add an authenticator** (a name, the password and a code, then scan the QR code and
  type the new phone's code), **Remove** (never the last; other browsers are signed out), the
  recovery codes left and **Make new recovery codes**. Each sends a mail to the owner.
- **The warning** "⚠️ Was this you?" stays at the top of My Account after a wrong code at
  sign-in until **That was me** (password and a code) or a password change.
- **With two or three authenticators** a wrong code counts once for each: three wrong codes in a
  row (two with three authenticators) pause sign-in, and at a confirmation two wrong answers
  (one with three) sign the browser out. The confirm dialog says so before sending.
- **A lost phone with a recovery code left** needs no administrator: sign in with the recovery
  code, add the new phone, remove the lost one, make new recovery codes, change the password.

**Hands-on checks** (on the dev server or a staging copy, signed in with an authenticator, a
second phone or app at hand, mail set up or the mail log read; the plan's section 6 has the full
list, H1 to H14):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | A database with a key made before 0069, after the deploy | The row says "Made before two-step sign-in: stops working on …"; **Keep this key** with password and code clears it; the key still works with curl | The key's value changed; the flag stays |
| K2 | `UPDATE api_keys SET deadline_at = '2020-01-01 00:00:00' WHERE id = <id>` on the copy, then curl `/api/v1/me` with it | `401` `Invalid or expired API key`; the row reads "Stopped working on … Generate a new key." with no Keep | The key works; Keep offered |
| K3 | Add "Spare phone" (password and code, scan, its code) | Two listed; a mail naming "Spare phone" and its date | A factor written before the code; the secret shown again on reload |
| K4 | Sign out, sign in with the second app's code; then confirm Reset All XP with it | Both accepted; the dialog says "You have 2 authenticators, so each wrong answer here counts twice…" | Refused; no line |
| K5 | Remove the first authenticator from browser A, with browser B signed in | The dialog lists keys and webhooks; B signed out at its next request; A stays; a mail "…was removed…" | B still signed in |
| K6 | **Make new recovery codes** | Ten shown once; closes only on "I have saved these codes"; an old code refused at sign-in | Codes in the page source after reload |
| K7 | A wrong code at sign-in, then My Account | The warning at the top; **That was me** clears it; a new wrong code shows it again | Not shown again within the hour |
| K8 | Import a backup made before 0069 | The answer says "*n* API key(s) from before two-step sign-in were given this server's deadline, …" | No sentence; keys without a deadline |

### The Release That Asks for the Password Before Report Mail (Card 2751)

**Card 2751 (card 2702's F1), built 2026-11-17.** Making a report schedule, a change to one that
adds an address, turns it on or widens its status filter, and a report emailed by hand from the
Reports page now ask for the password and a code (three more step-up actions, forty in all). At
the first start after the release, each owner of a schedule that is on is mailed once, listing
theirs. How it works is in
[Report Schedules and Report Mail](authentication-security.md#report-schedules-and-report-mail-card-2751);
the plan is `docs/planning/card-2751-report-mail-step-up.md`.

**Release rules.**

- **Order.** After card 2772 (it builds on its thirty-seven); in the same deploy is fine.
- **No migration and no setting.** The one-off's flag is a `settings` row written at start,
  `report_schedules_announced`.
- **Set up mail before the deploy** (Admin, 📧 Email / SMTP, with its password entered on this
  server). At the first start, `announceReportSchedules()` writes one `[WARN] [REPORTS]` line for
  each report schedule that is on, naming its owner, what it covers and every address (at `WARN`,
  so that `LOG_LEVEL=WARN` keeps them), then mails each owner "Your DumpFire report schedules":
  each of theirs that is on, what it covers and its addresses, that from this release a change
  that sends to a new address asks for the password and a code, and to delete any they do not
  recognise. The start does not wait for the mail. **With no mail set up nobody is mailed**: one
  `[WARN] [REPORTS]` line names the owners not told, and the flag is written all the same, so
  the `WARN` lines are the only record. Read them on the Audit page and tell each owner
  yourself.
- **Once, and only once every mail went.** The flag is written once the mail server has taken
  every owner's mail; a mail that did not go leaves it unwritten, with one `[WARN] [REPORTS]`
  line naming the owners not told, and the next start says it all again, to every owner. The
  flag makes every later start say nothing. A restore of a backup made before the release
  carries no flag, so the next start announces again. A failure is one `[WARN] [REPORTS]` line,
  and the next start tries again. The server starts whatever happens.
- **Not from a rehearsal or a dev copy.** Where the schedulers do not run (`SCHEDULERS=off`, or
  the dev server without `SCHEDULERS=on`), nobody is mailed and no flag is written: one `[INFO]
  [REPORTS]` line says so, and the first start that runs the schedulers announces.
- **Reload every open Reports tab** after the deploy. An old page sends no password: its
  **Email**, **+ New Schedule** and the switch turning a schedule on are answered `400` "Enter
  your password and a code from your authenticator app to confirm this. Nothing was changed.",
  with nothing saved or sent. Say so in the release notice.
- **Schedules keep running.** The scheduler is unchanged, and a scheduled run asks nothing.
- **`/api/v1`, API keys and the OpenAPI document are unchanged** (still `1.8.0`): no v1 route
  makes or changes a schedule or mails a report. A script that calls the internal routes as a
  signed-in session sends `currentPassword` and `currentCode` (see
  [Changes on 2026-11-17](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-11-17)).

To list the schedules that are on before the deploy (read-only, with the container's own reader
as in the 2769 release above):

```sql
SELECT u.username, u.email, s.id, s.name, s.scope, s.scope_id, s.recipients
FROM report_schedules s JOIN users u ON u.id = s.user_id
WHERE s.enabled = 1
ORDER BY u.username, s.id;
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Mail{"Mail set up, with its<br/>password entered?"} -->|"yes"| D["Deploy, no migration"]
    Mail -->|"no"| Fix["Set it up first, or tell<br/>the owners by hand afterwards"]
    Fix --> D
    D --> Flag{"settings has<br/>report_schedules_announced?"}
    Flag -->|"yes"| Quiet["Nothing said"]
    Flag -->|"no"| Run{"Schedulers run here?"}
    Run -->|"no: SCHEDULERS=off, dev"| Skip["One INFO line, no mail,<br/>no flag"]
    Run -->|"yes"| Info["One WARN line under REPORTS<br/>for each schedule that is on,<br/>its addresses named"]
    Info --> Notice{"Mail set up?"}
    Notice -->|"yes"| Sent["Each owner mailed:<br/>Your DumpFire report schedules"]
    Notice -->|"no"| Warn["One WARN line naming<br/>the owners not told"]
    Sent --> Went{"Every mail went?"}
    Went -->|"yes"| Write["Write the flag"]
    Went -->|"no"| Again["One WARN line naming the owners<br/>not told; no flag, next start again"]
    Warn --> Write
    Skip --> Off["Schedulers stay off"]
    Again --> Sched
    Write --> Sched["Schedulers start: every schedule<br/>runs as before"]
    Quiet --> Sched
```

**What people notice.**

- **Reports → Email** and **+ New Schedule** have a **Your password** box and a code box, with
  "You will be asked for your password and a code from your authenticator app."; both are
  emptied when the dialog or form closes.
- **Switching a schedule on** opens **Turn on this schedule?**, naming every address it will
  email, with a **Turn on** button; switching one off asks nothing. A schedule the server would
  refuse (a time it cannot read, more than 10 addresses) says why and opens nothing.
- **A mail to the owner** each time a schedule of theirs is made, given an address, switched on
  or widened. A report emailed by hand sends none; the system log names the addresses it reached.
- **A report that reached some addresses** keeps the rest in the box and says "Enter your
  password and a new code to send again."

**Hands-on checks** (on the dev server or a staging copy, mail set up or the mail log read,
signed in with an authenticator; the plan's section 6 has the full list, H1 to H15):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | Before deploying, make two schedules (one on, one off) on the old image; deploy and start | One `WARN` line for the one that is on; one mail "Your DumpFire report schedules" listing it alone. Restart: nothing more | No mail; the off one listed; a second mail |
| M2 | Reports, **Email** to an outside address, then to your own address alone | Send stays off until a password and a code are typed; each asks; sent with the right ones; `INFO` "Report … was mailed by … to: …" | Sent without asking |
| M3 | The same with a wrong code | "Your password or code was not right. Nothing was changed." in the dialog; nothing sent | A mail leaves |
| M4 | **+ New Schedule**, no addresses, password and code | Created; a mail "A report schedule was made…" | No mail |
| M5 | Switch a schedule **off**, then **on** | Off at once; on opens "Turn on this schedule?" naming its addresses; a right answer turns it on, with a mail | On without asking |
| M6 | With the session in a REST client: `PUT /api/report-schedules/<id>` adding an address; then `{ "statusFilter": "all" }` on one stored `completed`; then the stored list less one | `400` "Enter your password and a code…" twice; then `200` | `200` for either of the first two |
| M7 | A Reports tab opened before the deploy: **Email** | `400` "Enter your password…" in the dialog; nothing sent | Sent |
| M8 | A schedule made before the deploy, due now | Sent at its time | Not sent |

**Going back.** An older image asks nothing for these routes, which is the state before this
release; nothing was migrated. It keeps the flag unread, and rolling forward again does not
announce again: schedules made or changed on the older image meanwhile are not announced, so
check them with the query above.

### The Release That Keeps Requester Links as Hashes (Card 2870)

**Card 2870 (card 2849's F2), built 2026-11-17.** A requester without an account reaches their
request through a link mailed to them. Until this release the server kept each request's token
in plain (`task_requests.access_token`), so whoever could read the database file could read
every request thread and post into it as the requester. From this release **every mail that
carries a link gets a new link of its own, and only the SHA-256 of its token is kept**, in the new
table `request_links`; a request keeps its newest 20 links from mails and its newest 3 asked-for
links. **Migration `0070_add_request_links.sql` ends every link mailed before the deploy,
once.** How it works is in
[Requester Links Stored as Hashes](authentication-security.md#requester-links-stored-as-hashes-card-2870);
the plan is `docs/planning/card-2870-requester-link-hashes.md`.

**Release rules.**

- **Order.** After card 2751, whose `announceReportSchedules()` it starts after; in the same
  deploy is fine. Not tied to the release of two-step sign-in.
- **Set up mail before the deploy**, with its password entered on this server (Admin, 📧 Email /
  SMTP). A requester whose link stopped working is mailed a new one only when mail works; with
  the mail settings naming a user and holding no password (as a restore leaves them), the
  new-link page and, new in this release, the public form for a request that must be confirmed
  answer `503` "New links cannot be sent just now. Please contact the team that sent you the
  link.", with why in a `[WARN] [REQUESTS]` line.
- **No setting, no new environment variable**, and `/api/v1`, API keys and the OpenAPI document
  are unchanged: no published route reads a request.
- **Nobody needs telling in advance.** Each requester gets a new link by asking for one on the
  page their old link opens, or with the next team reply or progress mail.

To count, before the deploy, the requests whose links will stop working (read-only, with the
container's own reader as in the 2769 release above):

```sql
SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM task_requests WHERE access_token IS NOT NULL GROUP BY status;
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Mail{"Mail set up, with its<br/>password entered?"} -->|"yes"| D["Deploy"]
    Mail -->|"no"| Fix["Set it up first: nobody can<br/>be mailed a new link without it"]
    Fix --> D
    D --> M["First start: 0070 applied,<br/>request_links made, every access_token NULL"]
    M --> Sweep{"endPlainRequestLinks:<br/>any access_token not NULL?"}
    Sweep -->|"no, as at the release"| Quiet["Nothing said"]
    Sweep -->|"yes: an older image has run"| Warn["Every access_token NULL,<br/>every request_links row deleted,<br/>one WARN under REQUESTS"]
    Quiet --> Use["Each mail to a requester<br/>carries a new link"]
    Warn --> Use
    Use -.->|"going back, no step"| Old["Older image: reports request_links<br/>as unknown, leaves it, fills access_token"]
    Old -.->|"coming forward"| Sweep
    Sweep -->|"the sweep fails"| Fallback{"Every request_links<br/>row deleted on its own?"}
    Fallback -->|"yes"| Warned["One WARN under REQUESTS,<br/>the server starts"]
    Fallback -->|"no"| Stop["The server does not start"]
    Warned --> Use
```

#### What changes at the first start

- `[WARN] [DB] Applied migration: 0070_add_request_links.sql`. It makes `request_links` and its
  two indexes, and sets every `task_requests.access_token` to NULL. Requests and their messages
  are untouched.
- No "Ended the links of" line: `endPlainRequestLinks()`, which runs after `endPlainInvites()`
  and before `announceReportSchedules()` at every start, finds nothing at the release.
- The start's backfill no longer fills `access_token`: its `WARN` reads `Backfilled
  first_completed_at on <n> card(s)` alone, and a restore's "Filled in" no longer names
  `access_token`.
- **In the rehearsal**, `Migration files applied` lists `0070_add_request_links.sql`, and, for an
  export that holds requests, a note under `Worth knowing`: `task_requests: every access_token
  ended in its N row(s) by 0070_add_request_links.sql, a one-off declared in
  tests/rehearsal/one-offs.ts`. A rehearsal that applies 0055 too names 0055 in the note.

#### After the deploy

Both read-only, with the container's own reader:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM task_requests WHERE access_token IS NOT NULL;
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM request_links;
```

Each gives 0 right after the deploy. The second grows by one with each mail that carries a link,
and each new link asked for. `npm run schema:expected -- --check` passes in the source tree.

**What people notice.**

- **Every requester link mailed before the deploy stops working, once**: the confirmation, the
  team's replies and the progress mails, open, settled or unconfirmed. The page it opens says
  "This link no longer works…" and asks for the address the request was made with; a new link is
  mailed there. The next team reply or progress mail brings a new link by itself.
- **On a busy server some requesters wait**: at most 30 new-link mails go out in an hour across
  the server (and three an hour to one address), so after the release, as after a restore, some
  are answered the usual sentence with no mail until the hour turns. The next reply or progress
  mail brings a link anyway.
- **Each mail to a requester carries a link of its own**, and the earlier ones keep working: a
  requester with the conversation open is not cut off when the team answers. The 21st mail ends
  the oldest mail link; an asked-for link is one of at most three, and asking never ends a link a
  mail carried.
- **The new-link mail** reads "Use the button below to open it." where it said "from now on".
- **A team reply with the mail password missing** is saved and mails nothing, as every mail would
  fail; enter the password in Admin, 📧 Email / SMTP.
- **Every Import Backup ends every request's links**, as before: a backup holds no link, and
  the import's answer says how many requests' links were ended ("N request link(s) replaced…").

**Hands-on checks** (on a scratch copy of a database made by the image before this one, never a
live file; mail set up with a local mail catcher and an App URL; the plan's section 6 has the
full list, H1 to H13):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Start this image | `Applied migration: 0070_add_request_links.sql`, and no "Ended the links of" line | No such line, or a start failure |
| L2 | The two queries above | 0 and 0 | Any value |
| L3 | Open a link the old image mailed, give the request's address | "This link no longer works…", then the `202` sentence and a mail whose button opens the thread; one `request_links` row, `ask`, holding a 64-hex value that is not the token | No mail, a dead link, or the token in the table |
| L4 | With the thread open in one tab, reply as the team | The tab shows the reply at the next poll and stays open; a second mail with a different link; both links open the thread | The open tab drops to the dead-link form |
| L5 | Accept the request onto a board and comment on its card | A progress mail whose link opens the thread | No mail, or a dead link |
| L6 | Admin, Backup, Export; search the file for a mailed token | Not found, and no `request_links` rows | Found, or rows |

#### Going back to the previous image

**No step is needed, but do not drop `request_links`.** Start the previous image on the database
as it is ([Going Back to the Previous Image](#going-back-to-the-previous-image)).

- The older image's start-up schema check reports `request_links` as a table it does not know.
  That is expected; it leaves the table.
- Links this image mailed do not work there: the older image looks for the token in
  `task_requests.access_token`, and its backfill gives every request a new plain token nobody
  holds. Requesters ask for a new one from the page the link opens, and the older image mails
  one that works on it.
- The plain tokens the older image writes stay in the file until the next start of this image,
  and open nothing on this image.
- 0070 stays recorded: the older image logs one `[ERROR] [DB]` line for the recorded files it has
  no file for, and starts.

**Coming forward again**, `endPlainRequestLinks()` finds the plain tokens, sets them to NULL and
deletes every `request_links` row, in one transaction, with one line:
`[WARN] [REQUESTS] Ended the links of N request(s) held in plain by an older image, and M link(s)
kept as hashes: no request link mailed before this start works. Each requester can have a new one
sent from the page a link opens.` Every link mailed before, by either image, is ended once, and
requesters ask again (the 30-an-hour limit above applies). While the older image ran,
`request_links` was outside its rules, and its restore or reset may have replaced the requests
and left the table as it was, so a kept link could have opened somebody else's thread: that is
why every link is ended. A restart after that writes no such line.

If that sweep fails, for any reason, every `request_links` row is deleted on its own and one line
says so, `[WARN] [REQUESTS] Request links held in plain by an older image could not be looked
for: … Every link kept as a hash was ended instead (N): …`, and the server starts; requesters ask
for new links. If that delete fails too, the server **does not start**: it stops before it
listens, as it does when the form's signing key cannot be made, rather than run with links that
may open other people's threads (card 2870's code review, CS3). Fix the database (it is the
same cause that stops every other write) and start again.

### The Release That Checks the Card Window's Images (Card 2761)

**Card 2761 (card 2754's D20 and code review C3), built 2026-11-17.** Until this release an
image dropped onto a card was stored as the browser sent it: its type as claimed, its hidden
data kept, and no limit a card or a person. From this release **an image uploaded through the
card window goes through the same checks as one sent through an API key**, and **the images
already stored are checked once, at the first start**. How it works is in
[The Card Window's Images](authentication-security.md#the-card-windows-images-card-2761); the
plan is `docs/planning/card-2761-web-upload-checks.md`.

**What people notice.**

- A file named and typed as an image that is not one (a page renamed `.png`) is refused, with
  the reason under the upload area. So are an animated GIF, PNG or WebP, a PNG, GIF or WebP
  with anything stuck on after the end of the picture, and one over 8000 pixels on a side or
  40 megapixels.
- A phone photo loses its location, camera make and model and other hidden data, and keeps its
  "which way up" tag, so it still shows upright. What a phone stores after the end of a JPEG
  photo (a motion photo's video, an HDR gain map, a trailer) is cut off, and the photo is
  attached. Its shown name takes the extension of what the file really is (`photo.PNG` is
  `photo.png`).
- The 21st image on a card is refused ("This card already has 20 images"); an image for a card
  closed longer than `IMAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` is refused, as through a key.
- Each person has 30 image uploads an hour and 100 MB of images a day, **shared with their API
  keys**: a script uploading through the wrapper's `add-attachment` and the same person's card
  window count together, and a key can meet the `429` sooner than before.
- **Images already attached that are animated or too large become downloads**, kept as they
  were, metadata included: the one-off check below refuses them, as it refuses one that is not
  the image its type names or is malformed, and changes each to a plain download, never shown
  in the browser again. Nothing of such a file is rewritten.
- PDFs, documents, spreadsheets and every other file are attached as before (until card 2910,
  which counts every file: see [its release](#the-release-that-counts-every-upload-card-2910)).

**Release rules.**

- **Nothing to migrate**, no setting, no new environment variable. The OpenAPI document goes to
  `1.9.1`, a patch: no `/api/v1` operation, status or field changes (its dated note lists what a
  key sees differently).
- **The one-off check runs at every start until it has finished once**, whatever `SCHEDULERS`
  says, a rehearsal or a dev copy included, and again straight after every Import Backup (the
  restore replaces the setting that says it was done): it rewrites stored image files in place.
  Back up the uploads folder with the database before the first start of this image if a copy
  of the originals is wanted; the check keeps no copy. Each file is written to a temp file
  (`.recheck-<uuid>`) in its card's folder, flushed to the disk, and renamed over the original.
- **Order.** After card 2751 and card 2870 (it starts after `announceReportSchedules()`), in the
  same deploy or later. Cards 2719 and 2762 build after it.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    D["Deploy, first start, or an Import Backup"] --> F{"settings.stored_images_rechecked?"}
    F -->|"present"| Q["Nothing done, nothing said"]
    F -->|"absent"| R["Every image row, oldest first: checkImage on its file"]
    R --> S["clean: untouched, its size set if wrong; stripped: rewritten in place, size set;<br/>retyped: application/octet-stream, file untouched; missing: untouched"]
    S --> W["One WARN line under UPLOADS with the counts and ids"]
    W --> N{"Any row failed, and not yet<br/>three starts the same way?"}
    N -->|"no"| Flag["Flag written: later starts do nothing"]
    N -->|"yes"| Again["No flag: the next start checks again"]
```

#### What the first start says (card 2761)

One line on the Audit page's Live Console, when there is an image attachment at all:
`[WARN] [UPLOADS] Checked the n images stored before card 2761: s had hidden data taken out,
z had only their recorded size corrected, r were refused by the check (not the image its type
names, animated, too large, or malformed) and are now downloads only (attachment ids …), m had
no file, f could not be checked (attachment ids …), g were given up after failing the same way
at 3 starts (attachment ids …).` The ids are the attachments' (their card and name are not
logged). A row refused by the check is kept as it was, metadata included, is never shown in the
browser again, and no longer counts toward a card's 20. "had no file" counts rows whose file is
not in the uploads folder (a restore without the files): nothing is done to them. With `f`
above 0 the line ends "The next start checks them again.", and so it does; anything already
cleaned checks to itself and is left. A restart after a clean run writes no line. An import of
a backup made before this release carries no flag, so its images are checked straight after the
import.

**When `f` stays above 0.** Each failed row is named by id, and its failure (its error code) is
kept in `settings.stored_images_recheck_failures` between starts. A row that fails the same way
at three starts in a row is given up: counted under `g`, named, and no longer keeping the check
from finishing, so the flag is then written and later starts say nothing. For a row named under
`f` or `g`:

1. Find its file, read-only, with the container's own reader as in the 2769 release above:
   `SELECT card_id, filename FROM card_attachments WHERE id = <id>;` names
   `uploads/<card_id>/<filename>`.
2. Fix what the code names: `EACCES` or `EPERM`, the server cannot write the card's folder
   (the volume's ownership); `ENOSPC`, the disk is full; `EIO`, the disk or the volume is
   failing. A `.recheck-<uuid>` file left in the folder is a temp file and may be deleted.
3. Restart. A row given up is not tried again once the flag is written: delete the attachment
   from its card, or download it and attach it again through the card window, which checks it
   as an upload.

**Hands-on checks** (on a copy of production's database and uploads folder, never the live
files; the plan's section 6 has the full list, H1 to H9):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| U1 | Start this image | One `Checked the … images stored before card 2761` line; restart: no line | No line, or a second one |
| U2 | Drop a PNG screenshot on a card | Attached, thumbnail shown | Refused |
| U3 | Rename a `.html` file to `.png` and drop it | Refused: "The body is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image" | Attached |
| U4 | Drop an upright phone photo with location on, then download it | Shown upright; the download has Orientation alone in any EXIF viewer | Sideways, or location kept |
| U5 | Drop a motion photo or an Ultra HDR photo from a phone | Attached; the download is the still photo alone, smaller than the original | Refused, or the video kept |
| U6 | Admin → ISO 27001 checklist, A.8.7 | Met, no gap card | 2761 still listed |

#### Going back to the previous image

No step is needed. The previous image reads the rows and files as this one left them: a cleaned
image is still an image, and a row retyped `application/octet-stream` is a download there too.
The flag stays; coming forward again does not re-check.

### The Release That Answers What a Caller Cannot Open as Not There (Card 2719)

**Card 2719, built 2026-11-18.** Until this release a board or card that existed on a board the
caller could not open was answered `403`, and one that did not exist `404`, so anyone with an
account or an API key could learn which boards and cards exist on boards they will never see.
From this release **a board, a card, a dashboard grouping holding only boards the caller cannot
open, or anything on a board they cannot open is answered `404`, in the very words one that is
not there gets**, by every route and page; `403` is kept for a caller who can open the board and
whose role does not allow the act. How it works is in
[Not Found, Not Forbidden](authentication-security.md#not-found-not-forbidden-card-2719); the
plan is `docs/planning/card-2719-not-found-not-forbidden.md`.

**This is a breaking change for API keys** (OpenAPI document `1.10.0`, a dated note marked
breaking at the top of its description): a script that read `403` as "no access" is answered
`404` instead. The changelog entry is in [the API reference](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-11-18).

**Nothing to migrate.** No schema, setting or file changes. Going back to the previous image
needs no step; it answers `403` again.

**Before the release, tell the key holders (owner).** No Production access is used here: the
owner finds the holders of API keys with a read-only query of Production's database, as card
2772's release does (see [The Release That Gives Older API Keys a Deadline](#the-release-that-gives-older-api-keys-a-deadline-card-2772),
or check W3's), every key that still works, with its holder's address:

```sql
SELECT u.username, u.email, k.name, k.key_prefix, k.last_used_at, k.expires_at
FROM api_keys k JOIN users u ON u.id = k.user_id
WHERE k.expires_at IS NULL OR k.expires_at > datetime('now')
ORDER BY u.username, k.created_at;
```

and sends each holder a notice. Cards 2719, 2762 and 2911 go out in one release, so the notice
is card 2911's, which covers all three and replaces the one written here: see
[The Release That Answers a Milestone the Caller Cannot See as Not There](#the-release-that-answers-a-milestone-the-caller-cannot-see-as-not-there-card-2911).

**What people notice.** Someone who loses access to a board and follows an old link sees
"Board not found" where they saw "You do not have access to this board". The board page's
refresh and its live stream treat the two alike, as before.

**Accepted risk.** A missing id is answered a little faster than one on a board the caller
cannot open (R5 in [Accepted Risks](authentication-security.md#accepted-risks)), bounded by
the gate's 60 requests a minute.

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6, H1 to H9; on the dev server, two accounts: A owns
board X, B has no access to X, and a key for B):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | As B, open `/board/<X>` | "Board not found" error page | "You do not have access" |
| H2 | As B, open `/board/<X + 99999>` | The same page, the same words | Any difference |
| H3 | With B's key: `GET /api/v1/cards/<a card of X>` and `/999999` | Both `404 {"message":"Card not found"}` | A 403, or different words |
| H4 | With B's key: `GET /api/v1/webhooks/<a webhook of X>` and `/999999` | Both `404 Webhook not found` | `Board not found` for the first |
| H5 | Share X with B as viewer; `PUT /api/v1/cards/<card of X>` `{ "title": "x" }` | `403 No edit access to this card's board` | 404 |
| H6 | Unshare; with B's key `POST /api/v1/dependencies/bulk` with a link from B's card to a card of X, and the same with `999999` | Both 409 with `does not exist or is archived` for that end | "No edit access", or a duplicate or cycle |
| H7 | As B, the burndown page with `?boardIds=<X>` | "Not found" | "No access" |
| H8 | `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` | `info.version` `1.10.0`; the note first, "breaking" | 1.9.x |
| H9 | Admin → ISO 27001 checklist, A.8.3 | Gap cards 2730 and 2917 (card 2762 ships in the same release); accepted risk R5 | 2719 or 2762 still listed |

### The Release That Switches Off a Webhook Whose Setter Loses the Board (Card 2752)

**Card 2752, built 2026-11-18.** Since card 2325 a webhook sent nothing while the account that
set it up could not open its board, but it stayed on, and the next event after that account
could open the board again was sent: sharing the board back, putting the account back in a team,
making the board public or giving an administrator their role back restarted it, with no
password asked and nobody told. From this release **such a webhook is switched off for good**
(`active` false, with why and when in `held_because` and `held_at`) at the change that takes the
access away, at every start, after every restore and at its next event, and **stays off** until
the board's owner or an administrator switches it on with an API key, which gives it a new
secret. How it works is in
[A Webhook Switched Off When Its Setter Loses the Board](authentication-security.md#a-webhook-switched-off-when-its-setter-loses-the-board-card-2752);
the plan is `docs/planning/card-2752-held-webhook-stays-off.md`.

**This is a breaking change for API keys** (OpenAPI document `1.11.0`, a dated note marked
breaking at the top of its description): an integration whose setter leaves a board and rejoins
it stops until it is switched on again, and switching it on answers a new `secret` that the
receiver must be given. The changelog entry is in
[the API reference](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-11-18).

**Migration 0071** adds `webhooks.held_because`, `held_at`, `set_by_key` and `set_with_key`, the
index `idx_webhooks_set_by_key`, and the setting `webhook_keys_recorded_at`, the moment it ran
(see [Data Model](data-model.md#a-webhook-switched-off-for-good-migration-0071)). It changes no
webhook. The last two columns and the setting are card 2893's, which ships in the same release:
see [The Release That Switches Off a Webhook Whose API Key Ends](#the-release-that-switches-off-a-webhook-whose-api-key-ends-card-2893).

**At the first start after the deploy** every webhook that is on and whose setter cannot open its
board, and every one nobody is recorded as having set up (made before 2026-10-18/19, or whose
setter was deleted), is switched off, after the settings of non-administrators are removed and
before the schedulers start (`switchOffHeldWebhooksAtStart`). Each writes one
`[WARN] [Webhooks]` line, `Webhook <id> on board <board> switched off: … (found when the server
started). It stays off until an owner of the board or an administrator switches it on.`, never
