the address. Where the schedulers run (`SCHEDULERS`, the same decision as `startSchedulers`),
each board's owners are mailed once, naming the board, each webhook's id and host, and why;
elsewhere one more `WARN` says the owners were not mailed, so a dev server or a rehearsal mails
nobody. A second start changes nothing.

**Before the release, see what the first start will switch off (owner).** A read-only query of
Production's database; neither changes anything:

```sql
-- On, with no recorded setter, or a setter that names no account (the code review's CR6):
-- each is switched off at the first start.
SELECT w.id, w.board_id, b.name AS board
FROM webhooks w JOIN boards b ON b.id = w.board_id
WHERE w.active = 1
  AND (w.set_by IS NULL OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM users u WHERE u.id = w.set_by))
ORDER BY w.board_id, w.id;

-- On, with a setter who is no administrator, did not make the board, is not on its member
-- list, is in no team it is shared with, on a board that is not public: each is switched off too.
SELECT w.id, w.board_id, b.name AS board, u.username AS setter
FROM webhooks w JOIN boards b ON b.id = w.board_id JOIN users u ON u.id = w.set_by
WHERE w.active = 1
  AND u.role NOT IN ('admin', 'superadmin')
  AND (b.created_by IS NULL OR b.created_by <> u.id)
  AND b.is_public = 0
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM board_members m WHERE m.board_id = b.id AND m.user_id = u.id)
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM board_teams bt JOIN team_members tm ON tm.team_id = bt.team_id
                  WHERE bt.board_id = b.id AND tm.user_id = u.id)
ORDER BY w.board_id, w.id;
```

Tell each board's owner what will stop and why, so the mail at the first start is expected:
each such webhook was already sending nothing since card 2325.

**Card 2893's keys, in the same release.** A webhook whose API key ended is switched off for
good too, and a webhook set before this release, which records no key, is judged by whether its
setter still has a working key made before `webhook_keys_recorded_at`. The query for them, the
one-time mail with the earliest date each will stop, and how to keep one are in the next section.

**A restore sweeps too.** An import first reads this server's webhooks switched off for good,
whatever their secret, and carries each hold onto the restored row of the same webhook (same id,
board, address and setter), even where the backup had it on and its setter can open the board
there (the code review's CS5). Then, restored as it is (`outside=keep`), it switches off, inside
its transaction, every restored webhook that is on and whose setter cannot open its board in the
restored data; a backup made before 0071 holds no hold columns, so its webhooks come in on and
are swept. A webhook held off here is not switched back on by the backup's secret being filled
in. Each is a `WARN` line naming who restored, and the owners are mailed where the schedulers
run. A working copy (`outside=off`) switches every webhook off as before, and mails nobody. Of
`webhook_keys_recorded_at` the earlier of this server's and the backup's is kept (card 2893's
code review, CS1).

**What people notice.** Board owners are mailed when a webhook on their board is switched off,
naming what caused it ("Sam was taken off the board by Ann"), and whenever someone who is not an
owner or an administrator makes a webhook on their board. The Share Board window says "switched
off … It stays off, even if they are given the board back" in place of "held until they can
open the board again". Someone who is not the board's owner or an administrator cannot make a
webhook to a receiver (scheme, host and port) switched off on that board (`409`), nor delete one
switched off (`403`). A password reset, an invite used or an account deleted now records why it
switched a webhook off (`setter access ended`), so switching such a webhook on gives it a new
secret too (the code review's CS1, CS2, CS4); since card 2671 a disabled account, and since card
2915 a reset of the two-step sign-in, record the same. A team manager who takes a member out
of a team switches off that member's webhooks on the boards they lose.

**Going back** to the previous image needs no step. It does not read the four columns, and its
schema check reports them, the key and the index as ones it does not know and leaves them. A
webhook switched off here stays off there until an owner switches it on; one switched on there
is not held off again until it is judged here. Coming forward again, 0071 is already recorded.

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6; on the dev server with `SCHEDULERS=on` and mail
configured: an owner with a key, an editor E with a key, a team T holding E, a member-row owner
O2, and a receiver allowed by `WEBHOOK_ALLOW_INSIDE` or a public one):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | E makes a webhook with E's key, to a receiver that no webhook switched off on the board holds | Made; the owner and O2 each get "A webhook was made on <board>" | No mail, or refused |
| D2 | The owner takes E off in Share Board | The confirm says "switches off … It stays off"; one mail each to the owner and O2 naming "E was taken off the board by <owner>"; one `WARN` | No mail, or the old words |
| D3 | Share the board with E again; move a card | Nothing delivered; `GET` with the owner's key: `active: false`, "This was switched off because …" | Anything delivered |
| D4 | E tries `POST /api/v1/boards/{id}/webhooks` with the same address, then with another path on the same host, and the host in capitals; then `DELETE` of the switched-off webhook | Each `409` "A webhook to this receiver (the same scheme, host and port) on this board was switched off. …"; the delete `403` | Created, or deleted |
| D5 | The owner `PUT {"active": true}` | On; the answer's `secret` is new; deliveries signed with it | The old secret, or still off |
| D6 | Repeat D2-D3 with T's share removed, E taken out of T by T's manager, T deleted, and the board made private then public | Each: off at the change, the cause named, off after access returns | Any resumes |
| D7 | Back up (E still on the board), take E off (switched off), restore the older backup with `keep`, move a card | Off after the restore with its hold kept, though E can open the board in the backup; nothing delivered | On again, or delivered |
| D10 | Reset E's password as an administrator; then the owner `PUT {"active": true}` on one of E's webhooks | Off with "This was switched off because the account that set it up had its password or its two-step sign-in reset …" (the words since card 2915); the switch-on answers a new `secret` | The old secret |
| D8 | `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` | `info.version` `1.11.0`; its note first, "breaking" | 1.10.x |
| D9 | Admin → ISO 27001 checklist, A.5.14 and A.5.18 | 2752 and 2893 no longer listed (they ship together); A.5.14 met; A.5.18 gap card 2671 on an image without card 2671 (and 2894 on one without card 2894), met with none from card 2671's release | 2752 or 2893 still listed |

### The Release That Switches Off a Webhook Whose API Key Ends (Card 2893)

**Card 2893, built 2026-11-18, shipped with card 2752.** Webhooks are made and changed only with
an API key, and until this release a webhook went on sending after that key had expired, passed
its deadline (card 2772's, for keys made before two-step sign-in), been deleted or been revoked.
From this release each webhook records the key that created it, last set its address or secret,
or switched it on (`set_by_key`, `set_with_key`, migration 0071), and **is switched off for
good, `'key ended'`, when that key ends**: at the revoke on the Account page (in the same
change), or at the next start, restore or event after it expires or passes its deadline. It is
card 2752's switched-off state: the board's owners are mailed, the log says so, and only the
board's owner or an administrator switches it on again, with a key of their own, which gives it a
new secret. The account that set it up is mailed too, while it can still open the board. How it
works is in
[A Webhook Switched Off When Its API Key Ends](authentication-security.md#a-webhook-switched-off-when-its-api-key-ends-card-2893);
the plan is `docs/planning/card-2893-webhook-key-ended.md`. No migration of its own; it adds
items (9) and (10) to the OpenAPI `1.11.0` note.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Start as First start after the deploy
    participant Ann as announceWebhooksBeforeKeys
    participant Sweep as switchOffHeldWebhooksAtStart
    participant Owners as Boards' owners
    Start->>Ann: after announceReportSchedules (schedulers on)
    Ann->>Ann: one WARN per webhook from before the release still sent
    Ann->>Owners: one mail each, every webhook with the earliest date it stops
    Ann->>Ann: webhooks_before_keys_announced, once every mail went
    Start->>Sweep: before the schedulers
    Sweep->>Owners: those already held (no working key from before): switched off, mailed
```

**Webhooks made before this release.** They record no key (`set_with_key` NULL). Each keeps
sending while the account that set it up holds a working API key made before the release
(before `webhook_keys_recorded_at`, the moment 0071 ran), and is switched off once it has none:
for most, at card 2772's 60-day deadline for keys made before two-step sign-in, unless the key was
kept. A key made after the release does not count: it cannot have set the webhook. One whose
setter has no such key at the deploy is switched off at the first start, with card 2752's mail.

**The one-time announcement at the first start.** Where the schedulers run, the first start
writes one `[WARN] [Webhooks]` line for each such webhook still sent, `Webhook <id> on board
<board> was set up before API keys were recorded (user <id>): it stops at the earliest <date>
UTC; later if that account keeps or replaces a key from before the release. …` (or "on no set
date", where one of that account's keys has neither an expiry nor a deadline), never the
address, and mails each board's owners once ("A webhook on your board will stop when its key
ends"), listing board, id, host and the earliest date, with how to keep it. The date is the
latest end among that account's working keys from before the release, each key's end the earlier
of its expiry and its deadline; it is "at the earliest" because keeping a key (Keep this key)
moves it later (the code review's CS2). Then it writes the setting `webhooks_before_keys_announced`, but only
once every mail went: a mail that did not go leaves it unwritten, and the next start says it all
again. With no mail set up the lines are written, one more `WARN` says the owners were not told,
and the setting is written. Where the schedulers are off (`SCHEDULERS=off`, or the dev server)
the lines are written, one `WARN` says nobody was mailed, and no setting: the first start that
runs the schedulers mails them. A restore brings in the backup's settings: a backup that does
not hold `webhooks_before_keys_announced` (one made before the release, or before that start's
mail went) is announced again at the next start. Of `webhook_keys_recorded_at` a restore keeps
the earlier of this server's and the backup's (the code review's CS1), the backup's where this
server has none, so no key made after the release on either server counts as one from before
it.

**To keep one, re-save it with a key.** The board's owner or an administrator sends `PUT
/api/v1/webhooks/{id}` with `{"active": false}`, then with `{"active": true}`, using their own
key: that makes them its setter and binds it to that key, and the secret is kept. From then it
stops when that key ends.

**Before the upgrade, see which webhooks and keys this concerns (owner).** Read-only queries of
Production's database:

```sql
SELECT w.id, w.board_id, b.name AS board, w.set_by, u.username
FROM webhooks w JOIN boards b ON b.id = w.board_id LEFT JOIN users u ON u.id = w.set_by
WHERE w.active = 1 ORDER BY w.board_id, w.id;
SELECT k.user_id, k.name, k.created_at, k.expires_at, k.deadline_at
FROM api_keys k WHERE k.user_id IN (SELECT set_by FROM webhooks WHERE active = 1);
```

A setter with no key in the second list, or only keys whose expiry or deadline has passed, loses
those webhooks at the first start; otherwise the latest end of their keys is the date the mail
will give.

**Rotating a key now switches its webhooks off** (decision 12). Revoking a key on the Account page
switches off, in the same change, every webhook it set up, and, where it is the account's last
working key from before the release, the account's webhooks from then too: the key's row shows
how many first ("Revoking it switches off 2 webhooks"), the confirm says "Revoke? It switches off
2 webhooks.", and afterwards "Key revoked. 2 webhooks were switched off." (the code review's
CS4). The answer of `DELETE /api/account/api-keys/{id}` carries `webhooksSwitchedOff`; the log
line names the key by its id, never its name ("API key #12 was revoked by Sam"). So to rotate the
key an integration's webhooks were set with (the code review's CR6):

1. **Preferred, nothing stops and the secret is kept.** Make the new key. Then the board's owner
   or an administrator re-saves each webhook with their new key, `PUT {"active": false}` then
   `PUT {"active": true}`, which binds it to that key; only then revoke the old key, whose row
   now counts 0.
2. **Otherwise.** Revoke the old key first: its webhooks are switched off. The board's owner or an
   administrator then switches each on with their key (`PUT {"active": true}`), which gives it a
   **new secret** in that answer, to give the receiver.

A key that simply expires, or passes its deadline, switches its webhooks off the same way at the
next start, restore or event. A webhook written with a session, never with a key, is switched
off at its next event.

**This is a breaking change for API keys** (OpenAPI `1.11.0`, items (9) and (10) of its dated
note; [the API reference](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-11-18)).

**Going back** to an image before cards 2752 and 2893 needs no step: it does not read
`set_by_key`, `set_with_key` or the setting `webhooks_before_keys_announced`, and leaves them. On
that image a webhook whose key ended goes on sending; one already switched off here stays off
(`active` 0) until an owner switches it on. Coming forward again, a webhook switched on there
records no key from that switch-on, and is judged by the key it last recorded; a webhook created
on the older image records `set_with_key` NULL, so it is judged by the before-the-release rule (it
stops once its setter has no working key made before `webhook_keys_recorded_at`), and re-saving
it with a key (`{"active": false}`, then `{"active": true}`) binds it to that key (the code
review's CR8).

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6; on the dev server with `SCHEDULERS=on` and mail
configured, an owner and an editor E, each with a key):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | Make key K as E; `create-webhook` with it; move a card | Delivered | Not delivered |
| K2 | On the Account page, ✕ beside K | K's row says "Revoking it switches off 1 webhook"; the confirm: "Revoke? It switches off 1 webhook." | No count |
| K3 | Confirm | "Key revoked. 1 webhook was switched off."; the owner's mail and E's own ("A webhook you set was switched off"), the cause "API key #<id> was revoked by E", never the key's name; `GET` with the owner's key: off, the key sentence | Still on, or the name in the log |
| K4 | Make key L expiring in a few minutes; `create-webhook`; wait; move a card | Nothing delivered; off | Delivered |
| K5 | The owner, key M: `PUT {"active": true}` | On; a new secret in the answer | Refused, or the old secret |
| K6 | Upgrade a dev copy holding webhooks from before the release, schedulers on | One mail per owner listing them with dates; a second start sends nothing | No mail, or a second one |

### The Release That Answers a Milestone the Caller Cannot See as Not There (Card 2911)

**Card 2911, built 2026-11-18.** Card 2719 left milestones at `403 No access to this milestone`
for one the caller cannot see, beside `404 Milestone not found` for one that is not there, so
anyone with an account or an API key could still try milestone ids and learn which goals exist
among those they cannot see. From this release **a milestone the caller cannot see, named by its
id anywhere (the API, the plan page, the burndown chart, a card's milestone), is answered `404
Milestone not found`, the words one that is not there gets**. That includes a goal across boards
a user made, once it holds a card on a board they cannot open. `403 No edit access to this
milestone` is kept for a goal the caller can see and may not change; putting a card in another
milestone, or taking it out, when the caller cannot see the milestone it is in, is answered `403
No access to the milestone this card is in`. How it works is in
[Not Found, Not Forbidden](authentication-security.md#not-found-not-forbidden-card-2719); the
plan is `docs/planning/card-2911-hidden-milestone-not-found.md`.

**This is a breaking change for API keys** (OpenAPI document `1.12.0`, a dated note marked
breaking at the top of its description): a script that read `403 No access to this milestone`
is answered `404 Milestone not found` instead. The changelog entry is in
[the API reference](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-11-18).

**Nothing to migrate.** No schema, setting or file changes. Going back to the previous image
needs no step; it answers `403 No access to this milestone` again.

**Before the release, tell the key holders (owner).** Cards 2719, 2762 and 2911 go out in one
release, so one notice covers all three and replaces card 2719's (above). Find the holders with
the read-only query in card 2719's section, and send each this notice, as written:

> From the next DumpFire release, a request naming a board, card, milestone, or anything on a
> board that your account cannot open or see is answered `404` with the same message as one
> that does not exist, where it was `403`. `403` now means you can see it but your role does not
> allow the action. In a dependency batch, an end you cannot open is reported as not existing,
> and a loop through work you cannot open names it as withheld. `404 Milestone not found` is
> also the answer for a milestone you cannot see, where it was `403 No access to this
> milestone`. One case keeps a `403`: putting a card in another milestone, or taking it out,
> when you cannot see the milestone the card is in is answered `403 No access to the milestone
> this card is in`. If a script treats `403` as 'no access', treat `404` the same way.

**What people notice.** Someone who follows an old plan link to a goal they can no longer see
gets the "Milestone not found" error page where they got "No access to this milestone"; the
burndown page labels the problem "Not found".

**Accepted risks.** A missing id is answered a little faster than one the caller cannot open, a
milestone now among them (R5), and ids are counted up one at a time, so anyone who can make a
board, a card or a milestone learns how many were made since their last (R6). Both are in
[Accepted Risks](authentication-security.md#accepted-risks), bounded by the gate's rate limits.

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6, H1 to H8; on the dev server: account A owns board X
with a goal Gx; account B owns board Y and has no access to X; a goal Gxy across boards, made by
A, holds a card of X and B's card on Y; a key for B):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | As B, open `/plan/<Gx>`, then `/plan/<Gx + 99999>` | The same "Milestone not found" error page | "No access to this milestone" for the first |
| H2 | With B's key: `GET /api/v1/milestones/<Gx>` and `/999999` | Both `404 {"message":"Milestone not found"}` | A 403, or different words |
| H3 | With B's key: `GET /api/v1/milestones/<Gxy>` | `404 Milestone not found` | 403, or the goal |
| H4 | As B, the burndown page with `?milestoneId=<Gx>`, then `?milestoneId=999999` | "Not found", the same both times | "No access" |
| H5 | Share X with B as viewer; with B's key `PATCH /api/v1/milestones/<Gx>` `{ "name": "x" }` | `403 No edit access to this milestone`, name unchanged | 404 |
| H6 | Unshare; B makes a goal of no board; with B's key `PUT /api/v1/cards/<B's card in Gxy>` `{ "milestoneId": <B's goal> }`, then `{ "milestoneId": null }` | Both `403 No access to the milestone this card is in`, the card still in Gxy | 404, the old words, or the card moved |
| H7 | `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` | `info.version` `1.12.0`; its note first, "breaking" | 1.11.0 |
| H8 | `/docs`, Error Format | The 403 row no longer says a milestone is still 403, and names the milestone a card is in; the 404 row names a milestone the user cannot see | The old rows |

Released together with cards 2719, 2752 and 2893, the earlier sections' checks of the
document's version (card 2719's H8, card 2752's D8) read `1.12.0`, with its note first and the
1.11.0 and 1.10.0 notes after it; and card 2719's H9 finds A.8.3 listing the accepted risks R5
and R6.

### The Release That Answers a Task Request the Caller Cannot Read as Not There (Card 2914)

**Card 2914, built 2026-11-18.** Until this release a signed-in account was told "Access denied"
or "This request is not addressed to you" for a task request that exists and is not theirs, and
"Request not found" for one that does not exist, so any account could try request ids and learn
which exist among requests it cannot see. From this release **a signed-in caller who cannot read
a task request is answered `404 Request not found`**, the words a missing one gets, on its read,
its thread, a reply and an accept or reject, as a caller with no account has been answered since
card 2132. `403` is kept for someone who can read the request and asks for what they may not
do: the person who raised it accepting or rejecting it, or replying as the team. The accept and
reject now ask the one rule the other request routes ask (`requireRequest`). How it works is in
[The Public Request Form](authentication-security.md#the-public-request-form); the plan is
`docs/planning/card-2914-hidden-task-request-not-found.md`.

**No key holder is affected.** No task request route is under `/api/v1/`, so the OpenAPI
document does not change; the change is recorded in
[the API reference](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-11-18) as one to DumpFire's own routes,
and needs no notice beyond card 2911's (above), which a key holder is sent. The pages read a `404` as they
read a `403`: the requester's thread page shows the link as gone, and the inbox shows the
refusal's words.

**Nothing to migrate.** No schema, setting or file changes. Going back to the previous image
needs no step; it answers `403` again.

**Accepted risks.** R5 and R6 name task requests: a request the caller is not let into is
answered after up to two team-membership reads (the route's own rule, then `canReadRequest`),
and a request's id tells its maker
how many were made since their last
([Accepted Risks](authentication-security.md#accepted-risks)).

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6, H1 to H7; on the dev server: account A; account B,
signed in, in no team A is in; account C; a confirmed request R addressed to A, made on the
public form and confirmed from its mail; a request S that C raises signed in, addressed to A):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | As B, `GET /api/requests/<R>` and `/api/requests/999999` in the browser | Both `404 {"message":"Request not found"}` | `403 Access denied` for R |
| H2 | As B, `GET /api/requests/<R>/messages` | `404 Request not found` | 403 |
| H3 | As B, from the browser console, `fetch('/api/requests/<R>', { method: 'PATCH', headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' }, body: '{"action":"reject"}' })` | `404 Request not found`; A's inbox still shows R pending | 403, or R rejected |
| H4 | As B, the same `fetch` as a `POST` to `/api/requests/<R>/messages` with `{"message":"x"}`, then with `{"message":"x","senderType":"requester"}` | Both `404 Request not found`; no message saved | 403 |
| H5 | As C, the PATCH of H3 on S | `403 This request is not addressed to you`; S still pending | 404, or S rejected |
| H6 | As A, open the inbox, R's thread, and accept R onto a board A edits | As before: the thread opens, the card is made | Any refusal |
| H7 | Signed out, R's emailed link | The thread opens, as before | Any change |

### The Release That Keeps the System Log Through an Import (Card 2899)

**Card 2899, built 2026-11-18.** Until this release Import Backup cleared the system log and
copied the backup's log in its place, so every import deleted every line written since the
backup was made, and a backup edited before it was imported put its own lines there. From
this release **an import keeps this server's system log as it was, line for line, and brings
none of the backup's lines in**; they stay in the backup file. Once the import is committed it
writes one `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line naming who imported (by name and id as they were before
the import), the file's size and SHA-256, whether it is a backup this server made that nobody
has changed, as it is or as a working copy, and how many log lines the file held. The result
ends with "The system log was kept as it was: the backup's N log line(s) were not brought in,
and remain in the backup file." An import that changed nothing names who tried on the line it
writes, a file that is not a SQLite database and a backup with no superadmin each at `WARN`.
Reset Everything is unchanged: it keeps the log, as before.

**Two more changes to the log, from the code review.** The count cap of 50,000 lines never takes
a `CRITICAL` line: those go only after `LOG_RETENTION_DAYS`, however many lesser lines follow.
And a change that switches off more than one webhook writes one `WARN` naming the first 20 and
counting the rest, where it wrote a line for each; the owners' mail is unchanged, one to each.
A log reader that counted `Webhook <id> on board <board> switched off` lines counts the webhooks
named in the one line instead. How it works is in
[Restoring from Backup](admin-guide.md#restoring-from-backup); the plan is
`docs/planning/card-2899-import-keeps-system-log.md`.

**Nothing to migrate, and no key holder is affected.** No schema, setting or file changes, and
no route under `/api/v1/` changes. `/api/admin/import`'s answer gains `systemLog`, and its
`restored` counts no longer list `system_logs`. Going back to the previous image needs no
step; its imports replace the log again.

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6; on the development server with `DB_PATH` pointing at
a scratch copy of a database, never the repository's `dumpfire.db`, as the superadmin):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Save `GET /api/logs?limit=50`. Export a backup. Make a wrong-password attempt from a private window. Import the backup, "Restore everything as it is", sign in again, and read `GET /api/logs?limit=80` | Every saved line, with the same id and text, and the wrong-password line; one `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT] The database was replaced from an uploaded backup by <you> ...` whose SHA-256 is the file's (`Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 <file>`), saying "a backup this server made that nobody has changed"; the result's last line says the log was kept | A saved line missing or changed, the wrong-password line gone, or another hash |
| H2 | Copy the backup; in the copy, `sqlite3 <copy> "UPDATE system_logs SET message = 'nothing happened' WHERE id = (SELECT MAX(id) FROM system_logs);"`; import it "as a working copy" | The log as it was plus the new lines; `GET /api/logs?q=nothing%20happened` finds nothing; the CRITICAL line says "a backup whose seal does not check out" and "restored as a working copy" | The edited text in the log, or the line calling it this server's own |
| H3 | Reset Everything on the scratch copy | The log kept, the import's CRITICAL line and the reset's both there | Either line gone |

### The Release That Disables Accounts, and Deletes Only a Disabled One (Card 2671)

**Card 2671, built 2026-11-18.** Until this release the only way to take an account away was to
delete it, and a delete also took every comment the person wrote. From this release an
administrator **disables** an account first (⛔ on the Users list, with their password and code):
from that moment it cannot sign in, every session, invite, pending sign-in and API key it had
ends, the webhooks it set are switched off for good (`setter access ended`), its report
schedules are paused and the links mailed for its task requests stop working. An administrator's
mail settings, App URL and backup destinations go with it, and any account's address in the
backup failure address. Nobody can
assign it, share a board or a team with it, include it in a decision, link a person to it or
choose it for anything new, and nothing is mailed to it as an account holder except the notice
that it was disabled. Its name stays wherever it already appears. **Enable** (✅) gives back its
sign-in alone, with its own password and authenticator: nothing that disabling ended comes back
by itself. **Delete** (🗑️) stays, for an account already disabled only. An account the
superadmin disabled is enabled or deleted by the superadmin alone. How it works is in
[Disabled Accounts](authentication-security.md#disabled-accounts-card-2671); the plan is
`docs/planning/card-2671-disable-accounts.md`.

**This is a breaking change for API keys** (OpenAPI document `1.13.0`, a dated note marked
breaking at the top of its description): a key of a disabled account is answered `401`; a
disabled account named as an assignee, a Product Owner or a decider is refused `400` in the words
an account without the board gets; a person whose account is disabled cannot be included in a
decision (`409`). **And for scripts calling the internal API:** `DELETE /api/users/{id}` answers
`409 {"message": "Disable the account first"}` for an account that is not disabled, where it
deleted it. The changelog entry is in
[the API reference](api-reference.md#changes-on-2026-11-18).

**Migration 0072** adds `users.disabled_at` (when, or NULL for an enabled account),
`users.disabled_by` (who, set NULL if that account is deleted) and the index
`idx_users_disabled_by` (see
[Data Model](data-model.md#a-disabled-account-migration-0072)). It disables no account, and runs
once. A backup made before it restores with every account enabled, except those disabled here
(below).

**At the first start, and after every restore,** the settings an administrator set are removed
where that account is disabled, as they are for one made a user or deleted (card 2397):
`whose account is disabled (found at start-up)`. The start-up line for a missing superadmin now
counts only an enabled one: `There are N user account(s) and none of them is an enabled
superadmin.` See [If Nobody Can Sign In as the Superadmin](#if-nobody-can-sign-in-as-the-superadmin),
whose host command now enables the account it makes the superadmin.

**A restore keeps this server's disabled accounts disabled.** Before an import clears `users` it
reads the accounts disabled here, and afterwards disables again each restored account with the
same id and creation time, whatever the backup held, deleting its restored API keys and pausing
its restored report schedules; the restore's webhook sweep then switches off the webhooks it set.
`disabled_by` is kept only where that account is restored as itself, by id and creation time;
where the superadmin disabled it and is not, it names the restored superadmin, so that only the
superadmin may undo it there too; else it is emptied. It is never carried onto a
restored superadmin. A backup with user accounts and no enabled superadmin among them is refused
before anything is written.

**What people notice.** The Users list shows `Disabled <date> by <name>` on a disabled row,
offers ✅ and 🗑️ there, and no 🔑, 📧 or 🛡️; an enabled row offers ⛔ and no 🗑️. The disable
confirm names the teams the account is the only owner of, and, for an administrator, the mail
settings, App URL, destinations and failure address to be removed. The toast counts what ended,
and says when the notice could not be mailed because the disable removed the mail settings. The
assignee, Share, Teams and inbox pickers leave a disabled account out; its chip, comments and
team membership still name it.

**Before going back to an older image.** The older image does not read `disabled_at`: every
disabled account can sign in there with its own password and authenticator (its sessions and keys
are already gone). List them, read only:

```bash
docker exec <container> node -e "const db = require('better-sqlite3')(process.env.DB_PATH || 'dumpfire.db', { readonly: true, fileMustExist: true }); db.prepare('SELECT id, username, role, disabled_at FROM users WHERE disabled_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id').all().forEach((u) => console.log(u.id + ' ' + u.username + ' (' + u.role + ') disabled ' + u.disabled_at)); db.close();"
```

Then make their passwords unusable, since bcrypt never matches a value that is not a hash:

```bash
docker exec <container> node -e "const db = require('better-sqlite3')(process.env.DB_PATH || 'dumpfire.db', { fileMustExist: true }); const r = db.prepare(\"UPDATE users SET password_hash = 'disabled-before-going-back' WHERE disabled_at IS NOT NULL\").run(); console.log(r.changes + ' disabled account(s) can no longer sign in with a password'); db.close();"
```

It prints `2 disabled account(s) can no longer sign in with a password`. Its schema check
reports the two columns and the index as ones it does not know and leaves them. Coming forward
again, 0072 is already recorded, and each such account, once enabled, needs a password reset
before it can sign in: by an administrator, with 🔑 on its row (`PUT /api/users/{id}/password`). An
invite (📧) sets a password only for an account with no authenticator; one that has one is
refused it (card 2773).

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6; on the development server with `DB_PATH` pointing at a
scratch copy of a database, never the repository's `dumpfire.db`, with mail configured: the
superadmin `chief`, an administrator `ann` who saved the mail settings and is the backup failure
address, a user `bob` with an API key, a webhook on a board he edits, a report schedule on, a
request he raised, assigned to a card, sole owner of team `Ops`, linked to a person in People who
is a participant of an open decision):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | As `chief`, Users, ⛔ on `bob` | The confirm names `Ops`; the toast gives 1 key, 1 webhook, 1 schedule, 1 request link; `Disabled <today> by chief` | A count is 0, or 🔑 offered |
| D2 | In `bob`'s browser, reload | The sign-in page | Any page of the board |
| D3 | Sign in as `bob` with the right password, then a wrong one | The same words both times | Different words, or signed in |
| D4 | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <bob's key>" …/api/v1/boards` | `401` | Any board |
| D5 | Open `bob`'s card | His chip still says `bob`; the assignee, Share, Teams and inbox pickers do not list him | His name gone, or listed |
| D6 | Resend on the decision for `bob`'s person | The disabled words | Mailed |
| D7 | 🗑️ on `bob`; then look at another enabled user | Offered only now; confirm; gone. No 🗑️ on the enabled user | 🗑️ on an enabled account |
| D8 | ⛔ on `ann` as `chief` | The confirm names the mail settings and the failure address; the toast says the notice could not be sent | Either not named |
| D9 | Export a backup, disable a user, import the backup | Still disabled | Enabled |
| D10 | As `ann` (re-enabled by `chief`), look at an account `chief` disabled | No 🗑️ and no ✅ | Either offered |
| D11 | Run the two commands above, then sign in on the older image as one of the accounts listed with their old password | The wrong-password answer | Signed in |
| D12 | `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`; Admin → ISO 27001 checklist, A.5.16 and A.5.18 | `info.version` `1.13.0`, its note first, "breaking"; A.5.16 and A.5.18 met, 2671 no longer listed | 1.12.x, or 2671 still listed |

### The Release That Counts Every Upload (Card 2910)

**Card 2910 (card 2761's F1, with that plan review's S13 and S15), built 2026-11-18.** Until
this release only an image counted against a person's uploads: a PDF, a document or a zip
dropped onto a card took nothing from any allowance and met no limit on its card, so one
editor, or one stolen session, could fill the server's disk 25 MB at a time. From this release
**every file counts**, whichever way it is sent. How it works is in
[Upload Limits For Every File](authentication-security.md#upload-limits-for-every-file-card-2910);
the plan is `docs/planning/card-2910-upload-limits.md`.

**What people notice.**

- Each person has **30 uploads an hour and 100 MB a day, every file together**, shared with
  their API keys. The 31st file in an hour, or one that would pass 100 MB in a day, is refused
  with the wait, in the same words for an image and any other file ("An account can upload at
  most 30 files an hour. Nothing was read or written. Try again in …").
- A person can have **3 uploads going at once**, and the server 6 among everyone ("Too many
  uploads are in progress. … Try again when the others have finished."). The card window sends
  a drop's files one at a time, so an ordinary drop never meets it.
- A card holds **20 files that are not images**, beside its 20 images: the 21st PDF is refused
  ("This card already has 20 files other than images"). A card already holding more keeps them.
- A file's shown name is cleaned (odd and invisible characters and `<>:"|?*` out) and cut to
  100 characters, its extension kept; a file named `.env` is shown as `file-<date>-<time>.env`.
  Its type is kept only when it is a plain one. On disk a file that is not an image is named
  `<uuid>` alone. Files attached before keep their names and their names on disk.
- An over-limit upload is refused before the server reads it, so the refusal comes at once
  rather than after the file has been sent.
- Nothing changes for an ordinary day's use.

**Release rules.**

- **Nothing to migrate**, no setting, no new environment variable: the counts are in memory, as
  the image allowances were, and a restart empties them; the per-card limit is counted from the
  stored rows. The OpenAPI document goes to `1.13.1`, a patch: no `/api/v1` operation, status,
  field or schema changes (its dated note lists what a key sees differently).
- **Memory, not connections.** A 25 MB upload costs the server roughly 75 to 100 MB of memory
  while it is handled, so the 3 places an account and 6 the server hold uploads to about 300 MB
  for one person and 600 MB for the server. A refusal before the body bounds what the server
  reads, not the connection: the unread body still arrives on the socket. So every refusal
  before the body (no session, no such card, no access, a key's wrong type, a declared length
  over the limit, the places and the hour) is sent with `Connection: close`, and Node ends the
  connection after its answer rather than reading the rest into it. Behind a proxy, whether the
  browser stops sending at once depends on the proxy passing that on: check it by hand on the
  production path (H8).
- **A deadline on the body.** An upload's body is given 120 seconds to arrive once its read
  begins; past it the read is stopped, the upload answered `408` ("The upload did not arrive
  within 120 seconds. Nothing was written.") with `Connection: close`, its place given back and
  what was read charged to the day. Without it a few accounts sending their bodies a byte at a
  time could hold the server's six places for Node's whole `server.requestTimeout` of 300 seconds
  (see [How Large an Import Can Be](#how-large-an-import-can-be)), again and again. Every place
  also lapses after 10 minutes whatever happens to its upload. A person on a very slow
  connection uploading a large file may meet the `408`: a 25 MB file needs about 1.7 Mbit/s.
- **A failed read is charged.** A read that fails part way, is cut off past the size limit or
  runs out of time is charged what was read to the person's day, as a finished one is.
- **The log.** The first refusal of a person's hour or day, and the first refusal for want of a
  place in 15 minutes, writes one `[WARN] [UPLOADS]` line naming the account (or the server); no
  mail. A run of such lines for one account is someone pushing the limits.
- **Not covered.** Nothing refuses an upload when the disk is nearly full: card 2920. Images held
  inline in text as `data:` addresses are outside every upload limit: card 2921.

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6; on the development server, signed in as an editor of a
test board and, for H6, a second editor account, a card open on its Files tab; the order
matters: the restart comes before the hour is spent, and the card's limit is checked on an
account whose hour is not):

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Drop a PDF and a `.docx` | Both attached, saved to disk when clicked | Refused |
| H2 | Drop a file named with 150 characters and `.pdf` | Attached; its name shown cut to 100 characters, still ending `.pdf` | Refused, or the extension lost |
| H3 | Restart the dev server | The counts start empty (in memory) | |
| H4 | Upload 30 files in an hour (mix PDFs and images, and the wrapper's `add-attachment`), then one more PDF | The 31st refused: "An account can upload at most 30 files an hour. Nothing was read or written. Try again in …" | Attached |
| H5 | Admin → Audit → Live Console after H4 | One `[WARN] [UPLOADS]` line naming the account; a further refused upload adds none | No line, or one a refusal |
| H6 | As the second editor, on a card with 20 PDFs, drop another PDF, then an image | PDF refused "This card already has 20 files other than images"; image attached | PDF attached |
| H7 | Admin → ISO 27001 checklist, A.8.6 and A.8.7 | Both describe every upload's limits; A.8.7 still met, and says other files' names are cleaned and types normalised | Images only |
| H8 | On the production path (behind its proxy or tunnel), with the account's hour spent, drop a 20 MB file | The card shows the hour's words promptly, well before a 20 MB upload would finish; the Network tab shows `429` with `Connection: close` | The upload runs to the end before the refusal, or a proxy page in place of the words |

### The Release That Ends API Keys at a Two-Step Reset (Card 2915)

**Card 2915 (card 2894's S14 and F1), built 2026-11-18.** Until this release a reset of an
account's two-step sign-in, by an administrator's 🛡️ or on the host with
`scripts/mfa-reset.mjs`, kept the account's API keys and the webhooks it set, and listed them.
A key skips the second factor, so a key made by whoever had the lost phone and the password went
on reading every board after the reset. From this release **a reset ends the account's API keys
and switches off the webhooks it set**, as an administrator's password reset does: always from
the admin page, and on the host unless it is told `--keep-api-keys`. How it works is in
[The Administrator's Reset](authentication-security.md#the-administrators-reset) and
[The Host's Command](authentication-security.md#the-hosts-command); the plan is
`docs/planning/card-2915-reset-ends-keys.md`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Lost["An authenticator is lost"] --> Where{"Reset where?"}
    Where -->|"🛡️ on the admin page"| Always["Keys end, webhooks switched off,<br/>always: no box"]
    Where -->|"the host's command"| Flag{"--keep-api-keys?"}
    Flag -->|"no (the default)"| Always
    Flag -->|"yes"| Keep["Keys and webhooks kept,<br/>said on stdout and in the log line"]
    Always --> Tell["The message, stdout and the mail<br/>say what ended"]
```

**What people notice.**

- 🛡️'s confirm says "…, their API keys end, the webhooks they set up are switched off, …", and
  the dialog after says how many ended, with the day each was made ("Their 1 API key (made …) was
  ended and the 1 webhook they set up (made …) switched off; …"). The superadmin resetting an
  administrator who set the mail settings, the App URL or a backup destination is told to review
  them; the reset removes none of them (card 2922).
- The holder's mail names each key and webhook that ended, says to make new keys for the scripts
  they recognise, and that one they did not make means someone else had their password.
- A script using the account's key is answered `401` until the holder makes a new key, once their
  new authenticator is set up. A webhook the account set stops; the board's owner or an
  administrator switches it on again, which gives it a new secret. Its `pausedBecause` reads "…had
  its password or its two-step sign-in reset, …". The board's owners were not mailed when a
  reset switched a webhook off; since card 2923 they are (see the next release).

**Release rules.**

- **Nothing to migrate**, no setting, no new environment variable. The OpenAPI document goes to
  `1.14.0`, **breaking**: a two-step reset ends the account's keys (`401`) and switches off its
  webhooks; no operation, field or schema changes.
- **A host reset of the superadmin now ends that account's integration keys** unless
  `--keep-api-keys` is given. The superadmin is the account likeliest to hold the keys an
  integration uses. Before running the command, decide: phone lost, and the password safe, keep
  them (`node scripts/mfa-reset.mjs --keep-api-keys <username>`); phone stolen, or not sure, let
  them end and make new keys afterwards. Every refused argument (an unknown option, the flag twice,
  no username) changes nothing.
- **See what will end, without changing anything.** The command has no dry run; this reads the
  account's keys and the webhooks it set that are on, on the live database, read-only:

  ```bash
  docker exec <container> node -e "
    const db = require('better-sqlite3')(process.env.DB_PATH || 'dumpfire.db', { readonly: true, fileMustExist: true });
    const user = db.prepare('SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = ?').get(process.argv[1]);
    if (user === undefined) { console.log('No such account'); process.exit(1); }
    console.table(db.prepare('SELECT id, name, created_at, expires_at, deadline_at, last_used_at FROM api_keys WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY id').all(user.id));
    console.table(db.prepare('SELECT w.id, b.name AS board, w.created_at FROM webhooks w JOIN boards b ON b.id = w.board_id WHERE w.set_by = ? AND w.active = 1 ORDER BY w.id').all(user.id));
  " <username>
  ```

  Every key listed ends (one with `expires_at` or `deadline_at` passed is already refused by the
  gate, and is counted among the ended but not named as still working); every webhook listed is
  switched off. It prints no webhook address: a path or query may hold the receiver's secret.
- **A database from before migration 0071** (between 0065 and 0071) is refused by the command,
  "this database has no webhook holds": start the server once to migrate it.
- **Going back** to the previous image needs no step and undoes nothing. Keys a reset ended stay
  ended: their rows are deleted, and the holder makes new ones. Webhooks it switched off stay off,
  held `setter access ended`, which the previous image already reads (card 2752): the board's
  owner or an administrator switches each on, with a new secret. On the previous image a reset
  keeps keys again, and its command takes no option: `--keep-api-keys` there is a usage error,
  exit 2, nothing changed.

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6; on the development server: an administrator with an
authenticator, `ada`; a user `holder` with an authenticator, one API key, a board of their own
with a webhook made with that key, and one report schedule on; for H10, the superadmin and an
administrator who saved the App URL. Never run the host command on the repository's
`dumpfire.db` directly):

Copy the database with the server stopped, or while it runs with `node -e "require('better-sqlite3')('dumpfire.db',{readonly:true}).exec(\"VACUUM INTO 'scratch.db'\")"`. `DB_PATH=scratch.db node scripts/mfa-reset.mjs holder` | Exit 0; "Ended 1 API key(s); the 1 still working: …" and "Switched off 1 webhook(s) …" | Keys kept; names on stderr or in the log |

### The Release That Holds What an Account Set When Its Access Ends (Card 2922)

**What changes.** Resetting an administrator's password or two-step sign-in, an administrator
using an invite, or an administrator ending their own keys when changing their password, holds the
mail settings, the App URL and the backup destinations that account set for the superadmin's
review: no mail through held mail settings, no link from a held App URL, no backup to a held
destination, until the superadmin keeps or removes each under **Settings held for review** on the
admin page (password and code). The same endings end the links mailed for the account's own
requests. Disable, demotion and delete remove, as before.

**Removing held mail** ends every invite not yet used, every two-step set-up link and every
request link on the server, each of which was mailed through it.

**The host reset** does the same unless `--keep-api-keys`; after resetting the superadmin, mail is
held until you sign in with the new authenticator and keep it.

**Password-only set-up** (the two-step release's leave) is closed for good once mail has ever been
set up on the server: the first start of this release records it where a mail host is stored.

**A restore** carries this server's holds over the backup's, so a setting kept here since the backup
was made may come back held: keep it again. The import's answer says how many holds it carried.

**After upgrading.** Nothing records resets made before this release. Open the Users panel and
review what each administrator set; remove anything you do not recognise.

**Migration 0074** adds `setting_holds`, applied at start; it changes no row. `scripts/mfa-reset.mjs`
refuses a database without it.

**Going back to an older image** ignores the table: every held setting is in force again. Each
start of this release names the held settings at `WARN`; keep or remove each before going back.

No published API change: OpenAPI stays 1.15.0.

### The Release That Holds the Webhooks an Owner or Administrator Could Read (Card 2935)

A webhook's signing secret is given to its board's owner and to every administrator. From this
release, ending such an account's access with its keys (a password reset, a two-step reset, an
invite used, its own change that ends keys, a disable), or lowering its role, switches off or holds
every webhook whose secret it could read and can no longer, that has a secret, whoever set it.
Each is switched on again with `PUT /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` and `active: true`, which gives it a new
secret to pass to its receiver; the boards' owners are mailed. An account that provably read no
secret (never signed in, no API key, no invite used, made after two-step sign-in was released) is
left out.

- **Ending an administrator's access stops every webhook on the server that has a secret.** Expect
  it on an administrator's password reset or two-step reset, the superadmin's included.
- **The host command.** `node scripts/mfa-reset.mjs <username>` does the same, mails nobody, and
  prints the webhooks of others it switched off or held, by board: tell each board's owner.
  `--keep-api-keys` keeps the keys and every webhook, as before. **`--hold-readable <username>`**
  (new) resets nothing: it holds only the webhooks whose secret the account can read now, writes the
  Webhooks lines and one `[WARN] [AUTH]` line, and prints them. It cannot be given with
  `--keep-api-keys`.
- **Before upgrading: an account reset or enabled before this release.** Anyone who reset, or
  enabled again, an owner or administrator that may have been taken before this release runs
  `node scripts/mfa-reset.mjs --hold-readable <username>` after upgrading.
- **The first start** holds, once, every webhook with a secret that an owner or administrator
  disabled now could read and that was made before its disable, and every webhook with a secret
  made before migration 0056 was applied here (every one, where that moment is not recorded), and
  writes the moment to `webhooks_readable_by_disabled_held`. One `[WARN] [Webhooks]` line names
  them; the owners are mailed where `SCHEDULERS` lets the schedulers run. Each later start covers
  only accounts disabled after that moment.
- **Going back to an older image, and forward again.** Nothing to delete: holds are stored as
  `setter access ended`, which the older image also answers with a new secret; an account disabled
  there is disabled after the stored moment, and the next start of this release covers it.
- **A restore** runs the pass itself, from the backup's own moment (or in full where it has
  none), before any secret is filled.
- **Nothing to set.** No migration, no environment variable.

### The Release That Holds Already-Off Webhooks When Access Ends (Card 2923)

**Card 2923 (card 2915's review S6, S8, E17), built 2026-11-19.** Every way an account's access
ends with its keys (an administrator's password set, an invite used, the holder's own change that
ends their keys, a two-step reset on the admin page or on the host, a disable, a delete) switched
off the webhooks it set that were on, and said nothing to the boards' owners. A webhook it set
that was already switched off without a hold (its owner paused it with a `PUT`, or an intruder
did) kept the secret the setter knew, and was sent with it again once switched on. From this
release **such a webhook is held too**, `setter access ended`, so switching it on gives it a new
secret, and **the boards' owners are mailed**, once the change is committed, of the webhooks
switched off and, apart, of those held. How it works is in
[What Setting a Password Ends](authentication-security.md#what-setting-a-password-ends) and
[Notifications & Email](notifications-email.md#when-nobody-who-can-open-the-board-set-it-up);
the plan is `docs/planning/card-2923-ended-access-marks-webhooks.md`.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    End["An account's access ends with its keys"] --> Hold["One statement: on ones switched off,<br/>off ones with no hold held, active left off"]
    Hold --> Where{"Where?"}
    Where -->|"the server"| Mail["A WARN for each group,<br/>one mail to each owner of their boards"]
    Where -->|"the host's command"| Print["The same WARN rows and 'not mailed',<br/>stdout lists both: tell the owners"]
    Start["First start of this release"] --> Pass["Every already-off webhook with no hold<br/>held once, whoever set it; the flag written;<br/>one WARN, nobody mailed"]
    Later["Every later start"] --> Gone["Those of disabled or unrecorded setters,<br/>a WARN only when one was held"]
    Restore["A restore, a working copy included"] --> Pass2["The same hold after its carries;<br/>every one for a backup without the flag;<br/>the server's own told with its sweep"]
```

**What people notice.**

- The boards' owners get "A notice about webhooks on your boards" where the change held an
  already-off webhook; otherwise the old subjects, "A webhook on your board was switched off" for
  one, "*N* webhooks on your boards were switched off" for more. Each mail names each board, each
  webhook's id and host, and the kind of action that caused it, naming no account ("the account
  that set it up had its password reset by an administrator"); the system log names both
  accounts. A disabled or deleted account is not mailed; a board whose only owner it was is told
  through its enabled administrators.
- A webhook switched off because nobody was recorded as its setter is given a new secret when
  switched on, as every other hold is; a `secret` sent with that switch-on is refused `400`.
- The reset, two-step reset and disable dialogs, the Account page's box and the invite page say
  "Their boards' owners are mailed about them, and about any already switched off, which can now
  be switched on only with a new secret." (in the holder's words on the Account page).
- `pausedBecause` of a webhook switched off by a `PUT` reads the reworded `setter access ended`
  sentence once its setter's access ends, where it was `null`; switching it on gives a new secret,
  and an editor may no longer delete it or make a webhook to its receiver.
- **The host's command sends no mail**: it writes the server's `Webhooks` lines and "The owners of
  the boards of the N webhook(s) switched off or held above were not mailed, as this ran on the
  server's host, which sends no mail.", lists the held ones on stdout ("Held N webhook(s) they set
  up that were already switched off: …"), and ends "Their boards' owners were not mailed: tell
  them."
- **The first start** holds every webhook already switched off with no hold, whoever set it
  (an ending of access before this release held none of them), writes one `WARN` under
  `Webhooks` naming them ("N webhook(s) already switched off with no hold are now held, whoever
  set them up (found when the server started, once): …"), and the `settings` row
  `webhooks_already_off_held`. **Every later start** holds those whose setter is disabled or not
  recorded, one `WARN` only when it held one ("… whose setter is disabled or not recorded, are now
  held (found when the server started): …"). Nobody is mailed for those. Each needs a new secret
  at its switch-on: tell the boards' owners if their receivers must be updated.
- **A restore** holds the same way after its carries, every one for a backup made before this
  release; a working copy too, before it switches every webhook off, and it tells nobody. A
  restore of the server's own database tells with its sweep.
- An import's "to enter" words set apart a webhook held this way: "Nothing to enter for webhook(s)
  …, switched off for good: to keep one, the board's owner or an administrator should switch it on
  with no secret; it is given a new one, returned once in that answer".

**Release rules.**

- **Nothing to migrate**, no new environment variable; one `settings` row written at the first
  start. The OpenAPI document goes to `1.15.0`, **breaking**: stricter answers for such a webhook
  (`400` for a `secret` sent with its switch-on, `403` to an editor's delete, `409` to an editor's
  create at its receiver, and a new secret); no operation, field or schema changes.
- **Going back** to the previous image: the held webhooks stay held, which it reads (card 2752).
  **Delete the `settings` row** `webhooks_already_off_held` when you go back, so that the next
  start of this release holds again every webhook the older image left switched off with no
  hold (its endings of access hold none):

  ```bash
  docker exec <container> node -e "require('better-sqlite3')(process.env.DB_PATH || 'dumpfire.db').prepare(\"DELETE FROM settings WHERE key = 'webhooks_already_off_held'\").run()"
  ```

  A reset on the older image mails nobody.

**Hands-on checks** (the plan's section 6, on the development server with a mail catcher and SMTP
set; accounts Owner, owning board B, Ed, its editor, and an administrator; a key each for Owner and

| H2 | The administrator resets Ed's password | The dialog says the owners are mailed; one mail to Owner, "A notice about webhooks on your boards": W1 switched off, W2 in the held list, hosts only, "What caused it: Ed's password was reset by …"; two `Webhooks` WARN lines | No mail, two mails, W2 missing, or an address |
| H3 | Owner `GET`s W2 | `pausedBecause` the reworded sentence | null |

### The Release That Seals the Stored Secrets (Card 2898)

No migration, no API version. From this release the mail password, every backup destination's
credentials, every webhook's signing secret and the three signing keys are stored sealed under a
key derived from `MFA_KEY_FILE` (see
[Service Secrets at Rest](authentication-security.md#service-secrets-at-rest-card-2898)). The
first start seals every one held in plain, before the server listens, and scrubs the old plain
text out of the file.

**Before the deploy** (read-only, on production as well), to know what the first start should
say:

```sql
SELECT key, CASE WHEN value LIKE 'dfsealed:1:%' THEN 'sealed' WHEN value = '' THEN 'empty' ELSE 'plain' END AS form
  FROM settings WHERE key IN ('smtp_pass', 'known_browser_secret', 'request_form_secret', 'backup_seal_key');
SELECT COUNT(*) AS signed_webhooks FROM webhooks WHERE secret <> '';
SELECT json_array_length(value, '$.destinations') AS destinations FROM settings WHERE key = 'backup_config';
SELECT COUNT(*) AS key_check FROM settings WHERE key = 'mfa_key_check';
```

**The first start** writes one `[WARN] [STARTUP]` line, on the console whatever `LOG_LEVEL` is:
`Sealed N stored secret(s) held in plain (the mail password, D destination field(s), W webhook
secret(s), K signing key(s); U backup configuration(s) unreadable): they are now encrypted under
the MFA key.`, naming the import's safety copy (`.pre-restore-safety.json`) where there is one,
which holds them in plain as they were: delete it once it is not needed. It records the key
check before it seals anything. This first sealing start alone (it writes
`stored_secrets_first_sealed`) deletes the stale `.backup-temp` copies a stopped backup can leave
beside the database; a later start never does. Then it scrubs the file before it listens:
`wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, `VACUUM`, `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, and clears the setting
`secrets_scrub_pending`. On a large database that start takes as long as a VACUUM does. If a
reader holds the write-ahead log, one `[ERROR] [STARTUP]` line says to run **Admin › Vacuum**
once nothing else reads the database, and the scrub is tried again **after** the server listens,
in the background (a minute after the start, then every 30 minutes, an `ERROR` for each failure),
the setting kept until one succeeds. A scrub left pending by an earlier start, a restore, a
Reset or a key change is also tried in the background, never before the server listens. Admin ›
Vacuum now checkpoints after its `VACUUM` and clears the setting; when a reader holds the log it
answers `503` ("The database was compacted, but its write-ahead log is held by a reader …") with
an `ERROR [STARTUP]` line, and is run again once nothing else reads the database. Every restore
and every Reset sets `secrets_scrub_pending`, so the replaced rows' old text is scrubbed too.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q["Run the read-only queries"] --> D["Deploy the new image"]
    D --> K{"checkMfaKeyAtStart"}
    K -- "another key, with anything sealed" --> X["CRITICAL AUTH, exit 1"]
    K -- "this key" --> F["ensureFormSecret"]
    F --> S["sealStoredSecretsAtStart:<br/>one transaction, the key check recorded first,<br/>every plain secret sealed"]
    S --> W["WARN STARTUP: Sealed N stored secret(s)"]
    W --> V["Scrub: checkpoint, VACUUM, checkpoint"]
    V -- "a reader held the log" --> E["ERROR STARTUP naming Admin › Vacuum"]
    V -- "done" --> L["Listening on"]
    E --> L
    E -. "after listening" .-> B["Tried again in the background:<br/>+1 min, then every 30 min,<br/>ERROR each failure, marker kept"]
```

**Copies made before the release** still hold the secrets in plain: volume snapshots, cold copies
and the import's safety copy. Change the mail password, the destinations' credentials and the
webhooks' secrets if any such copy may be out of your hands. Backups never held them (card 2169)
and are unchanged.

**A value that does not open** (a row edited by hand, or sealed under another key) is named at
`ERROR` at start and never used: mail is not sent while a user is set, the destination is not
tried, the webhook is not delivered ("Not sent: its signing secret cannot be opened"), and a
signing key is replaced, which forgets remembered browsers, makes open forms reload and stops
older backups verifying. Enter it again where it is set.

**Going back to an older image** is possible but costs the secrets: there is no unseal command.
The older image reads the sealed text as if it were the secret, so mail and backups fail to sign
in, webhooks are signed with a key no receiver holds, remembered browsers and open forms reset,
and it replaces the backup seal key, so backups made under this image fill nothing there. No
secret is disclosed. Before going back, plan to enter the mail password and destination
credentials again there and to set new webhook secrets with their receivers, or do not go back.
What the older image writes is sealed again at the next start on this one.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Run the queries above, then start the new image | One `Sealed N stored secret(s) …` line, N matching the plain values found, **not counting** `known_browser_secret`, `request_form_secret` or `backup_seal_key`, which card 2943 makes anew instead of sealing (its `0 signing key(s)`); the safety file named if one exists. With nothing else in plain, no Sealed line at all: the keys' line is K2 of [the card 2943 note](#the-release-that-makes-the-signing-keys-anew-card-2943) | A count that differs, or secret text in the log |
| H2 | Run the first query again | Every row `sealed`; `key_check` 1; no `secrets_scrub_pending` row | Any `plain`, or the marker left |
| H3 | Restart | No sealing line | A second |
| H4 | Admin, Mail: send a test mail; save with the password masked | The mail arrives; the row is byte for byte as before | Mail fails, or the row changed |
| H5 | Run a backup by hand | It succeeds | A credentials error |
| H6 | Make a webhook with a known secret through v1; move a card; change its address with `PUT`; move a card | Both signatures verify with that secret; the owner's `GET` shows it plain; the table holds `dfsealed:1:` | A signature that fails, or a plain row |
| H7 | Export a backup; search it for `dfsealed` and the mail password | Neither found | Either found |
| H8 | With the server running, search `dumpfire.db` and `dumpfire.db-wal` for the mail password | Not found | Found |
| H9 | Stopped: change `smtp_host` by hand; start; Admin, Mail; send a test mail | One `ERROR` naming the mail password; the field empty; the test mail refused, nothing sent | The password used or shown |
| H10 | Change the key with `MFA_KEY_FILE_PREVIOUS` | The `Rotated …` line counts the stored secrets; mail and backups still work | A refused start, or a failure |
| H11 | Start with a different key file | Refused with the mismatch line naming stored secrets | It starts |
| H12 | Import Backup of the H7 backup | Mail password, destination and webhook kept and working | Any listed to enter |
| H13 | Admin › Vacuum | Succeeds; `dumpfire.db-wal` is empty after | A log left with frames |
| H14 | Stopped: point `MFA_KEY_FILE` at a new, empty key's file with nothing else changed; start | Refused: "None of the N stored secret(s) opens with this MFA key … FORGET_UNOPENABLE_SECRETS=1"; nothing changed. Put the right key back | It starts, or anything is forgotten |

### The Release That Makes the Signing Keys Anew (Card 2943)

> ⚠️ **Card 2898 never ships without card 2943.** Card 2898 seals the signing keys in place,
> and every whole copy of the database made before it holds them in plain. Card 2943 makes them
> anew at the same first start. An image carrying both is fine; one with card 2898 and without
> card 2943 is not to be deployed.

No migration, no API version. Until card 2898 the server stored three signing keys in plain:
the key it seals its backups with (`backup_seal_key`), the key remembered browsers are signed
with and the request form's key. Every cold copy, volume snapshot and old
`.pre-restore-safety.json` made before this release holds them. With the backup seal key,
whoever holds such a copy can make a backup file this server takes as its own and fills its
mail password, destination credentials and webhook secrets and addresses into. **The first start
of this release makes each of the three anew**, sealed under the MFA key with its form (`v2:`
and 64 hex) inside the seal, and any later start does the same for a key it finds in plain, of
the older form or (the seal key) missing. See
[The Signing Keys Made Anew Once](authentication-security.md#the-signing-keys-made-anew-once-card-2943).

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R["Before: read the import lines and the<br/>superadmins and administrators (read-only)"] --> S["Stop the old container"]
    S --> D["Start the new image"]
    D --> F["First start: the three keys made anew,<br/>one CRITICAL 'Key change recorded' line"]
    F --> B["Run Now: a backup sealed with the new key"]
    B --> C["Release known good:<br/>rm -rf the cold copy, delete the safety copy"]
```

**Before the deploy** (read-only, on the host, against the live database). A forged backup
restored before this release is not undone by it, so read who imported what and who holds the
two highest roles now:

```sql
SELECT timestamp, message FROM system_logs WHERE level = 'CRITICAL' AND context = 'IMPORT' ORDER BY id;
SELECT id, username, role, created_at FROM users WHERE role IN ('superadmin', 'admin') ORDER BY role, id;
```

Every import line should be one you made, and every account one you know. If not, stop and
treat the server as compromised (change every secret at its service) before deploying.

**Stop the old container before starting the new one.** The keys are made in one IMMEDIATE
transaction before the server listens. A second instance on the same database waits for it
(better-sqlite3's default busy timeout, 5 seconds), then finds the keys already made and makes
nothing; past the timeout it is refused and does not start.

**The first start** writes one line, on the console and in the system log, where it is kept for
good with the other CRITICAL lines:

`[CRITICAL] [STARTUP] Key change recorded: made at this start, each stored encrypted under the
MFA key: the backup seal key (the one stored was in plain); the remembered-browser key (the one
stored was in plain); the request-form key (the one stored was in plain). Backups sealed before
now are taken as another server's: …`

The reason is "the one stored was of an older form" where card 2898 has already sealed a key in
place, and "none was stored" for a seal key no backup ever made. Card 2898's own "Sealed N stored
secret(s)" line, written at the same start, counts **0 signing key(s)**: the three are made
anew, never sealed in place. A restart writes neither line. Read it back (read-only):

```sql
SELECT key, substr(value, 1, 9) AS form FROM settings WHERE key IN ('backup_seal_key', 'backup_seal_key_made_at');
```

`backup_seal_key` reads `dfsealed:`, and `backup_seal_key_made_at` holds the moment as an ISO
time: information only, never a reason the server keeps or replaces the key.

**What changes once, at that start:**

- **Every backup made before it is another server's**, **the one taken just before the deploy
  included**: Import Backup restores everything, then lists the mail password, each
  destination's credentials and each webhook's secret and address to enter again ("None was kept
  from this server, because this backup was not made by this server, or was changed since."), and
  gives no second factor to an account not on this server, nor, since card 3009, any password or
  API key to an account not the same here (by number, creation time and username, as such a backup
  carries no installation id). Have the mail password and the
  destinations' credentials to hand for as long as such a backup might be restored. The
  replacement is automatic: you do not choose when older backups stop counting as this server's.
  Run **▶ Run Now** after the deploy so a backup sealed with the new key exists at once.
- **Every remembered browser is forgotten**: each person meets sign-in's ordinary throttling
  until they next sign in.
- **Open request forms, decision revisions and comment keys are made again**: a page open
  across the deploy is refused once and reloaded. Nothing stored depends on them.
- **The import's safety copy** leaves out every signing key from now on.

**Going back to an older image, and forward again.** The older image (from before card 2898; no
image carries card 2898 without this card) cannot open the sealed keys:
- **The seal key.** It does not take the sealed text for a key, and writes a new plain one at
  its first backup. Backups made under this release then fill nothing there.
- **The remembered-browser and form keys.** It signs with the sealed text as it stands, and
  replaces neither. So remembered browsers and open forms start again once, there.

On the way forward, the start makes anew each key the older image replaced or made in plain, and
its key-change line names each by the reason "the one stored was in plain": usually the backup
seal key alone, once the older image has taken a backup. Those backups are another server's
here. A key the older image left sealed is kept, and is not named. Cookies and forms the older
image signed with that key's sealed text do not hold here, so remembered browsers and open forms
start again once more.

**Changing the backup seal key again later**: with the container stopped, delete its row, then
start; the start makes a new one, with the line, its record and a scrub of the file. On a copy of
this server's volume, change the installation id with it (card 3009): see
[Moving to a New Host](#moving-to-a-new-host).

```bash
docker stop dumpfire
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data dumpfire:latest node -e "
const db = require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db', { fileMustExist: true });
console.log('keys removed:', db.prepare('DELETE FROM settings WHERE key = ?').run('backup_seal_key').changes);
db.close();
"
docker start dumpfire
```

**Once the release is known good**, delete the copies that still hold the old keys and every
other secret in plain: the cold copy (`rm -rf "$HOME/dumpfire-cold"`) and the import's safety copy
(`docker exec <container> rm -f /app/data/.pre-restore-safety.json`). Returning the cold copy
brings the old keys back; the next start makes them anew again.

K1 to K6 restore backups, so they run on an instance that is not production, with a database
of its own and a made-up mail password saved, first on the older image and then updated; K7
and K8 run on production too.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| K1 | On the older image: ▶ Run Now once, then Export Backup, kept as file A | A file | |
| K2 | Stop it; start the new image on the same volume | One `[CRITICAL] [STARTUP] Key change recorded` line naming the three keys, with no hex in it | No line, two, or a value |
| K3 | Restart | No such line | The line again |
| K4 | Export Backup as file B; Import Backup of B as it is | Nothing to enter: "Kept from this server…" | The mail password listed |
| K5 | Import Backup of A as it is | "To enter again" names the mail password and ends "None was kept from this server, because this backup was not made by this server, or was changed since." | "Kept from this server" |
| K6 | Restart | No key-change line (the key and its record were kept across K5) | The line |
| K7 | Search `.pre-restore-safety.json` for `backup_seal_key`, `known_browser_secret` and `request_form_secret` | None found | Any found |
| K8 | The read-only query above | `dfsealed:` and an ISO time | Plain hex, or no time |

### The Release That Brings Service Account JSON to One Rule (Card 2939)

**Every start**, in the same transaction as the sealing above and before it, brings each backup
destination's service account JSON to the one rule: a key file from Google is rebuilt to the
fields DumpFire signs in with (`type`, `project_id`, `client_email`, `private_key_id`, `client_id`,
`private_key`, its sealed key carried as it is); a service account JSON that is not a key loses its
key; anything else, and any JSON on an OAuth or non-Drive destination, is emptied. When it changed
anything it marks the scrub (so the file is scrubbed before the server listens) and writes one
line after the commit, on the console whatever `LOG_LEVEL` is:

`[WARN] [STARTUP] Rewrote the service account JSON of N backup destination(s) to the fields
DumpFire signs in with: destination "Name" (kept its key, every other field dropped); …. What was
removed may still be in older copies of the database: the import's safety copy, backups and volume
snapshots.`

Each destination is named with how it changed (`kept its key, every other field dropped`; `its
key removed, as the JSON is not a service account key file from Google: enter the key file
again`; `cleared, as it held JSON that is not a service account key file, …`), never a value. The
first start after the release names every Drive service account saved before it (its file is
rebuilt); a later start says nothing. A destination whose key was removed or cleared is listed to
enter at start, as after a restore, and a run does not try it.

**A Test runs only a saved destination**, exactly as stored, for every type: a Test sent with a
secret typed, or with any setting that is not secret changed, is answered `400` and nothing is
connected to: with its secret masked, in the save's own words ("Backup destination "…": type its
… again …"); otherwise "Save the destination first, then Test it.". The admin page's Test sends
the saved destination, so it is unchanged.

**`GOOGLE_CLOUD_UNIVERSE_DOMAIN`.** A service account signs in with a JWT built for Google's own
universe, `googleapis.com`. Set this environment variable to anything else and every Google Drive
call fails ("The configured universe domain … does not match the universe domain found in the
credentials …"): leave it unset, or set it to `googleapis.com`.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H15 | On a scratch copy with a Drive service account saved before the release, start the new image | One `Rewrote the service account JSON of …` line naming it, "kept its key"; check 0g's line for it says `service account type "service_account"`; ▶ Run Now succeeds | No line, key text in it, or the run failing |
| H16 | Restart | No `Rewrote …` line | A second |
| H17 | Repeat a saved destination's Test from the browser's network panel with its host, endpoint or folder changed; then again with its secret emptied as well | `400`, nothing connected: with the secret masked, the save's own sentence ("Backup destination "…": type its … again …"); with no secret sent, "Save the destination first, then Test it." | Any connection attempt, or a `200` |

### The Release That Seals Webhook Addresses (Card 2928)

A Slack, Teams or Discord webhook address carries its secret in its path. From this release every
webhook address is stored sealed under the MFA key, beside a plain `receiver` (its scheme, host and
port, migration 0073); no backup or export holds one. Nothing is to be done on the deploy.

**Before the deploy (read-only):**

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) AS plain_addresses FROM webhooks WHERE url <> '' AND substr(url, 1, 9) <> 'dfsealed:';
```

**The first start** seals every address and fills `receiver`, counted in the sealing line ("…, N
webhook address(es), …"); rewrites each old `Webhook delivery failed for hook N → <address>` log
line to the host, its `meta` replaced, before the scrub takes the old text out of the file; marks
the scrub once whatever it seals, and deletes stale `.backup-temp` copies. Every start also
deletes a stale `.restore-temp` upload (and its `-journal`, `-wal` and `-shm`) that a crashed
import left: no import runs before the server listens. A log rewrite that fails is one WARN naming `GET /api/logs`, never a refused
start. A plain webhook secret beside an address that is empty or does not open is never sealed:
