every start blanks it, switches the webhook off, lists it among the webhooks to enter, marks the
scrub and names it at ERROR; a second start writes nothing.

**Copies from before the release** hold the addresses in plain: older backups and exports, volume
snapshots, cold copies, the import's safety copy, and container, console or shipped logs. Where any
may be out of your hands, regenerate the receiver's address (Slack: a new incoming webhook; Teams: a
new workflow URL; Discord: delete and recreate the webhook) and set it with
`PUT /api/v1/webhooks/{id}`.

**What stays plain.** A webhook's `receiver` (its scheme, host and port) stays plain in the
database, in backups, and in log lines and mails. A receiver that carries its token in the host
(a per-endpoint subdomain) is not covered: regenerate such addresses if copies may be out of your
hands.

**Backups from now on** hold every address as `''`, the webhook off, listed with a match keyed by
`webhook_address_mac_key`, which no copy holds. A restore onto this server puts each back; onto
another, or where the webhook here changed or the key is lost, each comes back off and is named
("the address(es) of webhook(s) …") until its `url` (and secret) is sent with `active: true`.

**Going back to 1.14.0.** No unseal command; nothing is disclosed. 1.14.0 reads each envelope as the
address: every webhook is refused as written and nothing is sent. Set each address again there with
`PUT`, or do not go back. Keep the `receiver` column. Coming forward, addresses 1.14.0 wrote are
sealed at the next start; a 1.14.0 `PUT` of a new `url` that kept the secret leaves that secret bound
to the old address, so set it again.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H18 | Run the query, then start the new image | One sealing line counting the webhook addresses; the query gives 0; `receiver` holds each origin | A plain address left, or a path in the log |
| H19 | Move a card | The receiver gets the event at its path, signed | Not delivered |
| H20 | Export a backup and search it for a webhook's path and `dfsealed:` | Neither found | Either found |
| H21 | Import that backup | Each webhook back with its address, on as it was | Listed to enter |
| H22 | `node scripts/mfa-reset.mjs --keep-api-keys <setter>` | Lists each webhook "to <host>" | A path or an envelope |

### The Release That Refuses Uploads When the Uploads Volume Is Nearly Full (Card 2920)

Before an upload is read, the server checks the free space on the disk that holds the uploads. If
what is free, less room for a 25 MB upload, would fall below 1 GB plus twice the database's size,
the upload is refused, `507`, with "Uploads are paused: the server has too little free disk space,
or cannot read how much it has. Nothing was written. An administrator can see which on the admin
page.", in the card window and through an API key alike; and so is every upload while the free
space cannot be read. The admin page's Database Overview shows the free space and the line; the system log says
once when uploads start being refused and once when they are accepted again. See
[Free space on the uploads volume](#free-space-on-the-uploads-volume).

**Before the deploy (read-only):** check the volume has more than about 1 GB plus twice the
database's size free:

```bash
docker exec dumpfire df -h /app/data
docker exec dumpfire ls -l /app/data/dumpfire.db /app/data/dumpfire.db-wal
```

If not, uploads are refused from the first start until space is freed or the volume grown.

Nothing to migrate and nothing to configure. **Going back to an older image** takes the check
away; nothing is stored. **Published API:** OpenAPI stays `1.15.0` (unreleased), with note 8: the
`507` on `POST /api/v1/cards/{cardId}/attachments`.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | As an administrator, open Admin | Database Overview shows Uploads Disk Free and "Uploads are refused when less than … is free" | No line, or an error on the page |
| H2 | On a test host whose uploads are on a small volume of their own (a loop or tmpfs mount, never the real disk), fill it below the line, then drop a file on a card | The card shows "Uploads are paused: …"; 507 with `Connection: close`; one `[WARN] [UPLOADS] Uploads are refused: …`; the admin line in red | Accepted, a 500, or a WARN for every refusal |
| H3 | Free the space and upload again | Accepted; one `[INFO] [UPLOADS] Uploads are accepted again: …` | Still refused |
| H4 | With an API key, send an image while below the line | 507, the same words | Any other status or words |

### The Release That Reports Retention Problems and Addresses OneDrive App-Only (Card 2941)

**Retention problems are reported.** After a good upload, a listing or delete that fails at any
destination, or one that does not answer within 60 seconds, leaves the run a success but puts the
reason on its Backup History row (✅ ⚠️), in the Run Now answer, and in the failure mail ("DumpFire
Backup Needs Attention", or "Failed" where a destination also failed). The mail repeats every run
until the cause is put right. Keep Last removes only files named as DumpFire names its copies; on
Google Drive and S3 only one it has just listed. The first call that does not answer stops the
removals, and one destination's retention stops after five minutes.

**S3 counts only its own copies** (card 2991, taken into card 2941): the listing reads every page
(it read the first 1,000 keys), one level under the prefix and a `/`, so a copy in a folder below
the prefix, or under a prefix that only begins the same (`dumpfire-old/` beside `dumpfire/`), is no
longer counted or removed. A bucket that held more than 1,000 keys under the prefix will have its
older copies removed down to Keep Last at the first run after the deploy.

**OneDrive needs whose OneDrive.** DumpFire signs in to Microsoft Graph as the app, with no user;
the addresses it used before were not valid for that sign-in. Each OneDrive destination now holds a
user's sign-in name or object ID, or a drive ID (`b!…`). One saved before the release is kept but
not tried until it is edited, given its user or drive, and its client secret typed again; Backup
History, the mail and Test say so. For least privilege, give the app Microsoft Graph Application
permission `Sites.Selected` (admin consent, like any Application permission) and, as a separate
step, `write` granted on one site, and give that library's drive ID;
`Files.ReadWrite.All` reads and writes every user's files in the tenant.

**A held destination cannot be moved by a save**: a change of any field of its place (host, port,
user name, remote path, region, bucket, prefix, endpoint, access key ID, folder ID, client ID,
tenant ID, folder path, or a OneDrive drive added, changed or removed) is refused `409` until the
superadmin keeps or removes it.

**Before the deploy (read-only)**, to word the release note (ruling R8):

```sql
SELECT status, substr(error, 1, 120) AS error, created_at FROM backup_log WHERE destination_type = 'onedrive' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10;
```

Only `failed` rows, or none, confirms that no OneDrive backup ever succeeded with the old addresses.

Nothing to migrate: no schema change, and nothing already sealed, held or recorded changes. **Going
back to an older image** ignores `drive` and uses the old addresses again, which fail. **Published
API:** none; OpenAPI stays `1.15.0` with notes 1 to 8.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Add a OneDrive destination with the user/drive box empty | Add stays disabled; sent from the network panel, `400` "drive is required for OneDrive" | It saves |
| H2 | App with Application `Files.ReadWrite.All` and admin consent; give the test user's sign-in name, save, Test | "Connected to <user>'s OneDrive (drive business); folder "DumpFire Backups" will be made by the first backup" | `/drives/root:`, "Invalid request", or a token error |
| H3 | ▶ Run Now | ✅; the folder and the `…-manual.db` copy are in the user's OneDrive | A failed row |
| H4 | Keep Last 1, Run Now twice | The older copy gone; ✅ with no ⚠️ | It is kept |
| H5 | Give the user's object ID instead, type the client secret again, save, Test | As H2 | Refused |
| H6 | Set the box to `not-a-drive`, or the folder to `a/../b`, and save | `400` naming the field | Saved |
| H7 | On a scratch SFTP destination, `chmod 333` its remote folder; Run Now with failure mail on; then `chmod 755` | ✅ ⚠️ "Keep Last was not applied: …", a warning toast, one "DumpFire Backup Needs Attention" mail with "Problem:" | No ⚠️, or no mail |
| H8 | Remove the app's admin consent, then Test | A failure in Graph's words | Success |
| H9 | Change the user box without typing the client secret, save | Refused: type the client secret again | Saved |
| H10 | The read-only query above, before the deploy | Only `failed` rows, or none | A `success` row: word the release note conditionally |
| H13 | On an S3 destination whose prefix has a folder below it and a sibling prefix (`dumpfire/old/` and `dumpfire-old/`), each holding a copy-named file, set Keep Last 1 and Run Now twice | Only the newest `…-manual.db` directly under `dumpfire/` is kept beside the run's; the two files below and beside are untouched | Either removed |
| H11 | App with Application `Sites.Selected` only (admin consented); an administrator also grants it `write` on a dedicated SharePoint site (`POST /sites/{site-id}/permissions`); give the library's drive ID, Test, Run Now | Test names the library's owner; the copy lands in that library | `403`, or the copy elsewhere |
| H12 | Hold a destination (end its setter's access), then change its folder and save | `409` "where it sends its copies cannot be changed by a save" | Saved |

### The Release That Holds What an Ended API Key Was Given (Card 2947)

**Migration 0075** adds `webhook_reveals` and changes no row. From this release every answer
that gives a webhook's signing secret records the API key it went to; revoking that key holds,
in the same change, every webhook with a secret it was given, and a key that expires or passes its
deadline does within five minutes (a sweep at every start, then every five minutes, whatever
`SCHEDULERS` says; the owners are mailed only where the schedulers run). Each is held as `setter
access ended`: the board's owner switches it on (`PUT /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` with
`{"active": true}`) for a new secret, and gives it to the receiver.

**The first start.** Every API key ever used through the API counts as given the secret of each
webhook with a secret its account can read or set (an administrator's: every board) that was made
before the key's last use. Where such a key has already expired or passed its deadline, those
webhooks are held at that first start, one Webhooks WARN naming them, and an INFO line counts the
rows seeded. To see beforehand which keys that is, on a read-only copy of the database:

```sql
SELECT u.username, u.role, u.disabled_at, k.id AS key_id, k.name, k.last_used_at, k.expires_at, k.deadline_at
FROM api_keys k JOIN users u ON u.id = k.user_id
WHERE k.last_used_at IS NOT NULL
  AND ((k.expires_at IS NOT NULL AND (datetime(k.expires_at) IS NULL OR datetime(k.expires_at) <= datetime('now')))
    OR (k.deadline_at IS NOT NULL AND (datetime(k.deadline_at) IS NULL OR datetime(k.deadline_at) <= datetime('now')))
    OR u.disabled_at IS NOT NULL)
ORDER BY u.username, k.id;
```

Each row's account's webhooks with a secret (on every board, for an administrator) made before its
`last_used_at` are held at the first start. An expiry or a deadline that names no moment counts as
passed, and a key of a disabled account as ended, as the seed and the sweep read them (fail closed).
Keep or rotate those integrations' receivers ready.

**Keys revoked before this release.** A key revoked before this release left no row, so nothing
holds what it read. Where a key may have leaked and was revoked before upgrading, rotate the
secret of every webhook it could read: send a new `secret` with `PUT /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` (a
switch-off and switch-on by `PUT` keeps the old secret), and give the receiver the new one.

**The cost of rotating a key.** Routine expiry holds too: a key that lists webhooks is given their
secrets, so its expiry, deadline or revoke gives each of them a new secret, which each receiver
needs. Prefer a key with no expiry for a script that reads webhooks, and rotate deliberately; the
Account page says beside each key how many webhooks its end would hold.

**The `PUT` answer.** `PUT /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` now gives `secret` only where it set or replaced
it. A script that read the secret back from an `events`-only change reads it with `GET` instead.

**Going back to an older image.** The table is left unread and unwritten: a revoke or an expiry
there holds nothing it revealed, and reveals there are not recorded. Holds already made stay
`setter access ended`, which the older image answers with a new secret at the switch-on. The host
command (`scripts/mfa-reset.mjs`) of this release refuses a database without the table.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Owner lists a board's webhooks with key K | The secrets given; `Cache-Control: no-store` | No header |
| H2 | Account page | K's line: "and holds N whose secret it was given" | No count |
| H3 | Revoke K | Each listed webhook off; one mail per owner naming no account, saying to change the secret at the receiver now | Still on, or a name in the mail |
| H4 | Owner switches one on with key M | A new secret | The old one |
| H5 | Give a key an expiry five minutes out, list with it, wait | Within five minutes of the expiry each listed webhook is off, one WARN naming the key | Still on |
| H6 | `PUT` changing only `events` | Answer without `secret` | The secret given |

### The Release That Keeps Ended API Keys Ended Across a Restore (Card 2995)

**Ships with card 2947**: migrations 0074, 0075 and 0076 are applied in one start, with OpenAPI
`1.15.0`. **Migration 0076** adds `api_key_revocations` and changes no existing row.

**What changes.** A restore never brings back an API key that was revoked here, ended with its
account's access (a password set by an administrator, an invite used, the holder's own change that
ends keys, a two-step reset in the app or on the host, a disable, a delete), or cleared by Reset
Everything. Each such ending records the key's id and its SHA-256, never the key. Every import leaves
those keys out, from this server's backups and any other's; the result and the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]`
line count them, the line's details naming them by id; what such a key set up or was given the secret
of is held as at a revoke. Every check of a key refuses one the record names, and the start and the
five-minute sweep end any found in place, with one `[WARN] [AUTH]` line.

**A working copy leaves out every API key.** No key of the backup works on a copy restored with
"Restore as a working copy"; the result counts them. Make new keys on the copy.

**This release's image.** The commands below name it `dumpfire:2995`: tag it so as soon as it is
built (`docker tag dumpfire:latest dumpfire:2995`), so that a command meant for this release never
runs an image that `latest` has since moved to, or back from. Any image of this release or later does.

**The first start.** 0076 writes the watermark W, the larger of the `api_keys` id counter and the
largest key id held (Admin › Vacuum and Reset deleted the counters before c6ed310, so the counter
alone can be low), and records by id every id from 1 to W that `api_keys` no longer holds, one row
each, never a range. A restore of any backup made before the deploy leaves those keys out, a key an
earlier import removed included, and records each one's hash when it is found. Preview before the
deploy, read-only, from a container of the image on the same volume (nothing in it is written; it
can run beside the server):

```bash
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data dumpfire:2995 node -e "const d=require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true,fileMustExist:true});console.log(d.prepare(\"SELECT w, w - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM api_keys) AS seed_rows FROM (SELECT max(coalesce((SELECT seq FROM sqlite_sequence WHERE name = 'api_keys'), 0), coalesce((SELECT max(id) FROM api_keys), 0)) AS w)\").get())"
```

**Where `seed_rows` is above 1,000,000** the first start halts at 0076 (card 2995's code review,
FP5), changing nothing of it, with `CHECK constraint failed: migration 0076 would record more than
1,000,000 API key ids this server no longer holds …`: the id counter has been set far above every
key, by hand or by a fault. Find out why before going on. Lowering the counter
(`UPDATE sqlite_sequence SET seq = <the largest key id> WHERE name = 'api_keys'`, with the container
stopped) lets the start go on, and gives up the record of every id between: any key issued there
and ended before this release could come back with an older backup.

**Keys ended on another server.** A restore onto another server cannot know of keys ended on the
server that made the backup after the backup was made: it applies its own record, nothing else,
since that server's backup never verifies here and adds none of its record (card 3013). Restore the newest backup available.

**What stays possible (residual).** A key ended before this release whose hash this server never
saw (it was gone before 0076, and recorded only by its id) can come back if a backup is edited to
move it to an id the record does not name. Only the superadmin can import, and an import names the
file's SHA-256 in its `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line. A seed row from another server's backup can also
leave out a key of this server whose id it names: that is the fail-closed direction, counted in the
answer, and the key is made again in a minute.

**Before a host file rollback** (see [Taking and Returning the Cold Copy](#taking-and-returning-the-cold-copy)):
the cold copy holds the keys as they were when it was taken, so a key revoked since would work
again. Dump the record first, with the container stopped, from this release's image:

```bash
docker run --rm --network none --user root -v dumpfire-data:/app/data -v "$HOME/dumpfire-cold:/cold" \
  dumpfire:2995 node -e "const D=require('better-sqlite3');const d=new D('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true});require('fs').writeFileSync('/cold/revocations.json',JSON.stringify(d.prepare('SELECT * FROM api_key_revocations').all()))"
```

While an image older than this release runs on the returned copy, it neither has nor reads the
record: revoke again, on each holder's Account page, every key ended since the cold copy was taken.

To put the dump back when this release runs again on a copy that predates it, the table must exist,
and only 0076 makes it. So: **first start this release on the copy with no network, and stop it as
soon as it is migrated**; then put the dump back with the server stopped; then start it as usual.
This is the simplest safe order: 0076 never meets a table it did not make, no request can present a
key while the copy is migrated and the record not yet back (there is no network), and the start
that follows ends every key the dump names that is in place, before the schedulers.

```bash
# 1. The first start, with no network: run it as the usual `docker run` does (the same volume, the
#    same environment and MFA_KEY_FILE), but with --network none, and stop it once the log says the
#    migrations were applied.
docker run -d --name dumpfire-migrate --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data <the usual -e and -v options> dumpfire:2995
docker logs -f dumpfire-migrate   # until "Listening on"; then Ctrl+C
docker stop dumpfire-migrate && docker rm dumpfire-migrate
# 2. The dump put back, with the server stopped.
docker run --rm --network none --user root -v dumpfire-data:/app/data -v "$HOME/dumpfire-cold:/cold" \
  dumpfire:2995 node -e "const D=require('better-sqlite3');const d=new D('/app/data/dumpfire.db');const rows=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/cold/revocations.json','utf8'));const put=d.prepare('INSERT OR IGNORE INTO api_key_revocations (key_id, key_hash, revoked_at, revoked_because) VALUES (@key_id, @key_hash, @revoked_at, @revoked_because)');d.transaction(()=>rows.forEach((row)=>put.run(row)))()"
# 3. Start as usual.
```

Where the returned copy was taken after this release had already run (it has the table), skip step 1.
The node commands run from the image's own working folder, where `better-sqlite3` is installed. The
dump holds key ids and SHA-256 fingerprints, never a key, and is safe to keep beside the cold copy.

**Reset Everything** records every key it clears and keeps the record.

**Going back to an older image.** That image never writes the record, and **its import clears the
record and refills it from the backup**: never import a backup while an image older than this
release runs. Where it must be done, dump the record first (the command above), and once this
release runs again put it back (steps 2 and 3 above, with the server stopped); coming forward, the
first start also ends any present key the record still names, as a revoke does. The host command
(`scripts/mfa-reset.mjs`) of this release refuses a database without the table.

**Nothing to set.** No environment variable, no OpenAPI change.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Export a backup; revoke key K on its holder's Account page | K gone | |
| H2 | Import the file as it is | "1 API key(s) in the backup were left out …"; the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line "…leaving out 1 API key(s) ended on this server…", its details naming K's id and no account | K listed again, or a name in the line |
| H3 | `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <K>" …/api/v1/me`, then with a key L not revoked | 401, then 200 | 200 for K |
| H4 | Import the same file as a working copy | Every key left out and counted | Any key works on the copy |
| H5 | Restart | No new line; K still refused | K works |

### The Release That Keeps Ended Accounts Ended Across a Restore (Card 2996)

**Ships with cards 2947, 2995 and 2997**, before the release is pushed: migrations 0074 to 0077 are
applied in one start, with OpenAPI `1.15.0` (neither this card nor card 2997 changes OpenAPI). It never
ships without card 2997, so no database runs this card's build without card 2997's reading of
`password` rows. **Migration 0077** adds `account_endings` and changes no existing row. Any image of
this release can run the commands below (the image tagged for card 2995, `dumpfire:2995`, once rebuilt
with this release).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Start["first start of this release"] --> M77["0077: guard, table, watermark W,<br/>seed by id up to W, present roles and disables"]
    M77 --> Pass["start pass: accounts the record ends<br/>ended again (none at first)"]
    Pass --> Live["every delete, disable, enable,<br/>role change and creation recorded"]
    Live --> Imp["every import keeps them ended"]
```

**What changes.** A restore never brings back an account deleted here, never lifts a disable made
here, and never gives back a role lowered here. Every delete, disable, enable and role change, and the
role every account is made with, records the account's id and creation time and, for a delete, a
fingerprint of its password hash, never the hash. Every import, of this server's backups and any
other's, as it is or as a working copy, keeps those endings: a deleted account comes back disabled
with no password or second factor that works and cannot be enabled (delete it again, then make a new
account for anyone who returns); a disabled one stays disabled; a role is capped at this server's.
The result and the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line count them and name nobody. The next start, and every
five minutes, end again any such account found otherwise, with one `[WARN] [AUTH]` line of counts.

**The first start.** 0077 writes the watermark W, the larger of the `users` id counter and the largest
account id held; records by id every id up to W that `users` no longer holds, one row each; and
records every present account's role and every disable, the superadmin's never. Preview, read-only,
from a container of this release's image on the same volume:

```bash
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data dumpfire:2995 node -e "const d=require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true,fileMustExist:true});console.log(d.prepare(\"SELECT w, w - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users) AS seed_rows FROM (SELECT max(coalesce((SELECT seq FROM sqlite_sequence WHERE name = 'users'), 0), coalesce((SELECT max(id) FROM users), 0)) AS w)\").get())"
```

**Where `seed_rows` is above 1,000,000** the first start halts at 0077, changing nothing of it, with
`CHECK constraint failed: migration 0077 would record more than 1,000,000 account ids …`: the users id
counter is set far above every account. Find out why before going on; lowering the counter (with the
container stopped) gives up the record of every id between.

**Accounts that only share a number.** A backup holding an account whose id this server once had and
deleted before 0077 (or held, just before the import, with a later creation time) brings it back
disabled with no working password: the superadmin enables it and sends it an invite if it should
stay. Counted in the result.

**Account ids above W** (card 2995's N1, for accounts). Where Admin › Vacuum or Reset deleted the
`users` counter and the highest accounts were then ended, before this release, those ids are above W
and a backup from before can bring them back. Inherent to the watermark; the counter alone can be low.

**Another server's endings.** A restore onto another server applies its own record, nothing else:
that server's backup never verifies there, so its record is not taken (card 3013), and it cannot know
of accounts ended there after the backup was made.

**What stays possible (residual).** An account deleted before 0077 can come back as a new account if
someone edits an old backup to change its id, its creation time and its password hash: only the
superadmin can import, and the import's line names the file's SHA-256.

**Reset Everything** keeps the record and records every account but the superadmin as disabled: an
import after a reset brings the accounts back disabled, and the superadmin enables the ones wanted.
Since card 2997 it records each one's password as replaced too, so each comes back with a password
nothing matches as well, and needs its password set (🔑) or an invite (📧) once enabled.

**Passwords (card 2997, same release).** No import brings back a password replaced here: the same
account keeps this server's, an account not here gets one nothing matches. A password replaced before
this release was never fingerprinted, so a backup made before that change can still bring it back:
after restoring such a backup, reset those accounts' passwords as before. A backup whose seal does not
verify keeps this server's password for the same account and, since card 3009, gives an account not
the same here none of its own (see
[The Release That Takes Nothing That Signs In From an Unsealed Backup](#the-release-that-takes-nothing-that-signs-in-from-an-unsealed-backup-card-3009)).
See [Restoring from Backup](admin-guide.md#restoring-from-backup).

**A database that ran an unreleased card 2996 build** (a development or test server, never production:
`332634f` never ran one, so it holds none). Card 2997 fingerprints a password hash in its `$2b$` form
(R1), so that a `$2a$` or `$2y$` copy of the same hash cannot escape the record. A `deleted` row
written by that earlier build of a hash stored with a `$2a$` or `$2y$` prefix holds the fingerprint
of that form, which no longer matches the account's hash. bcryptjs writes `$2b$`, so such rows arise
only from hashes written by another tool. Such a row still names its account by id and creation
time; only a copy of that account under another id or creation time is no longer caught by its
fingerprint.

**Before a host file rollback** (see [Taking and Returning the Cold Copy](#taking-and-returning-the-cold-copy)):
dump `account_endings` with `api_key_revocations`, with the container stopped, and put both back once
this release has migrated the returned copy, by the same three steps as card 2995's (the first start
with no network, the dump put back with the server stopped, the usual start):

```bash
# Before returning the copy, with the container stopped: the dump.
docker run --rm --network none --user root -v dumpfire-data:/app/data -v "$HOME/dumpfire-cold:/cold" \
  dumpfire:2995 node -e "const D=require('better-sqlite3');const d=new D('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true});require('fs').writeFileSync('/cold/account-endings.json',JSON.stringify(d.prepare('SELECT * FROM account_endings ORDER BY seq').all()))"
# 1. This release's first start on the returned copy, with no network, stopped once migrated (card 2995's step 1).
# 2. With the server stopped, the dump put back, in its order, after the rows the migration wrote:
docker run --rm --network none --user root -v dumpfire-data:/app/data -v "$HOME/dumpfire-cold:/cold" \
  dumpfire:2995 node -e "const D=require('better-sqlite3');const d=new D('/app/data/dumpfire.db');const rows=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/cold/account-endings.json','utf8'));const put=d.prepare('INSERT INTO account_endings (user_id, account_created, ending, role, credential, ended_at, stated_ended, origin) VALUES (@user_id, @account_created, @ending, @role, @credential, @ended_at, @stated_ended, @origin)');d.transaction(()=>{for(const r of rows)put.run(r)})()"
# 3. The usual start.
```

Put the dump back after `api_key_revocations`' in the same stopped window: the two are independent,
and the order between them does not matter. The re-migrated copy's own rows never outrank the dump's
(card 2996's code review, FP4): 0077 dates the role rows it writes at each account's creation and
the disables at their own moment, so a demotion, a disable or a delete made before the rollback, in
the dump with its own later moment, stands. The next start then ends again every account the dump
names that the copy brought back. The dump holds ids, creation times and fingerprints, never a
password hash.

**Passwords changed since the copy** (card 2997). The dump already carries the `password` rows:
every password change here (the holder's own, an administrator's reset, an invite used, Reset
Everything) records the fingerprint of the hash it replaced, and those rows go back with the rest.
After the put-back, every account but the superadmin whose password was changed since the copy holds,
in the copy, a password the record names as replaced: the next start gives it a password nothing
matches and signs it out (its sessions, pending sign-ins, unused invites and API keys ended), with
one `[WARN] [AUTH]` line of counts, and it needs its password set (🔑) or an invite (📧). The
superadmin is never changed or refused this way: it signs in with the password the copy holds, and
`[WARN] [AUTH] The superadmin holds a password the record of account endings says was replaced on
this server: …` repeats at every start and every five minutes until that password is changed on the
Account page; change it at once.

**A `deleted` row cannot be lifted** (FP17). Once the record names an account as deleted (a delete
here, or a backup's row brought by an import), no enable, no import and no start brings it back into
use: it stays disabled with no password that works, and an administrator who needs the person back
deletes the inert account and makes a new one. The record is append-only, and nothing in the
application deletes a row of it.

**Going back to an older image.** That image never writes the record, and its import clears and
refills it from the backup: never import under an older image. Its Reset Everything clears the record
too (card 2996's code review, FP13), since that image's reset keeps only the tables it knows: never
reset under an older image either, or dump the record first and put it back once forward. Coming
forward, the start ends again any account the record ends; a delete, disable or demotion made on the
older image is not recorded.

**Nothing to set.** No environment variable, no OpenAPI change.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Export a backup | A `.db` file | |
| H2 | Make Ann a user; disable and delete Bob | Done | |
| H3 | Import the file as it is | "1 account(s) in the backup are named as deleted by the record of account endings: …" and "1 account(s) in the backup were given back the lower role …"; the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line "…keeping 2 account(s) ended or lowered as the record of account endings says…", no name, no id | Bob enabled, Ann an admin, or a name in either |
| H4 | Sign in as Bob with his old password and authenticator | Refused | Signed in |
| H5 | Users panel: Enable on Bob | "The record of account endings names this account as deleted, and a restore brought it back: it cannot be enabled. …" | Enabled |
| H6 | Delete Bob again | Deleted | Refused |
| H7 | Import the same file as a working copy | The same two lines | Bob can sign in on the copy |
| H8 | Restart | No new AUTH line about accounts | A WARN: the restore left something the start ended |

### The Release That Takes Nothing That Signs In From an Unsealed Backup (Card 3009)

**Ships in the release since `332634f`** (production), which holds cards 2943, 2947, 2994 to 2997,
3006 and 3009, together. No migration, no environment variable, no OpenAPI change:
`POST /api/admin/import` is internal, and its answer only gains fields.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Imp["Import of a backup\nwhose seal does not verify"] --> Same{"The same account here?\nnumber, creation time, and\nthis installation's id\n(no id: the same username)"}
    Same -->|"Yes"| Here["This server's password,\nfactors and keys;\nkeys end at the earlier date"]
    Same -->|"No"| None["No password, factor or key\nfrom the file; schedules paused;\n🔑 or 📧"]
    Imp --> Sup["The importer not in the file:\nthe backup's superadmin given\nthe importer's password and authenticators"]
    Imp --> Hold["Mail, App URL and new destinations\nheld for review"]
```

**What changes.** An import of a backup whose seal does not verify here (another server's, an edited
file, one made before seals, or one made before card 2943's first start, when the seal key was made
anew; and, since card 3013 names them, this server's own backup made before Reset Everything, or one
restored onto a database rebuilt after a loss, as the seal key went with it), as it is or as a working copy, takes no password, second factor, API key or invite from the
file for any account that is not the same account here, and no invite at all (its code review, FP1).
Each such account is given a password nothing matches, keeps no leave to set up two-step sign-in, has
its report schedules paused whatever the file holds for it, stays enabled, and needs 🔑 or 📧. A key is kept only where this server held that very key (the same id, fingerprint
and owner) for the same account, and then ends at the earlier of this server's and the file's expiry
and deadline. A superadmin of this server restored as the same account is an enabled superadmin
after the import, whatever the file says. Where the account importing is not in the file as the same
account and could not sign in as itself afterwards, the file's lowest-numbered enabled superadmin
that is not the same here is given the importer's password, its authenticators sealed again (not its
recovery codes), its leave to set up on its password alone, and its email address, which any other
account of the file holding it gives up for one that receives no mail; its schedules are paused.
Every other such superadmin gets a password nothing matches, as each does where any superadmin of
this server restored as the same account can sign in, or none is enabled (FP2, FP5, FP6). Restored as
it is, the file's mail settings, App URL and destinations at places this server did not hold are held
for the superadmin's review (card 2922's hold), each told as from a backup whose seal did not verify,
never as a setter's; a working copy removes them, the App URL included (FP3, FP4). The answer and the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line count
all of it and name nobody; the line's details say only `installation`: `this`, `other` or `none`. A
backup this server sealed restores as before.

**The installation id.** Every server now has `settings.installation_id`, 32 hex characters, made
once at the start in the signing keys' transaction, and every backup made from now on carries it
under its seal. One a host edit left not of that form is made anew at the next start, with one
`[CRITICAL] [STARTUP]` line naming neither id (FP13). It is not secret, is never written to a log or an answer, and is never brought in
by a restore: the restore puts back this server's own. An account in an unsealed backup carrying
this id is the same account here by its number and creation time; one carrying another id has none;
one carrying none (made before this release) is matched by number, creation time and username.

**Moving to a new host**: move the volume and the MFA key file, or import onto a fresh installation
in the order [Moving to a New Host](#moving-to-a-new-host) gives. **On any clone of the volume**,
change the backup seal key and the installation id as that section says.

**Nothing to set.** No migration, no environment variable, no OpenAPI change.

**What stays possible (residual).** The username fallback for a backup made before this release
cannot tell apart servers built by one script with the same usernames made in the same seconds. A
superadmin renamed since such a backup is not the same account in an unsealed restore of it, and
needs the host's `scripts/mfa-reset.mjs`. A same-account password that differs is counted under card
2997's `here` and `reset`, and an account not the same here under `unsealed`, apart. A backup of a
host-file or volume clone of this server not changed as above verifies as this server's own.

**This release's image.** The commands below name it `dumpfire:3009`: tag it so as soon as it
is built (`docker tag dumpfire:latest dumpfire:3009`), so that a command meant for this release never
runs an image that `latest` has since moved to, or back from. Never use `dumpfire:latest` in its
rollback path: after a rollback it may name either image (card 3020's code review, FP7).

**Rolling back** goes to `332634f`, production before this release, and to nothing between: card
2997's image was never released on its own. [Card 2943's rollback constraints](#the-release-that-makes-the-signing-keys-anew-card-2943)
bind first, for the whole release. On `332634f` the `installation_id` row stays in `settings`, and
that image ignores it; its imports take the file's passwords, keys and invites for accounts not here,
as before cards 2995 to 3009, and copy the file's `installation_id` over this server's. It reads no
`setting_holds`, so a mail host, App URL or destination an unsealed import held is in force there:
remove each such setting under Settings held for review before rolling back. **Coming forward
again**, if any import was made on the older image, delete the row on the host, with the server
stopped, so that the next start makes a fresh one:

```bash
docker stop dumpfire
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data dumpfire:3009 node -e "
const db = require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db', { fileMustExist: true });
console.log('rows removed:', db.prepare(\"DELETE FROM settings WHERE key = 'installation_id'\").run().changes);
db.close();
"
docker start dumpfire
```

This server's backups made before then carry the old id, so one of them whose seal does not verify
reads as another installation's, which only fails safe: none of its accounts is the same here, and
none takes a password, factor or key from it. **If this step is skipped**,
this server carries the id of the installation whose backup was imported, so that installation's
backups read here as `this` in an unsealed restore, and an account in them with the same number and
creation time is taken for the same account: skipping it weakens the rule for backups of the server
whose id was copied.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | ▶ Run Now, then import that backup as it is | Restored as before; no new sentence | A new sentence, or a password changed |
| H2 | Copy that backup, add an admin account with a known password and an API key, then import it | "1 account(s) in the backup are not on this server as the same account …" and "1 API key(s) in the backup were left out …"; no name | The added account signs in, or its key answers `/api/v1` |
| H3 | Set up a second, empty instance with its own superadmin and authenticator; import the first server's backup there with that superadmin's password | "The backup's superadmin is not the account you imported with …"; the backup's superadmin signs in there with the new superadmin's password and a code from its authenticator, and not with its own | Locked out, or the import refused |
| H4 | On the second instance, sign in as an ordinary account with its first-server password | Refused | Signed in |
| H5 | On the second instance, call `/api/v1/me` with that account's first-server key | `401` | Answered |
| H6 | On the second instance, open Settings held for review | The mail settings and the App URL held | Neither held |

### The Release That Keeps an Unsealed Backup From Reaching Outside (Card 3012)

**Ships in the release since `332634f`** (production), with cards 2943, 2947, 2994 to 2997, 3006 and
3009, together, and with card 3020 ([below](#the-release-that-holds-an-unsealed-backups-requester-and-people-mail-card-3020)),
which closes the requester, participant and people addresses this card left open. No migration and no environment variable. The OpenAPI document stays `1.15.0`
(unreleased) with point (10) added to its note: the hold, its `pausedBecause` sentence, and a new
secret on switch-on.

**What changes.** An import of a backup whose seal does not verify sends nothing outside as the file
has it:

- every webhook with an address is switched off for good, its secret discarded; switching it on gives
  it a new secret;
- every enabled report schedule is paused;
- each person who is the same account here keeps the email address and notification choices they have
  here;
- every other account has notification mail switched off, its other choices kept;
- the backup failure mail keeps this server's address;
- the restore's notice of webhooks it switched off is written to the log and mailed to nobody.

Counts only, in the answer and the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line. The invite confirm names the address.

**The cost.** Production at `332634f` predates card 2928, so every backup it has made carries plain
webhook addresses, and after this release's first start every one of them restores as unsealed. **The
first restore of such a backup holds every webhook that has an address.** Each needs:

1. switching on by its board's owner or an administrator (`PUT /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` with
   `{"active": true}` alone);
2. the new secret it is given put in at its receiver.

Every schedule is paused too, for its owner to turn back on on the Reports page.

**Nothing to set.** No migration, no environment variable.

**This release's image.** The commands below name it `dumpfire:3012`: tag it so as soon as it
is built (`docker tag dumpfire:latest dumpfire:3012`), so that a command meant for this release never
runs an image that `latest` has since moved to, or back from. Never use `dumpfire:latest` in its
rollback path: after a rollback it may name either image (card 3020's code review, FP7).

**Rolling back** goes to `332634f` only, after [card 2943's constraints](#the-release-that-makes-the-signing-keys-anew-card-2943).
That image has no `held_because` and would let a held webhook be switched on with no new secret, to
the file's address. **Before rolling back,** with the server stopped:

```bash
docker stop dumpfire
# Preview, read-only: the webhooks held for this card's reason.
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data dumpfire:3012 node -e "
const db = require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db', { fileMustExist: true, readonly: true });
console.log(db.prepare(\"SELECT id, board_id, receiver, held_at FROM webhooks WHERE held_because = 'restored from a backup whose seal did not verify' ORDER BY id\").all());
db.close();
"
# Delete them, with their reveal rows.
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data dumpfire:3012 node -e "
const db = require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db', { fileMustExist: true });
const why = 'restored from a backup whose seal did not verify';
db.transaction(() => {
  db.prepare('DELETE FROM webhook_reveals WHERE webhook_id IN (SELECT id FROM webhooks WHERE held_because = ?)').run(why);
  console.log('webhooks removed:', db.prepare('DELETE FROM webhooks WHERE held_because = ?').run(why).changes);
})();
db.close();
"
```

Then follow card 2943's rollback. Paused schedules, emails and choices stay as written.

**What stays possible (residual).** Invites and notices to an account not the same here still go to
the file's address (card 3021). Webhooks and schedules switched off or deleted here
coming back from a sealed backup are card 3004's, and board or team access an unsealed file grants
is card 3002's.

### The Release That Holds an Unsealed Backup's Requester and People Mail (Card 3020)

**Ships in the release since `332634f`** (production), with cards 2943, 2947, 2994 to 2997, 3006, 3009
and 3012, together. It closes card 3012's open gap (its F1), which blocked the release. **Migration
0078** (`drizzle/0078_hold_request_mail.sql`) adds four nullable columns to `task_requests`
(`mail_held_because`, `mail_released_at`, `mail_released_by`, `mail_released_by_name`) and the index
`idx_task_requests_mail_released_by`, and is applied at start. Nothing to set. The OpenAPI document
stays `1.15.0` (unreleased), with point (11) added to its note and `Person.status` described anew.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Imp["Import of a backup<br/>whose seal does not verify"] --> Req{"Each request:<br/>held here as it is?"}
    Req -->|"yes"| Same["this server's hold, or none"]
    Req -->|"no, with an address"| Held["mail held:<br/>no mail, link or report"]
    Held --> Rel["Release: administrator,<br/>password and code, address as reviewed"]
    Imp --> Ppl{"Each person:<br/>same id, address and account here?"}
    Ppl -->|"yes, active"| Keep["untouched"]
    Ppl -->|"no, or left here,<br/>or a planted status"| Left["marked left,<br/>people_changes by DumpFire"]
    Left --> Act["Mark active:<br/>password and code"]
```

**What changes.**

- An unsealed import holds the mail of each request whose requester or card this server did not hold
  as it is. A held request gets no progress mail, report, accept or decline, reply or link. An
  administrator releases each under **Mail held** in the Requests inbox, with a password and a code,
  against the address they reviewed. Unconfirmed held requests cannot be released; they lapse in 7
  days.
- It marks left each person whose address and account this server did not hold, and any person with a
  planted status, each recorded by DumpFire in the people change record.
- Marking a person active now asks for a password and a code, everywhere.
- Progress mail now goes to every accepted request on a card that is not held.
- A reply to a held request says the requester was not mailed.
- Addresses taken from a file are shown with their code points.
- The answer and the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line give counts only.

**The cost.**

- A move between servers, or a forged file, holds every request with an address and marks every
  person left.
- The first restore of one of production's own older backups holds only what changed since it was
  made: a request accepted since, a card retitled or moved, a person whose address or account changed.
  It also holds the requests whose timestamps predate card 2095's normalisation (L9): the identity
  compares the stored text, so an old-form `created_at` never matches. That over-holding fails closed:
  review and release them.
- Until they are marked active, account holders among those people cannot answer their decisions.

**Rolling back** goes to `332634f` only, after [card 2943's constraints](#the-release-that-makes-the-signing-keys-anew-card-2943)
and card 3012's steps (above). That image ignores `mail_held_because` and would mail every held
requester. People marked left stay unmailed there, as that image honours `left`.

**Name the images exactly.** Tag this release's image as soon as it is built,
`docker tag dumpfire:latest dumpfire:3020`, and keep the old one as `dumpfire:rollback`
([Updating a Running Installation](#updating-a-running-installation), step 3). Never use
`dumpfire:latest` in these steps: after a rollback it may name either image (card 3020's code
review, FP7).

**Before rolling back,** with the server stopped:

```bash
NEW=dumpfire:3020   # the tag made as soon as the release was built
docker stop dumpfire
# Preview, read-only: how many requests are held, never their addresses.
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data "$NEW" node -e "
const db = require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db', { fileMustExist: true, readonly: true });
console.log(db.prepare('SELECT COUNT(*) AS held FROM task_requests WHERE mail_held_because IS NOT NULL').get());
db.close();
"
# Take the address off each held request, so that the older image mails none of them.
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data "$NEW" node -e "
const db = require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db', { fileMustExist: true });
console.log('requests whose address was taken off:',
  db.prepare('UPDATE task_requests SET requester_email = NULL, requester_user_id = NULL WHERE mail_held_because IS NOT NULL').run().changes);
db.close();
"
```

**After rolling back, before importing a backup made by the new release on `332634f`:**

On `332634f` a held request is an ordinary one, so from the import until step 4's UPDATE has run,
nothing may mail its requester. **Pause integrations and API-key automations** (anything that
calls `/api/v1`, and any script with a key) for that window: a comment or a move made through the
API on such a request's card mails its requester. And **run the import with no outbound mail**, by
one of:

- the `332634f` container on an internal Docker network, which has no route out
  (`docker network create --internal dumpfire-quiet`, then `--network dumpfire-quiet` in place of
  its usual network), until the UPDATE has run. A published port does not answer on such a network,
  so the import is then made from a browser or a container on that network; or
- the mail settings removed from a copy of the backup before it is imported, and entered again in
  Settings once the UPDATE has run:

  ```bash
  cp "<backup file>" quiet.db
  docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD:/b" dumpfire:rollback node -e "
  const db = require('better-sqlite3')('/b/quiet.db', { fileMustExist: true });
  console.log('mail settings removed:', db.prepare(\"DELETE FROM settings WHERE key LIKE 'smtp%'\").run().changes);
  db.close();
  "
  ```

  and import `quiet.db` in the steps below.

1. Preview its held count from the file, read-only:

   ```bash
   docker run --rm --network none -v "$PWD:/b:ro" dumpfire:rollback node -e "
   const db = require('better-sqlite3')('/b/<backup file>', { fileMustExist: true, readonly: true });
   const has = db.prepare(\"SELECT 1 FROM pragma_table_info('task_requests') WHERE name = 'mail_held_because'\").get();
   console.log(has ? db.prepare('SELECT COUNT(*) AS held FROM task_requests WHERE mail_held_because IS NOT NULL').get() : 'no column: nothing held');
   db.close();
   "
   ```

2. Pause integrations and API-key automations, and shut outbound mail off, as above.
3. Import it.
4. **Straight after the import, before anyone acts on the board**, stop the server and run the same
   UPDATE as above, with `dumpfire:rollback` in place of `"$NEW"`. Then start it on its usual
   network, enter the mail settings again if they were removed, and resume the integrations.

These steps lose who asked, for held requests only. The columns stay, since migrations are fixed
forward, and the older image starts with one model-check `ERROR` line.

**What stays possible (residual).** Invites and notices to an account not the same here still go to
the file's address (card 3021). The mail settings' From address and name are this server's since
card 3029, which ships in the same release. A participant the file plants on a person this server holds is mailed (N4, left), and a planted
`people.user_id` still gives decision access on the register's side (card 3002).

### The Release That Takes No Record From an Unsealed Backup (Card 3013)

**Ships in the release since `332634f`** (production), with cards 2995, 2996, 2997, 3009, 3012, 3020
and 3029, together, and never without card 3009. Card 3014 is folded in. **No migration**, nothing to
set, and no change to the v1 API or its OpenAPI document; the internal import answer gains two
additive fields, `recordsNotTaken` and `accountStateAsHere`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Imp["Import of a backup<br/>whose seal does not verify"] --> Rec["Both records:<br/>counted, none taken"]
    Imp --> Belt["No belt from the file;<br/>a key recorded only if this server held it"]
    Imp --> State{"An account of this server?"}
    State -->|"its id and creation time"| Role["this server's role"]
    State -->|"its id and creation time"| Dis["this server's enabled<br/>or disabled state"]
    Rec & Role & Dis --> Said["counted in the answer, the panel<br/>and the CRITICAL line, naming nobody"]
```

**What changes.** An import of a backup whose seal does not verify here, as it is or as a working
copy:

- adds nothing to the record of account endings or the record of ended API keys, and counts the rows
  it did not take;
- writes no safety entry ("belt") from the file's word;
- records an ended key only where this server held that key for the same account;
- gives every account of this server's number and creation time its role and enabled or disabled
  state exactly as here, a superadmin's included, counted, and refuses, changing nothing, where that
  leaves no enabled superadmin;
- says both counts in the answer, the panel and the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line, naming nobody, and
  writes no line of problems.

On an unchecked import a disable is carried only where this server's record attests it; a sealed
restore carries every disable, as before. On every restore an account counts as held here with a later
creation time only where the record holds a row for it.

**Security.** It closes an elevation of privilege on an unchecked import (Critical: a file could make an
ordinary account a superadmin, which then signed in with its own password) and four ways an unchecked
file could defeat a later restore of a genuine backup.

**The cost.** No record comes from an unchecked file. A move by import onto another server brings
neither record, and nor does disaster recovery from this server's own backup onto a new database: the
seal key went with the lost database, so the file no longer verifies. Both records then start empty,
and, by card 3009, no password, second factor or key that signs in comes back. The host-level move
([Moving to a New Host](#moving-to-a-new-host)) keeps both.

**Going back.** There is no migration and no new kind of row, so going back to the build before this
card (`7a8b773`) is code only. Going back to `332634f` follows the existing steps and adds none: the
"Going back to an older image" paragraphs of
[card 2995](#the-release-that-keeps-ended-api-keys-ended-across-a-restore-card-2995) and
[card 2996](#the-release-that-keeps-ended-accounts-ended-across-a-restore-card-2996), and
[card 2943's constraints](#the-release-that-makes-the-signing-keys-anew-card-2943). `332634f`'s import
clears both records and refills them from the file; coming forward again, the start passes enforce
any rows it planted.

**Servers that ran the unreleased batch.** Rows a build before this card carried from an unchecked
file stay in this server's records: nothing removes them and no start warns of them. Production never
ran that batch. On a staging or test server that did, count the account rows any import carried,
read-only, with the container stopped:

```bash
NEW=dumpfire:3013   # the tag made as soon as the release was built
docker stop dumpfire
# Read-only: the rows of the record of account endings that an import brought, and when they were ended.
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data "$NEW" node -e "
const db = require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db', { fileMustExist: true, readonly: true });
console.log(db.prepare(\"SELECT count(*) AS n, min(ended_at) AS first, max(ended_at) AS last FROM account_endings WHERE origin = 'backup'\").get());
db.close();
"
docker start dumpfire
```

A sealed backup's rows are `backup` too, so a count above 0 is not by itself a fault. Rebuild any such
server that imported an unchecked file under the unreleased batch: `api_key_revocations` has no
`origin`, so the key rows it carried cannot be told apart.

**Release note.** "Rows a build before card 3013 carried from a backup whose seal did not verify stay
in this server's records; rebuild any non-production server that imported one."

**What stays possible (residual).** An older backup of another server brings its ended accounts back
enabled but unable to sign in, with the file's role: check each before inviting it. An account an
unchecked restore made inert only because this server held its number with a later creation time
stays disabled with a password nothing matches, and nothing re-asserts it. And (open) an account
disabled here is disabled again even where a file not of this server restores it, under that number
and creation time, as a superadmin; where that is every superadmin of the file, the import is left
with none enabled.

### The Release That Keeps Board, Team and Person Access Removals Across a Restore (Card 3002)

**Ships in the release since `332634f`** (production), with cards 2995, 2996, 2997, 3009, 3012, 3013,
3020 and 3029, and with card 3033 (decision roles an unchecked backup can give), together.
**Migration 0079** adds `access_changes`, its three indexes and a once-only seed; it changes no existing
row. Migrations 0074 to 0079 apply in one start. No change to the v1 API or its OpenAPI document
(it stays `1.15.0`); the internal import answer gains three additive fields, `accessKept`,
`accessAsHere` and `recordsNotTaken.accessChanges`. Nothing to set.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Start["first start of this release"] --> M79["0079: table, indexes,<br/>seed of today's access"]
    M79 --> Live["every share, team, visibility,<br/>Product Owner and person link change recorded"]
    Live --> Imp{"An import"}
    Imp -->|"seal verified"| Cap["access capped at the record;<br/>none guessed away that is held here"]
    Imp -->|"seal not verified"| Here["same-here accounts get exactly<br/>this server's access; none on boards<br/>and teams not here; record untouched"]
    Cap & Here --> Sweep["start and five-minute pass:<br/>recorded items above their row lowered"]
```

**What changes.** Every change of who may open a board (its members, its shares with teams, whether it
is public, its creator), who is in a team, a board's Product Owner and which account a person in the
People directory is linked to is recorded by identity (id and creation time), never by name, in the
transaction that makes it. A restore of this server's own backup brings that access back no higher
than recorded, and never takes away on a guess access the server holds when the restore runs: a
removed member or share stays removed, a role lowered stays lower, a private board stays private, a
Product Owner or creator replaced here is cleared (never replaced), a person unlinked here stays
unlinked, and a team deleted here comes back without the members and boards it had then. A backup
whose seal does not verify adds nothing to the record and gives every account that is the same here
exactly its access here, and none on the boards and teams this server does not hold, which come back
private. The answer, the panel and the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line count what was kept and name nobody.
The next start, and every five minutes, lowers again anything above its recorded row, with one
`[WARN] [AUTH]` line of counts, mailing the owners of held webhooks only where the schedulers run.

**The first start.** 0079 records today's access: each board's creator and visibility, its Product
Owner, its members and shares, each team and its members, and each person's link, every row dated at
the earliest stamp so that any later change outranks it. Preview, read-only, from a container of this
release's image on the same volume (an upper bound: values whose creation time does not read as a
moment are skipped):

```bash
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data dumpfire:3002 node -e "const d=require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true,fileMustExist:true});console.log(d.prepare('SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM boards) * 2 + (SELECT count(*) FROM boards WHERE product_owner_user_id IS NOT NULL) + (SELECT count(*) FROM board_members) + (SELECT count(*) FROM board_teams) + (SELECT count(*) FROM teams) + (SELECT count(*) FROM team_members) + (SELECT count(*) FROM people) AS seed_rows').get())"
```

**Untracked boards, teams and people.** A board, team or person deleted before 0079 is not in the
record: a backup that holds it brings it back whole, with the access it had (R16). So does one whose
creation time does not read as a moment, until a restore brings it: every restore gives each restored
board, team and person whose creation time does not read (and, from a file whose seal does not verify,
each account not the same here that the record of account endings did not rule) the restore's moment,
with one line counting them and naming none, so that every change of its access is recorded from then
on (code review, FP2). And where a board's creator, or a person's linked account,
has a creation time that does not read as a moment, 0079 writes no row for it (R21): that board or
person is untracked, so neither a start nor a restore clears the creator or the link on a guess. A
member, share or Product Owner whose account's or team's creation time does not read is not written.

**Access granted on an older image.** A member row or share made while an image older than this
release ran (or by a host edit) has no row of its own. The start pass leaves it; a restore caps it at
the access the server holds when the restore runs, never higher, on any board or team, recorded or not
(R20; code review, FP3), and guesses it away only where the backup holds it and this server did not.
Sending such a grant again from the Share window, or the team's page, records it (code review, FP1). A
row of this server's dated after the moment a restore or a start runs is not read by either (R1, FP12).

**The cost.** After an unchecked import of an older backup of this server (one made before card 2943,
or after Reset Everything), boards this server no longer holds come back private and open to
administrators only, until they are shared again. A person whose account link such a backup changed
stays marked left until an administrator marks them active, with a password and a code.

**Reset Everything** keeps the record and records nothing: an import after a reset is capped by it as
any other.

**Before going back to an older image.** No image older than this release knows `access_changes`.
`332634f` writes nothing to it and its Reset empties it; worse, **its import clears the record and
copies the backup's rows in, each with the `origin` the backup gives it, so the backup's own rows
arrive as `here` rows** and would rank as this server's (R1). So, as card 2995's dump and put-back
([above](#the-release-that-keeps-ended-api-keys-ended-across-a-restore-card-2995)) and card 2996's
([above](#the-release-that-keeps-ended-accounts-ended-across-a-restore-card-2996)):

```bash
NEW=dumpfire:3002   # the tag made as soon as the release was built
# Before going back, with the container stopped: the record dumped beside the other two, in seq order.
docker run --rm --network none --user root -v dumpfire-data:/app/data -v "$HOME/dumpfire-cold:/cold" \
  "$NEW" node -e "const D=require('better-sqlite3');const d=new D('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true});require('fs').writeFileSync('/cold/access-changes.json',JSON.stringify(d.prepare('SELECT * FROM access_changes ORDER BY seq').all()))"
```

On return, with the server stopped:

1. **Compare, read-only.** The rows in the table and not in the dump, and in the dump and not in the
   table, by kind, subject, holder, `access` and `stated_changed`:

   ```bash
   docker run --rm --network none --user root -v dumpfire-data:/app/data -v "$HOME/dumpfire-cold:/cold" \
     "$NEW" node -e "const D=require('better-sqlite3');const d=new D('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true,fileMustExist:true});const key=(r)=>[r.kind,r.subject_id,r.subject_created,r.holder_id,r.holder_created,r.access,r.stated_changed].join('|');const dump=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/cold/access-changes.json','utf8')).map(key);const live=d.prepare('SELECT * FROM access_changes').all().map(key);const a=new Set(dump),b=new Set(live);console.log({onlyInTable:live.filter((k)=>!a.has(k)).length,onlyInDump:dump.filter((k)=>!b.has(k)).length})"
   ```

   Rows only in the table are what the older image's import copied in; rows only in the dump are what
   it cleared. Both are expected after an import there; neither is expected where none was made.
2. **Put the dump back whole**, a host step outside the application (the application never deletes
   from the record): the table emptied and the dump inserted with its own `seq`, in one transaction.
   Where the returned copy predates 0079 (it has no table), first start this release on it with no
   network and stop it once migrated, as card 2995's step 1.

   ```bash
   docker run --rm --network none --user root -v dumpfire-data:/app/data -v "$HOME/dumpfire-cold:/cold" \
     "$NEW" node -e "const D=require('better-sqlite3');const d=new D('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{fileMustExist:true});const rows=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync('/cold/access-changes.json','utf8'));const put=d.prepare('INSERT INTO access_changes (seq, kind, subject_id, subject_created, holder_id, holder_created, access, changed_at, stated_changed, origin) VALUES (@seq, @kind, @subject_id, @subject_created, @holder_id, @holder_created, @access, @changed_at, @stated_changed, @origin)');d.transaction(()=>{d.prepare('DELETE FROM access_changes').run();for(const r of rows)put.run(r)})()"
   ```

3. **Start as usual.** The start pass lowers what an import on the older image raised above a recorded
   row. Access granted on the older image to a tracked board has no row: the start pass keeps it, and
   only a later restore of a backup that holds it where this server does not guesses it away. A removal
   made while the older image ran (a member, share or team member taken off, a role lowered, a board
   made private, a Product Owner or a person's link cleared) was not recorded either: a later restore of
   a backup made before it brings that access back. Make each such removal again on this release once
   returned, so that it is recorded.

The dump holds ids, creation times and access words, never a name, and is safe to keep beside the cold
copy. Put it back in the same stopped window as `api_key_revocations`' and `account_endings`'; the
order among the three does not matter.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | Export a backup; take Bob off board B on its Share window | Bob gone | |
| H2 | Import the file as it is | "1 board or team membership(s) and share(s) in the backup were removed on this server after it was made, and are left out."; the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line "…keeping 1 access change(s) made on this server…", its details counting, naming nobody | Bob a member again, or a name in the line |
| H3 | Make B public, export, make it private; import the file | B private; "1 board(s) made private on this server after the backup stay private." | B public |
| H4 | Edit a copy of an export (its seal then fails) to make an account owner of B; import it | B's members exactly as here; "The backup's seal did not verify, so who may open what is not taken from it: 1 board(s) …" | The account an owner |
| H5 | Restart | No `[WARN] [AUTH]` line of lowered access | A line, with no host edit made |

**Release note.** "A restore never brings back board, team or person access removed, lowered or made
private on this server since the backup was made, and a backup whose seal does not verify gives no
account access this server did not give it. Boards and teams deleted before this release are not
recorded and come back whole from an older backup."

### The Release That Keeps Decision Role Removals Across a Restore (Card 3033)

**Ships in the same release as card 3002**, since `332634f` (production). **Migration 0080** seeds four
decision kinds into card 3002's `access_changes` and adds one index, `access_changes_changed
(changed_at)`, for the start pass's one read of a row dated after now; no new table or column, and it
changes no existing row. Migrations 0074 to 0080 apply in one start. The v1 OpenAPI document stays
`1.15.0` (unreleased), its note gaining point (12), R14's 409; the internal import answer's
`accessKept` and `accessAsHere` gain fields. Nothing to set.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Start["first start"] --> M80["0080: seed of every decision,<br/>its decider, places and their accounts;<br/>index on changed_at"]
    M80 --> Live["every participant, place account<br/>and decider change recorded"]
    Live --> Imp{"An import"}
    Imp -->|"seal verified"| Cap["roles capped at the record"]
    Imp -->|"seal not verified"| Here["held decisions as here;<br/>the rest inert; no ruling's<br/>Product Owner from the file"]
    Cap & Here --> Sweep["start and five-minute pass:<br/>recorded roles above their row lowered"]
```

**What changes.** Every change of a decision's participants (removal, informed or consulted, which
account each place holds) and of its decider is recorded by identity. A restore of this server's own
backup brings them back no higher than recorded, and never takes away on a guess a role held when it
runs. A backup whose seal does not verify adds nothing to the record, leaves every decision this
server holds with its board, stage and roles here, brings the others in with no board, no account and
nobody on them, takes no ruling's Product Owner from the file, and leaves no account id a later
account could inherit. Naming a Product Owner or decider whose account's creation time does not read
is refused (409). The next start, and every five minutes, lowers again anything above its recorded row.

**The first start.** 0080 seeds every decision present, dated at the earliest stamp. Preview,
read-only, from a container of this release's image on the same volume (an upper bound):

```bash
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data dumpfire:3033 node -e "const d=require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true,fileMustExist:true});console.log(d.prepare('SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM decisions) * 2 + (SELECT count(*) FROM decision_participants) + (SELECT count(*) FROM decision_participants WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL) AS seed_rows').get())"
```

**Untracked decisions.** A decision whose creation time does not read as a moment is not seeded, and
nothing records its roles. Such a decision is **matched by id alone while any row of the record has
that id**, and is untracked otherwise, its removals then not recorded (N4). Decisions made, and roles
changed, while an older image ran are not recorded either (N6): make each removal again on this
release.

**The cost.** After an unchecked import of an older backup of this server (one made before card 2943,
or after Reset Everything), past decisions come back with no board and nobody on them, open to
administrators only; a decision is carried on by making a new one.

The start and five-minute pass (`capAccessAtStart`) adds, per run, one read on `access_changes_changed`
of whether any row of this server's is dated after now, and then one ceiling for each live place, place's
account and decider that has a recorded row (two where such a dated row exists), the candidates
pre-filtered in SQL (`START_DECISION_CANDIDATES`), each ceiling a few reads of its own item's rows on
its index. Its cost grows with the number of tracked decision roles, not with the size of the record,
and it writes nothing where none is above its row. A restore adds, per restored decision, the two reads
of `decisionDeletedHere` on their indexes and one ceiling per place, place's account and decider.

**Before going back to an older image.** `access_changes` now holds the decision kinds too, so card
3002's dump, compare and put-back ([above](#the-release-that-keeps-board-team-and-person-access-removals-across-a-restore-card-3002))
carry them unchanged: the same commands, the same file, the same stopped window. An older image's
import brings removed participants back and its own changes are not recorded; coming forward, the
start pass lowers what is above a recorded row, and removals made while it ran must be made again.
Decisions made on it are untracked and come back whole.

| # | Do | Expect | Fault if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H6 | Export a backup; take Bob off an open decision on its page | Bob off | |
| H7 | Import the file as it is | Bob still off; "1 place(s) on decisions removed on this server after the backup was made stay removed."; the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]` line counting it, naming nobody | Bob back on, or a name in the line |
| H8 | Edit a copy of an export (its seal then fails) to make an account the decision's decider; import it | The decider as here; "… of the decisions in it, 1 this server holds kept their board, stage, author, decider and participants as here …" | The account the decider |
| H9 | Restart | No `[WARN] [AUTH]` line of lowered access | A line, with no host edit made |

**Release note.** "A restore never brings back a decision's participant, a place's account or a
decider removed or replaced on this server since the backup was made, and a backup whose seal does not
verify gives no account a role on a decision this server did not give it. Decisions made before this
release whose creation time cannot be read, and roles changed on an older version, are not recorded."

### The Release That Keeps Where the Server Sends Across a Restore (Card 3004)

**Ships in the same release as cards 3002 and 3033**, since `332634f` (production), and closes card 3031
(outbound settings that are not text). **Migration 0081** adds `outbound_changes` and its three indexes,
DDL only: no seed in SQL, and it changes no existing row. Migrations 0074 to 0081 apply in one start.
The v1 OpenAPI document stays `1.15.0` (unreleased), its note gaining point (13), the webhooks a
restore brings back switched off, and "nothing else changed" becoming (14); the internal import answer
gains `outboundKept` and `recordsNotTaken.outboundChanges`, additive. Nothing to set, but the MFA key
must be loaded (below).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Start["first start"] --> M81["0081: empty table, three indexes"]
    M81 --> Seed["the sweep seeds today's state once<br/>(MFA key loaded; one INFO line)"]
    Seed --> Live["every webhook, schedule, address,<br/>destination, mail and App URL change recorded"]
    Live --> Imp{"An import"}
    Imp -->|"seal verified"| Cap["nothing more open than here or recorded;<br/>unrecorded items held as not in the record"]
    Imp -->|"seal not verified"| Here["rules 1 and 2 only; record untouched;<br/>cards 3009 and 3012 hold the rest"]
    Cap & Here --> Sweep["start and five-minute pass:<br/>recorded items above their row held again"]
```

**What changes.** Every change of where the server sends is recorded by identity, never a name or an
address in plain: webhooks and report schedules by id and creation time, a webhook's address and each
address on a schedule as keyed digests, backup destinations, the mail server and the App URL by place.
A restore never switches on what is off here, never puts an address back on a schedule, and holds what
was removed, moved or (on this server's own backup) is not in the record: a webhook switched off for
good with its secret discarded, a schedule paused, a destination, mail server or App URL held for the
superadmin's review. An account a restore signs out because its password was replaced here has its
webhooks and settings held as a real reset holds them. Outbound settings that are not text are converted
or left out at the copy, and no sender uses one. The answer, the panel and the `[CRITICAL] [IMPORT]`
line count what was kept and name nothing.

**The first start.** 0081 makes an empty table; the first sweep seeds today's state once (`[INFO]` "The
record of where this server sends was started (once, card 3004): N webhook(s), report schedule(s),
schedule address(es), backup destination(s), mail setting(s) and App URL(s) recorded as they are now.").
Preview, read-only, from a container of this release's image on the same volume (the item rows, before
the addresses on schedules and the places):

```bash
docker run --rm --network none -v dumpfire-data:/app/data dumpfire:3004 node -e "const d=require('better-sqlite3')('/app/data/dumpfire.db',{readonly:true,fileMustExist:true});console.log(d.prepare('SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM webhooks) + (SELECT count(*) FROM report_schedules) AS item_rows').get())"
```

**The MFA key.** The record's digests use a subkey of it (`outboundKey`, HKDF of the key file). Without an
MFA key loaded, the seed is written only where no webhook and no report schedule has an address (else one
`[WARN]` per sweep, "The record of where this server sends could not be started: …", and the next sweep
tries again), and every write that must name an address is refused `503` with nothing written and none of
the day's report mail taken: "No MFA key is loaded, so this server cannot record report addresses or
webhook addresses right now. Nothing was saved. Ask an administrator to load the MFA key (MFA_KEY_FILE)."
That is a webhook made or given another url, and a report schedule saved with an address added or taken
off (a schedule made with addresses included), asked before the password. A change of a webhook that
leaves its address as it is (its events, or a switch-off) needs no key. Load the key before this release
(`MFA_KEY_FILE`, see [the key that protects authenticator
secrets](#the-key-that-protects-authenticator-secrets)).

**After replacing the key**, the digests recorded under the old key cannot be compared with anything, and
both halves fail closed:

- **Webhooks.** A restore compares a restored webhook's address with the record only under the current
  key. Where the record names it under the old key, it is left as restored only where this server holds
  the same webhook, by id and creation time, at the very address restored; every other such webhook with
  an address is held `re-pointed here`, its secret discarded, and counted apart in the answer ("… whose
  address could not be compared with this server's record …"). One pointed elsewhere here is still held as
